Math. 22 (1975), 266–272, DOI 10.1007/BF02761594, Josefson-Nissenzweig theorem; Diestel, Sequences and Series; Lean states `RCLike` infinite-dimensional Banach case with `‖φ n‖=1` and pointwise weak-star nullness.

articles.title: Krein–Smulian theorem
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be a subset of its dual $E^*$ that is convex over $\mathbb{R}$. Then $C$
is weak-star closed if and only if, for every $r > 0$, the set
$\{\varphi \in C : \|\varphi\| \le r\}$ is weak-star closed.

## Sources

- M. Krein and V. Smulian, Ann. of Math. 41 (1940) 556-583; Dunford-Schwartz I; Lean states `RCLike` Banach case with `Convex ℝ s` and closedBall intersections.

articles.title: Mazur's lemma in the textbook phrasing
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$,
where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, regarded also as a real vector space by
restricting scalars. Let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and $x \in E$ such that
$f(u_n) \to f(x)$ for every continuous $\mathbb{K}$-linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$.
Then for every $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a finite index set
$I$, real weights $w_i \ge 0$ with $\sum_{i \in I} w_i = 1$ and natural numbers $n_i \ge N$ for
$i \in I$ such that $\left\| \sum_{i \in I} w_i u_{n_i} - x \right\| < \varepsilon$.

articles.title: Mazur's lemma, explicit finite convex combinations
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed space over
$\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, regarded also as a real vector
space by restricting scalars. If a sequence $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ converges to
$x \in E$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by the continuous $\mathbb{K}$-linear
functionals on $E$), then for every $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there are
a finite index set $I$, real weights $w_i \ge 0$ with $\sum_{i \in I} w_i = 1$ and natural
numbers $n_i \ge N$ for $i \in I$ such that
$\left\| \sum_{i \in I} w_i u_{n_i} - x \right\| < \varepsilon$.

articles.title: Mazur's lemma, hull form
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$
is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, regarded also as a real vector space by restricting scalars. If
a sequence $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ converges to $x \in E$ in the weak topology of $E$
(the topology induced by the continuous $\mathbb{K}$-linear functionals on $E$), then for every
$N \in \mathbb{N}$ the point $x$ lies in the norm closure of the real convex hull of the tail
$\{u_n : n \ge N\}$.

articles.title: Mazur's lemma, hull form for the whole sequence
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed space over
$\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, regarded also as a real vector
space by restricting scalars. If a sequence $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ converges to
$x \in E$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by the continuous $\mathbb{K}$-linear
functionals on $E$), then $x$ lies in the norm closure of the real convex hull of the set
$\{u_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$.

articles.title: Principle of local reflexivity
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, with dual $E^*$, bidual $E^{**}$ and canonical embedding $J \colon E \to E^{**}$.
Let $M$ and $N$ be finite-dimensional normed spaces over $\mathbb{K}$ with injective bounded
linear maps $i_M \colon M \to E^{**}$ and $i_N \colon N \to E^*$, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Then
there is a bounded linear map $T \colon M \to E$ such that for all $m \in M$, $n \in N$ and
$x \in E$ we have
$(1 + \varepsilon)^{-1} \|i_M(m)\| \le \|T m\| \le (1 + \varepsilon) \|i_M(m)\|$,
$i_N(n)(T m) = i_M(m)(i_N(n))$, and $T m = x$ whenever $i_M(m) = J x$.

Proof: Helly's lemma applied to finitely many linear conditions plus one norm bound, then a finite
$\delta$-net of the unit sphere of $i_M(M)$ turns net-point bounds into the $(1+\varepsilon)$
bounds (the elementary proof in Albiac–Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*).

## Sources

- J. Lindenstrauss and H. Rosenthal, Israel J. Math. 7 (1969) 325-349, principle of local reflexivity; Johnson-Rosenthal-Zippin 1971 refinements; Albiac and Kalton, Topics in Banach Space Theory; Lean states `RCLike` Banach finite- dimensional `M, N` version with `(1+ε)`-isometry and pairing preservation.

articles.title: Weakly convergent sequences are norm-bounded
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed space over
$\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$
and let $x \in E$. If $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for every continuous linear
functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$, then the norms are bounded above: there is a real
number $C$ with $\|u_n\| \le C$ for all $n$.

articles.title: Weakly convergent sequences are norm-bounded (weak topology form)
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a
normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be
a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology
induced by all continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{K}$), then there is a real number
$C$ with $\|u_n\| \le C$ for all $n$.

articles.title: Weak closure of the unit sphere is the closed unit ball
articles.statement:
In an infinite-dimensional normed space, the weak closure of the unit
sphere is the closed unit ball.

articles.title: Weakly open sets contain lines through each point
articles.statement:
Every nonempty weakly open set contains a whole line through each of its
points: if `U` is weakly open and `x ∈ U`, then `x + t • v ∈ U` for all scalars
`t` and some nonzero `v` (a common kernel vector of the finitely many
functionals constraining a basic weak neighbourhood of `x`).

articles.title: Finitely many functionals have a common nonzero kernel vector
articles.statement:
Finitely many continuous linear functionals on an infinite-dimensional
normed space have a common nonzero kernel vector.

articles.title: Weakly open sets are unbounded in infinite dimensions
articles.statement:
Every nonempty weakly open set in an infinite-dimensional normed space is
unbounded in norm.

articles.title: Weak convergence gives convergence under every functional
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed space
over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in
$E$ and let $x \in E$. If $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by all
continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{K}$), then $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for
every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$.

articles.title: Weak topology equals norm topology in finite dimensions
articles.statement:
In finite dimensions the identity map from the norm topology to the weak
topology is an open map: the weak topology agrees with the norm topology.

articles.title: Weak lower semicontinuity of the norm
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed space over
$\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$
and let $x \in E$. If $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for every continuous linear
functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$, that is, $u_n$ converges weakly to $x$, then
$\|x\| \le \liminf_{n \to \infty} \|u_n\|$.

articles.title: Weak lower semicontinuity of the norm (weak topology form)
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed space
over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in
$E$ and let $x \in E$. If $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by all
continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{K}$), then
$\|x\| \le \liminf_{n \to \infty} \|u_n\|$.

articles.title: Unit sphere is not weakly closed in infinite dimensions
articles.statement:
The unit sphere is not weakly closed in infinite dimensions: its weak
closure is the whole closed unit ball.

articles.title: Unit sphere is not weakly compact in infinite dimensions
articles.statement: The unit sphere is not weakly compact in infinite dimensions.

articles.title: Open unit ball is not weakly open in infinite dimensions
articles.statement: The open unit ball is not weakly open in infinite dimensions.

articles.title: Unit sphere is not weakly open in infinite dimensions
articles.statement: The unit sphere is not weakly open in infinite dimensions.

articles.title: Weak topology is strictly coarser in infinite dimensions
articles.statement:
In infinite dimensions the identity map from the norm topology to the weak
topology is not an open map: the open unit ball is norm-open but not
weakly open.

articles.title: Bounded operators preserve weak convergence
articles.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be normed spaces over
$\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T \colon E \to F$ be a continuous linear map,
let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ for
every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$, then $g(T u_n) \to g(T x)$ for
every continuous linear functional $g \colon F \to \mathbb{K}$.

articles.title: Bounded operators preserve weak convergence (weak topology form)
articles.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be
normed spaces over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T \colon E \to F$ be a
continuous linear map, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$.
If $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$, then $T u_n \to T x$ in the weak topology of $F$;
here the weak topology of a space is the one induced by its continuous linear functionals.

articles.title: Convergence under every functional gives weak convergence
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed space
over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in
$E$ and let $x \in E$. If $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for every continuous linear
functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$, then $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the
topology induced by all continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{K}$).

articles.title: Finite-dimensional spaces have the approximation property
articles.statement:
Finite-dimensional spaces have the approximation property: the identity
operator is itself finite-rank.

articles.title: Separable Hilbert spaces have the approximation property
articles.statement:
A Hilbert space with a Hilbert basis indexed by `ℕ` has the approximation
property, via the associated Schauder basis
(`HilbertBasis.toSchauderBasis`).

articles.title: Banach spaces with a Schauder basis have the approximation property
articles.statement:
A Banach space with a Schauder basis has the approximation property.
The partial-sum projections are finite-rank, converge pointwise to the
identity, and are uniformly bounded by the Banach–Steinhaus theorem
(`SchauderBasis.exists_norm_proj_le`); pointwise convergence plus uniform
boundedness gives uniform convergence on compact sets via a finite
`ε`-net argument.

articles.title: Approximation property
articles.statement:
A normed space has the **approximation property** if, on every compact
set, the identity operator is a uniform limit of finite-rank continuous
linear operators.

articles.title: Negative answer to Mazur's Problem 153
articles.statement:
There are a continuous function
$f \colon [0,1]^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ and a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every natural
number $n$, all points $a_1, \dots, a_n, b_1, \dots, b_n \in [0,1]$ and all real numbers
$c_1, \dots, c_n$ there are $x, y \in [0,1]$ with

$$\Bigl| f(x, y) - \sum_{k=1}^n c_k \, f(a_k, y) \, f(x, b_k) \Bigr| > \varepsilon.$$

That is, the approximation scheme of Mazur's Problem 153 fails.

## Sources

- S. Mazur, Problem 153 of the Scottish Book; refuted via P. Enflo's counterexample to the approximation problem in Banach spaces, Acta Math. 130 (1973), 309–317, DOI 10.1007/BF02392270; see the commentary in R. D. Mauldin (ed.), The Scottish Book, 2nd ed. (Birkhäuser, 2015). This is the original bivariate-function form of the problem, distinct from its consequence for the approximation property.

articles.title: Approximation property passes to complemented subspaces
articles.statement:
The approximation property passes to complemented subspaces: if `P` is a
continuous projection onto the submodule `F`, restrict a finite-rank
approximant on the ambient space via `P`. The key point is that `P` fixes
every point of `F`, so `P (S x) - x = P (S x - x)` for `x ∈ F`.

articles.title: Approximation property is invariant under linear isomorphism
articles.statement:
The approximation property is preserved under continuous linear
equivalence: conjugate a finite-rank approximant by the equivalence.

articles.title: Mazur's Problem 153
articles.statement:
The claim of Mazur's Problem 153 from the Scottish Book, in its
original form: for every continuous function $f \colon [0,1]^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ and every real
$\varepsilon > 0$ there are a natural number $n$, points
$a_1, \dots, a_n, b_1, \dots, b_n \in [0,1]$ and real numbers $c_1, \dots, c_n$ such that

$$\Bigl| f(x, y) - \sum_{k=1}^n c_k \, f(a_k, y) \, f(x, b_k) \Bigr| \le \varepsilon$$

for all $x, y \in [0,1]$.

articles.title: Coordinate functional of a basis as a continuous linear map
articles.statement:
The `i`-th coordinate functional of a basis, as a continuous linear map.
In finite dimensions every linear map is continuous, so this is just the
coordinate functional bundled with its continuity.

articles.title: Auerbach's theorem
articles.statement:
Every finite-dimensional normed space over `𝕜`
has an Auerbach basis, indexed by `Fin (Module.finrank 𝕜 E)`.

articles.title: Auerbach basis
articles.statement:
An *Auerbach basis* is a basis of unit vectors whose coordinate
functionals all have operator norm `1`.

articles.title: Coordinate functional of a unit basis vector has operator norm 1
articles.statement:
If the `i`-th basis vector has norm `1` and the `i`-th coordinate
functional is bounded by the norm, its operator norm is exactly `1`: it
attains `1` at the `i`-th basis vector.

articles.title: Operator norm of a norm-bounded coordinate functional is at most 1
articles.statement:
If the `i`-th coordinate functional is bounded by the norm, its operator
norm is at most `1`.

articles.title: Banach–Mazur embedding theorem
articles.statement:
Every separable real Banach space $E$ admits a linear
isometric embedding $e \colon E \to C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ into the space of continuous real
functions on $[0, 1]$ with the supremum norm, such that the range of $e$ is closed.

## Sources

- S. Banach and S. Mazur 1932 embedding theorem; Banach, Theorie des operations lineaires; Henson-Michalewski, separable Banach as universal space; Lean states separable real Banach case with `E →ₗᵢ[ℝ] C(Icc 0 1, ℝ)` and `IsClosed (range)`.

articles.title: Banach–Saks theorem for uniformly convex spaces
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real Banach
space and let $(x_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $E$. Then there are a strictly
increasing map $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a point $y \in E$ such that the Cesàro
means $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_{\varphi(i)}$ converge to $y$ in norm as $n \to \infty$.

## Sources

- S. Banach and S. Saks, Studia Math. 2 (1930) 51-57; uniformly convex form and property due to Kakutani, 1939; textbook Diestel, Sequences and Series in Banach Spaces; Lean gives uniformly convex real Banach specialization with explicit `StrictMono φ` and norm-convergent Cesàro means.

articles.title: Banach–Stone theorem for real scalars
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Hausdorff spaces, and let
$C(X, \mathbb{R})$ and $C(Y, \mathbb{R})$ be the real Banach spaces of continuous real functions
on them with the supremum norm. If there is a surjective linear isometry from $C(X, \mathbb{R})$
onto $C(Y, \mathbb{R})$, then $X$ and $Y$ are homeomorphic.

## Sources

- S. Banach, Theorie des operations lineaires, 1932 and M. Stone, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 41 (1937) 375-381; textbook Semadeni, Banach Spaces of Continuous Functions, 1971; Lean states compact Hausdorff case with Banach-space linear isometric isomorphism implies homeomorphism, real coefficient field specialization.

articles.title: Duality-mapping characterization of Birkhoff–James orthogonality
articles.statement:
Birkhoff–James orthogonality to `y` is equivalent to the existence of a
functional in the duality mapping at `x` that vanishes at `y`.

articles.title: Norming-functional characterization of Birkhoff–James orthogonality
articles.statement:
For `x ≠ 0`, Birkhoff–James orthogonality to `y` is equivalent to the
existence of a norming functional of `x` vanishing at `y`.

articles.title: Birkhoff–James orthogonality in inner product spaces
articles.statement:
In an inner product space, Birkhoff–James orthogonality is ordinary
inner-product orthogonality.

articles.title: Annihilating norming functional implies Birkhoff–James orthogonality
articles.statement:
If a norming functional of `x` vanishes at `y`, then `x` is
Birkhoff–James orthogonal to `y`.

articles.title: Only zero is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to itself
articles.statement: A vector is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to itself if and only if it is `0`.

articles.title: Homogeneity of Birkhoff–James orthogonality
articles.statement: Birkhoff–James orthogonality is homogeneous in both arguments.

articles.title: Zero is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to every vector
articles.statement: `0` is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to every vector.

articles.title: Every vector is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to zero
articles.statement: Every vector is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to `0`.

articles.title: Birkhoff–James orthogonality
articles.statement:
`x` is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to `y`
if `x` is a shortest vector on the affine line `x + 𝕜 • y`.

articles.title: Duality mapping is nonempty
articles.statement:
The duality mapping is nonempty at every point: take a Hahn–Banach norming
functional and scale it by `‖x‖`.

articles.title: Duality mapping of a normed space
articles.statement:
The **duality mapping** (duality set) at `x`: the functionals `f` with
`f x = ‖x‖ ^ 2` and `‖f‖ = ‖x‖`. At `x = 0` this is the singleton `{0}`.

articles.title: Birkhoff–James orthogonality gives an annihilating norming functional
articles.statement:
The converse: if `x ≠ 0` is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to `y`, there is a
norming functional of `x` vanishing at `y`. Birkhoff–James orthogonality makes
the distance from `x` to `𝕜 ∙ y` equal to `‖x‖`, so the dual distance formula
supplies an annihilating norming functional.

articles.title: Bishop–Phelps theorem
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, with dual space $E^*$. The functionals that attain their norm on the closed unit
ball, that is, the $f \in E^*$ such that $|f(x)| = \|f\|$ for some $x \in E$ with
$\|x\| \le 1$, form a dense subset of $E^*$ in the norm topology.

## Sources

- E. Bishop and R. R. Phelps, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 67 (1961) 97-98 and Pacific J. Math. 1961; Bollobas quantitative version; Lean states `RCLike` Banach case as density of attaining functionals.

articles.title: Daugavet's theorem for compact operators
articles.statement:
Let $C[0,1]$ be the real Banach space of continuous
functions $[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ with the supremum norm, and let $I$ be the identity operator on
it. Every compact bounded linear operator $T : C[0,1] \to C[0,1]$ satisfies
$\|I + T\| = 1 + \|T\|$, where the norms are operator norms.

## Sources

- I. K. Daugavet, Izv. Vyssh. Uchebn. Zaved. Matematika 1963; Kadets et al., 1980s Daugavet property; Werner, Recent progress on Daugavet property, 2001; Lean states `C(Icc 0 1, ℝ)` compact-operator specialization of the general Daugavet property `‖Id+T‖=1+‖T‖`.

articles.title: Dvoretzky–Rogers theorem
articles.statement:
Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space $E$ contains a series
that converges unconditionally but not absolutely: there is a sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $E$
such that the rearranged series $\sum_n x_{\sigma(n)}$ converges for every permutation $\sigma$
of $\mathbb{N}$, while $\sum_n \lVert x_n \rVert$ diverges.

## Sources

- S. Mazur and W. Orlicz, Problem 122 of the Scottish Book; A. Dvoretzky and C. A. Rogers, "Absolute and unconditional convergence in normed linear spaces", Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 36 (1950), 192-197.

articles.title: Extreme points of the unit ball of continuous real functions
articles.statement:
The extreme points of the closed unit ball of `C(X, ℝ)`, for `X`
compact Hausdorff, are exactly the functions with `|f x| = 1` for every
`x`.

articles.title: Extreme points of the unit ball of finite $\ell^1$
articles.statement:
The extreme points of the closed unit ball of `PiLp 1 (fun _ : ι => 𝕜)`
are exactly the unit multiples of the coordinate vectors. The proof: an
extreme point must have norm `1` (otherwise a one-coordinate perturbation
stays in the ball and exhibits it as a midpoint), and it cannot have two
nonzero coordinates (otherwise mass can be transferred between them, in
the direction of the phases of the two coordinates, staying at norm `1`
on both sides). Conversely, a unit multiple of a coordinate vector is
extreme: a convex combination equalling it must have total norm `1`,
hence coordinatewise triangle equality, hence vanishing off the
coordinate, and strict convexity of the scalar field at the coordinate.

articles.title: Extreme points of the unit ball of finite $\ell^\infty$
articles.statement:
The extreme points of the closed unit ball of `PiLp ∞ (fun _ : ι => 𝕜)`
are exactly the vectors all of whose coordinates have norm `1`. If some
coordinate has norm `< 1`, a small perturbation of that coordinate stays
in the ball and exhibits the point as a midpoint; conversely, a vector
with all coordinates of norm `1` that is a convex combination of two ball
points must agree with both of them coordinatewise, by strict convexity
of the scalar field.

articles.title: Membership criterion for extreme points of the unit ball of $C(X)$
articles.statement: Membership form of `extremePoints_closedBall_continuousMap`.

articles.title: Grothendieck's inequality (real case)
articles.statement:
There is a constant $K > 0$ such that for all
$m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, every real $m \times n$ matrix $A = (a_{ij})$, every real Hilbert space $H$
and all vectors $x_1, \dots, x_m, y_1, \dots, y_n \in H$ of norm at most $1$, there are signs
$\varepsilon_1, \dots, \varepsilon_m, \delta_1, \dots, \delta_n \in \{1, -1\}$ such that
$\bigl|\sum_{i=1}^{m} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij} \langle x_i, y_j \rangle\bigr| \le
K \bigl|\sum_{i=1}^{m} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij} \varepsilon_i \delta_j\bigr|$.

## Sources

- A. Grothendieck, Resume de la theorie metrique des produits tensoriels topologiques, Bol. Soc. Mat. Sao Paulo 8 (1953) 1-79, inequality; Pisier, Grothendieck's theorem past and present, 2012; Lean states real finite-matrix scalarized form with `Fin`-indexed unit vectors and `±1` signs, existential universal constant `K`.

articles.title: Scottish Book Problem 144 is false as stated
articles.statement:
The Scottish Book Problem 144 claim fails: some
separable real Banach space $E$ admits no injective map $f$ from its unit sphere $K$ to $[0, 1]$
such that the image under $f$ of every nonempty open subset of $K$ has positive Lebesgue outer
measure.

For example, take $E = \mathbb{R}$: its unit sphere is $\{-1, 1\}$, so $U = \{1\}$ is a nonempty
open subset of $K$, and its image under any $f$ is a single point, of measure zero. The source
contains no dimension restriction (it says "infinite-dimensional" explicitly when it means it,
e.g. Problem 7), so none is added here.

## Sources

- S. Mazur and S. Ulam, Problem 144 of the Scottish Book, typescript p. 63 (printed), PDF p. 66; see the commentary in R. D. Mauldin (ed.), The Scottish Book, 2nd ed. (Birkhäuser, 2015).

articles.title: Scottish Book Problem 144 (Mazur–Ulam), as a claim
articles.statement:
For every separable real Banach
space $E$, with unit sphere $K = \{x \in E : \|x\| = 1\}$, there is an injective map
$f \colon K \to [0, 1]$ such that for every nonempty open subset $U$ of $K$ the image $f(U)$ has
positive Lebesgue outer measure.

Mazur and Ulam ask, in a separable Banach space, whether such a map exists.

articles.title: Kadec–Klee iff, all-functionals form
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real normed space,
let $(u_n)$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. Then $u_n \to x$ in norm if and only if
$f(u_n) \to f(x)$ for every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{R}$ and
$\|u_n\| \to \|x\|$.

articles.title: Kadec–Klee iff, weak-topology form
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real normed space,
let $(u_n)$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. Then $u_n \to x$ in norm if and only if
$u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by the continuous linear
functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$) and $\|u_n\| \to \|x\|$.

articles.title: Kadec–Klee property, all-functionals form
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real normed
space, let $(u_n)$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ for every
continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\|u_n\| \to \|x\|$, then
$u_n \to x$ in norm.

articles.title: Kadec–Klee property, weak-topology form
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real normed
space, let $(u_n)$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology
of $E$ (the topology induced by the continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$) and
$\|u_n\| \to \|x\|$, then $u_n \to x$ in norm.

articles.title: Metric center of a pair of points
articles.statement:
Let $p, q, c$ be points of a pseudometric space $E$
and let $R_n$, for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, be the iterated metric center sets of $(p, q)$. We say
that $c$ is the metric center of $(p, q)$ when $c \in R_n$ for every $n$, and every point
$y \in E$ with $y \in R_n$ for every $n$ equals $c$.

articles.title: Mazur–Ulam Problem 69 refuted
articles.statement:
The Scottish Book Problem 69 claim is false: there is a
complete pseudometric space $E$ such that (1) for all $p, q \in E$ there is exactly one point
$c \in E$ that is the metric center of $(p, q)$, and (2) for all $p, q \in E$ there is exactly
one point $x \in E$ such that $q$ is the metric center of $(p, x)$, but there is no complete
real normed space $F$ with an isometric bijection $E \to F$.

## Sources

- S. Mazur and S. Ulam, Problem 69 of the Scottish Book; typescript Ad 69 records the negative answer (S. Mazur, December 21, 1936).

articles.title: Iterated metric center sets
articles.statement:
Let $p, q$ be points of a pseudometric space $E$ with
distance $d$. The iterated metric center sets $R_n \subseteq E$ of $(p, q)$, for
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, are defined by $R_0 = \{x \in E : d(p, x) + d(x, q) = d(p, q)\}$ and
$R_{n+1} = \{r \in R_n : d(r, x) \le \operatorname{diam}(R_n) / 2 \text{ for all } x \in R_n\}$.

articles.title: Scottish Book Problem 69 claim
articles.statement:
The statement that every complete pseudometric space
$E$ with the following two properties is isometric to a real Banach space: (1) for all
$p, q \in E$ there is exactly one point $c \in E$ that is the metric center of $(p, q)$, and
(2) for all $p, q \in E$ there is exactly one point $x \in E$ such that $q$ is the metric
center of $(p, x)$. Here "isometric to a real Banach space" means that there are a complete
real normed space $F$ and an isometric bijection $E \to F$. This is the affirmative answer to
Problem 69 of S. Mazur and S. Ulam in the Scottish Book.

articles.title: Milman–Pettis theorem
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a uniformly convex Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$
or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $E^*$ be the space of continuous linear functionals on $E$. Then every
continuous linear functional $\Phi$ on $E^*$ is evaluation at a point: there is $x \in E$ with
$\Phi(f) = f(x)$ for every $f \in E^*$.

## Sources

- D. Milman, C. R. (Doklady) Acad. Sci. URSS 18 (1938) and B. Pettis, Duke Math. J. 1939, Milman-Pettis theorem that uniformly convex Banach spaces are reflexive; Clarkson uniform convexity 1936; Lean states `RCLike` uniformly convex complete case via double-dual evaluation surjectivity.

articles.title: Mazur's Problem 91 has a negative answer
articles.statement:
There is a finite-dimensional real normed
space $E$ that is linearly isometric to its dual space $E^*$ (the continuous linear
functionals on $E$ with the operator norm) but whose norm is not induced by any inner
product on $E$. Thus the Banach-space form of Mazur's Problem 91 is false.

## Sources

- S. Mazur, Problem 91 of the Scottish Book. The typescript itself records the negative answer when `n` is even (for example, `ℓ¹ 2`, whose unit ball is a diamond, is linearly isometric to its dual `ℓ^∞ 2` but is not a Hilbert space, since its norm does not satisfy the parallelogram law); the odd-dimensional case is not needed to refute the universal claim.

articles.title: Mazur's Problem 91 (Scottish Book), Banach-space form
articles.statement:
This is the proposition that
every finite-dimensional real normed space $E$ that is linearly isometric to its dual
space $E^*$ (the continuous linear functionals on $E$ with the operator norm) is an inner
product space, that is, its norm is induced by some inner product on $E$.

Mazur's original formulation asks whether, for every $n$, a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$
that is affinely equivalent to its conjugate (polar) body is necessarily an ellipsoid.

articles.title: Bound on the average Rademacher norm
articles.statement:
The average Rademacher norm is at most `(∑ᵢ ‖xᵢ‖²)^{1/2}`
(Cauchy–Schwarz for the finite average, plus the exact second moment).

articles.title: Average squared Rademacher sum of unit vectors
articles.statement: For unit vectors, the average squared Rademacher sum equals `n`.

articles.title: Average squared norm of a Rademacher sum
articles.statement:
The average (uniform over sign vectors) of `‖∑ᵢ εᵢ • xᵢ‖²` is exactly
`∑ᵢ ‖xᵢ‖²`.

articles.title: Number of sign vectors of length n
articles.statement: Number of sign vectors: `Fin n → Bool` has `2 ^ n` elements.

articles.title: Discrete partial derivative on the Rademacher cube
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $n$ a
natural number and $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to X$. For $j \in \{1, \dots, n\}$ and
$\varepsilon = (\varepsilon_1, \dots, \varepsilon_n) \in \{-1, 1\}^n$, the discrete partial
derivative of $f$ in direction $j$ at $\varepsilon$ is

$$
D_j f(\varepsilon) = \frac{1}{2}\bigl(f(\varepsilon) -
f(\varepsilon_1, \dots, -\varepsilon_j, \dots, \varepsilon_n)\bigr),
$$

where only the $j$-th coordinate of $\varepsilon$ is negated in the second term.

articles.title: Enflo type
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $C \in [0, \infty]$ and $p$ a real number. We
say that $X$ has Enflo type $p$ with constant $C$ if for every $n \ge 1$ and every function
$f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to X$,

$$
\mathbb{E}\Bigl\|\frac{f(\varepsilon) - f(-\varepsilon)}{2}\Bigr\|^p \le
C^p \sum_{j=1}^n \mathbb{E}\,\|D_j f(\varepsilon)\|^p,
$$

where $\varepsilon = (\varepsilon_1, \dots, \varepsilon_n)$ is a sequence of independent
Rademacher random variables, $-\varepsilon = (-\varepsilon_1, \dots, -\varepsilon_n)$, and
$D_j f$ is the discrete partial derivative of $f$ in direction $j$. Both sides are computed in
$[0, \infty]$.

articles.title: Rademacher type
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $C \in [0, \infty]$ and $p$ a real
number. We say that $X$ has Rademacher type $p$ with constant $C$ if for every $n \ge 1$ and all
$x_1, \dots, x_n \in X$,

$$
\mathbb{E}\Bigl\|\sum_{j=1}^n \varepsilon_j x_j\Bigr\|^p \le C^p \sum_{j=1}^n \|x_j\|^p,
$$

where $\varepsilon_1, \dots, \varepsilon_n$ are independent Rademacher random variables. Both
sides are computed in $[0, \infty]$.

articles.title: Rademacher signs have norm one
articles.statement: Every Rademacher sign has norm `1`.

articles.title: Hilbert spaces have Rademacher cotype 2
articles.statement:
Rademacher cotype 2 with constant `1`: `∑ᵢ ‖xᵢ‖²` is at most the
average of the squared Rademacher sums.

articles.title: Rademacher distribution
articles.statement:
The Rademacher distribution is the measure on $\{-1, 1\}$,
viewed as a subset of $\mathbb{Z}$, that gives mass $1/2$ to each of $1$ and $-1$.

articles.title: Product Rademacher distribution
articles.statement:
For an index type $\iota$, this is the product over
$\iota$ of copies of the Rademacher distribution: the joint law of a family
$(\varepsilon_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of independent Rademacher random variables, as a measure on the
functions $\iota \to \{-1, 1\}$.

articles.title: Rademacher sign on a false coordinate is minus one
articles.statement: The sign is `-1` on a `false` coordinate.

articles.title: Rademacher sign on a true coordinate is one
articles.statement: The sign is `1` on a `true` coordinate.

articles.title: Rademacher sign of a coordinate
articles.statement:
The Rademacher sign attached to a coordinate: `1` for `true`, `-1`
for `false`.

articles.title: Hilbert spaces have Rademacher type 2
articles.statement:
Rademacher type 2 with constant `1`: the average of the squared
Rademacher sums is at most `∑ᵢ ‖xᵢ‖²`.

articles.title: Square-root form of the Rademacher second moment
articles.statement: Square-root form of the exact second moment.

articles.title: Second moment of a Rademacher sum in a Hilbert space
articles.statement:
Exact second moment of a Rademacher sum in a Hilbert space:
the sum over all sign vectors of `‖∑ᵢ εᵢ • xᵢ‖²` equals
`2 ^ n * ∑ᵢ ‖xᵢ‖²`. Cross terms cancel: the induction step pairs the
two values of the last sign and applies the parallelogram law.

articles.title: Second moment of a real Rademacher sum
articles.statement:
Scalar real form: the second moment of `∑ᵢ ±aᵢ` over all sign choices
is `2 ^ n * ∑ᵢ aᵢ²`.

articles.title: Enflo type constant
articles.statement:
For a real Banach space $X$ and a real number $p$, $T^E_p(X)$ is
the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of all $C \in [0, \infty]$ such that $X$ has Enflo type $p$ with
constant $C$.

articles.title: Comparison of Rademacher and Enflo type constants
articles.statement:
For every real Banach space $X$ and every
real number $p$ with $1 \le p \le 2$, the Rademacher type constant and the Enflo type constant
of $X$ satisfy $T^R_p(X) \le T^E_p(X) \le \frac{\pi}{\sqrt{2}}\, T^R_p(X)$.

## Sources

- P. Ivanisvili, R. van Handel, and A. Volberg, `Rademacher type and Enflo type coincide`, Annals of Math, 192 (2) 2020. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_rademacher_enflo_type` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Rademacher type constant
articles.statement:
For a real Banach space $X$ and a real number $p$,
$T^R_p(X)$ is the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of all $C \in [0, \infty]$ such that $X$ has
Rademacher type $p$ with constant $C$.

articles.title: Schauder basis
articles.statement:
A sequence $(e_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in a real normed space $E$ is a Schauder
basis when for every $x \in E$ there is exactly one sequence of real numbers $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$
such that the partial sums $\sum_{i < N} a_i e_i$ converge to $x$ as $N \to \infty$.

articles.title: Krein's theorem on bases in dense sets
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real Banach space that has a Schauder
basis. Then for every dense subset $H \subseteq E$ there is a Schauder basis $(e_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of
$E$ with $e_n \in H$ for all $n$, and likewise for every dense linear subspace $S \subseteq E$
there is a Schauder basis $(e_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of $E$ with $e_n \in S$ for all $n$.

## Sources

- S. Banach, S. Mazur, S. Ulam, Problem 108 of the Scottish Book; affirmative answer (Krein), typescript addendum Ad 108.

articles.title: Convergence of minimizing sequences in uniformly convex spaces
articles.statement:
In a complete uniformly convex space, a minimizing sequence for the
distance from a point `x` to a closed convex set `K` converges to a point
of `K` attaining that distance. The argument is the usual one: if the
sequence were not Cauchy, two far-apart almost-minimizing terms would have
normalized displacements far apart on the unit sphere, and uniform
convexity would force their midpoint to beat the infimum, contradicting
convexity of `K`.

articles.title: Unique nearest point from a minimizing sequence in finite dimensions
articles.statement:
In a finite-dimensional strictly convex space, a minimizing sequence for
the distance to a closed convex set supplies a unique nearest point. The
uniqueness clause only assumes that a second point belongs to the set and
attains the distance; it does not assume that the minimizing sequence
converges to that point.

articles.title: Minimizing sequences converge to the unique nearest point
articles.statement:
In a finite-dimensional strictly convex space, a minimizing sequence for
the distance to a closed convex set converges to the unique point of the
set attaining that distance. This preserves the original combined API as a
corollary of nearest-point uniqueness and minimizing-sequence convergence.

articles.title: Strict and uniform convexity agree in finite dimensions
articles.statement:
In finite dimensions, strict convexity and uniform convexity are
equivalent.

articles.title: Strict convexity implies uniform convexity in finite dimensions
articles.statement:
In a finite-dimensional real normed space, strict convexity implies
uniform convexity. The proof maximizes `‖x + y‖` over the compact set of
pairs of unit vectors at distance at least `ε`; strict convexity says the
maximum is `< 2`, and the gap is the required `δ`.

articles.title: Bezout identity for polynomials without a common zero
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex Banach space
and let $F, G : E \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous polynomial functions with no common zero, that
is, $G(x) \neq 0$ whenever $F(x) = 0$. Then there are continuous polynomial functions
$\varphi, \psi : E \to \mathbb{C}$ such that $F(x) \varphi(x) + G(x) \psi(x) = 1$ for every
$x \in E$.

This is the identity recorded in the addendum to Problem 27 of the Scottish Book (Mazur-Orlicz,
4 April 1939). The problem asks whether two complex polynomials on a complex Banach space that
both tend to $0$ along a sequence $(x_n)$ in the unit ball must have a common zero. The answer
is positive and follows from the identity by contradiction: continuous polynomials are bounded
on the unit ball, so $F(x_n) \varphi(x_n) + G(x_n) \psi(x_n)$ would tend to $0$, yet it equals
$1$.

## Sources

- S. Mazur and W. Orlicz, Problem 27 of the Scottish Book, with the positive answer via the Bezout identity in the addendum; see the commentary in R. D. Mauldin (ed.), The Scottish Book, 2nd ed. (Birkhäuser, 2015).

articles.title: Continuous polynomial functions on a complex normed space
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex normed
space. A function $F : E \to \mathbb{C}$ is a continuous polynomial function if there are a
natural number $n$, natural numbers $m_1, \dots, m_n$ and continuous $\mathbb{C}$-multilinear
maps $A_i : E^{m_i} \to \mathbb{C}$, with $A_i$ taking $m_i$ arguments, such that
$F(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} A_i(x, \dots, x)$ for every $x \in E$.

A $0$-multilinear map is a constant, so constant functions are polynomial functions.

articles.title: Mazur's Problem 55 has a negative answer
articles.statement:
The factorisation claim of Scottish Book
Problem 55 is false: there are a real Banach space $E$, an unbounded set $R \subseteq E$ and a
continuous bilinear form $B : E \times E \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for some $\varepsilon > 0$
the quadratic form $W(x) = B(x, x)$ is bounded on the set of points at distance less than
$\varepsilon$ from $R$, yet there are no continuous linear functional $L : E \to \mathbb{R}$,
constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ and real polynomial $V$ with $W(x) = V(L(x) + c)$ for all $x \in E$
and $|L(r) + c|$ bounded for $r \in R$.

## Sources

- S. Mazur, Problem 55 of the Scottish Book; refuted by V. Pestov, who constructs a continuous scalar-valued 2-polynomial `W` on the separable Hilbert space `ℓ²` and an unbounded set `R` such that `W` is bounded on an `ε`-neighbourhood of `R` but does not factor through any bounded first-degree polynomial sending `R` to a bounded set ("Two 1935 questions of Mazur about polynomials in Banach spaces: a counter-example", 1997, arXiv:funct-an/9705002). The same counterexample refutes Problem 75. In finite dimensions the answer is positive (Auerbach), so the infinite-dimensional Banach setting is essential.

articles.title: Mazur's Scottish Book Problem 75 fails in general Banach spaces
articles.statement:
The Scottish Book Problem 75
claim is false: there are a real Banach space $E$, a set $R \subseteq E$, a continuous bilinear
form $B$ on $E$ and a real $\alpha \ne 0$ such that $|B(x, x)|$ is bounded on some open
$\varepsilon$-neighbourhood of $R$ with $\varepsilon > 0$, but is unbounded on every open
$\delta$-neighbourhood of $\alpha R = \{\alpha r : r \in R\}$ with $\delta > 0$.

## Sources

- S. Mazur, Problem 75 of the Scottish Book; refuted by V. Pestov, whose counterexample to Problem 55 is a continuous scalar-valued 2-polynomial `W` on `ℓ²`, bounded on an `ε`-neighbourhood of an unbounded set `R`, but unbounded on `(1 / 2) R`, hence unbounded on every neighbourhood of `(1 / 2) R` ("Two 1935 questions of Mazur about polynomials in Banach spaces: a counter-example", 1997, arXiv:funct-an/9705002). Plichko and Zagorodnyuk gave an independent negative solution ("On automatic continuity and three problems of 'The Scottish Book' concerning the boundedness of polynomial functionals", J. Math. Anal. Appl. 220 (1998), 477–494). In the Euclidean case the statement is true, per typescript Ad 75.

articles.title: Mazur's factorisation claim (Scottish Book Problem 55)
articles.statement:
The claim that for every real
Banach space $E$, every unbounded set $R \subseteq E$ and every continuous bilinear form
$B : E \times E \to \mathbb{R}$, if the quadratic form $W(x) = B(x, x)$ is bounded on the set
of points at distance less than $\varepsilon$ from $R$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$, then there
are a continuous linear functional $L : E \to \mathbb{R}$, a constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ and a
real polynomial $V$ such that $W(x) = V(L(x) + c)$ for all $x \in E$ and $|L(r) + c|$ is
bounded for $r \in R$.

This is Mazur's question in the general Banach-space form for scalar-valued 2-polynomials: $W$
factors as $V \circ \varphi$ through the first-degree polynomial $\varphi(x) = L(x) + c$, which
maps $R$ to a bounded set.

articles.title: Scottish Book Problem 75 (Mazur), general Banach-space form
articles.statement:
The claim that for every real
Banach space $E$, every set $R \subseteq E$, every continuous bilinear form $B$ on $E$ and every
real $\alpha \ne 0$ the following holds: if for some $\varepsilon > 0$ the values $|B(x, x)|$ are
bounded on the open $\varepsilon$-neighbourhood of $R$, that is, for the $x \in E$ with
$\operatorname{dist}(x, r) < \varepsilon$ for some $r \in R$, then for some $\delta > 0$ the values
$|B(x, x)|$ are bounded on the open $\delta$-neighbourhood of the scaled set
$\alpha R = \{\alpha r : r \in R\}$.

articles.title: Norm bound for the finite $\ell^p$ lift
articles.statement:
The target `ℓ^p` norm of the finite lift is bounded by
`N ^ (1 / p)` times the supremum norm of its first `N` coordinates.
The norm on the source Pi type `Fin N → 𝕜` is the supremum norm.

articles.statement: Truncation is a contraction.

articles.title: Riesz–Fréchet–Kolmogorov criterion for total boundedness in $\ell^p$
articles.statement:
The Riesz–Fréchet–Kolmogorov criterion for `ℓ^p (ℕ, 𝕜)`, `1 ≤ p < ∞`:
a set is totally bounded if and only if it is bounded and its tails vanish
uniformly.

articles.title: Uniform vanishing of tails
articles.statement:
The tails of the elements of a set `K` vanish uniformly: for every
`ε > 0` there is `N` such that every `x ∈ K` is within `ε` of its truncation
to the first `N` coordinates.

Convolution of two coordinate vectors: positions add, coefficients

Convolution of an `ℓ¹` sequence with an `ℓ^p` sequence, as an element of

articles.statement: Translating an `ℓ^p` sequence on `ℤ` preserves `ℓ^p` membership.

The terms of a convolution of an `ℓ¹` sequence with an `ℓ^p` sequence are

articles.title: The $\ell^1$ norm as a sum of coordinate norms
articles.statement: The `ℓ¹` norm is the sum of the coordinate norms.

articles.title: Coordinates are bounded by the norm in $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, and let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of families $x = (x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ in
$\mathbb{K}$ that tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter, with the supremum norm. Then
$|x_i| \le \|x\|$ for every $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and every index $i \in \iota$.

articles.title: Finite sums of the coefficients of a functional on $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$
or $\mathbb{C}$, let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of families in $\mathbb{K}$ indexed by
$\iota$ that tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter, with the supremum norm, and for $i \in \iota$
let $e_i \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the family that is $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. For every
continuous linear functional $\Phi$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and every finite set
$s \subseteq \iota$, we have $\sum_{i \in s} |\Phi(e_i)| \le \|\Phi\|$, where $\|\Phi\|$ is the
operator norm.

articles.title: The $\ell^1$ coefficient sequence of a functional on $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of families in $\mathbb{K}$
indexed by $\iota$ that tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter, and for $i \in \iota$ let
$e_i \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the family that is $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. For a
continuous linear functional $\Phi$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, this is the family
$(\Phi(e_i))_{i \in \iota}$, regarded as an element of the space $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ of
absolutely summable families.

articles.title: The coefficients of a functional on $c_0$ are absolutely summable
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of families in $\mathbb{K}$
indexed by $\iota$ that tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter, and for $i \in \iota$ let
$e_i \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the family that is $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. For every
continuous linear functional $\Phi$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the family
$(\Phi(e_i))_{i \in \iota}$ lies in $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, that is,
$\sum_{i \in \iota} |\Phi(e_i)| < \infty$.

articles.title: Coefficients of a functional on $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$,
let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of families in $\mathbb{K}$ indexed by $\iota$ that tend
to $0$ along the cofinite filter, and for $i \in \iota$ let $e_i \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the
family that is $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. The coefficients of a continuous linear functional
$\Phi$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ are the family $i \mapsto \Phi(e_i)$ in $\mathbb{K}$.

articles.title: The dual of $c_0$ is $\ell^1$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let
$c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of families in $\mathbb{K}$ indexed by $\iota$ that tend to
$0$ along the cofinite filter, with the supremum norm, and let $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the
space of absolutely summable families, with the norm $\|a\|_1 = \sum_{i \in \iota} |a_i|$. This
is the linear isometric isomorphism from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ onto the space of continuous
linear functionals on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, with the operator norm, that sends $a$ to the
functional $x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$.

articles.title: Formula for the $\ell^1$–$c_0$ duality pairing
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of families in $\mathbb{K}$ indexed by
$\iota$ that tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter, and let $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the
space of absolutely summable families. For $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and
$x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the canonical continuous linear map from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$
to the continuous linear functionals on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ sends $a$ to a functional whose
value at $x$ is $\sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$.

articles.title: Formula for the $\ell^1$–$c_0$ pairing as a linear map
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of families in $\mathbb{K}$ indexed by
$\iota$ that tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter, and let $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the
space of absolutely summable families. For $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and
$x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the linear map from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to the continuous
linear functionals on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ given by the pairing sends $a$ to a functional
whose value at $x$ is $\sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$. This holds by definition.

articles.title: The $\ell^1$–$c_0$ pairing is continuous in the $\ell^1$ variable
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of families in $\mathbb{K}$
indexed by $\iota$ that tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter, with the supremum norm, and let
$\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of absolutely summable families. The linear map from
$\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to the space of continuous linear functionals on
$c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, with the operator norm, that sends $a$ to the functional
$x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$ is continuous.

articles.title: The $\ell^1$–$c_0$ pairing as a linear map
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of families in $\mathbb{K}$ indexed by
$\iota$ that tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter, and let $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the
space of absolutely summable families. This is the linear map from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to
the space of continuous linear functionals on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ that sends $a$ to the
functional $x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$.

articles.title: The $\ell^1$–$c_0$ pairing is isometric
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field
and $\iota$ an index type. For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the continuous linear
functional $x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the space of
sequences $\iota \to \mathbb{K}$ tending to $0$ at infinity with the supremum norm, has operator
norm equal to $\|a\|_1 = \sum_{i \in \iota} |a_i|$.

articles.title: Pairing with a unit vector is evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field
and $\iota$ an index type, and for $i \in \iota$ let $e_i \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the
sequence equal to $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then the functional
$x \mapsto \sum_{j \in \iota} (e_i)_j x_j$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ given by pairing with
$e_i$ is the evaluation $x \mapsto x_i$ at $i$.

articles.title: Every functional on $c_0$ comes from $\ell^1$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex
field and $\iota$ an index type. For every continuous linear functional $\varphi$ on
$c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ there is $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with
$\varphi(x) = \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$ for all $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$; that is, the
pairing map from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to the continuous dual of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$
is surjective.

The proof takes $a_i = \varphi(e_i)$, where $e_i$ is the sequence equal to $1$ at $i$ and $0$
elsewhere, and recovers $\varphi(x)$ as the limit of $\varphi$ on the finite truncations of $x$.

articles.title: The $\ell^1$–$c_0$ duality pairing
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and
$\iota$ an index type. The pairing is the continuous linear map from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$
to the continuous dual of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ that sends $a$ to the functional
$x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$.

articles.title: Coordinate evaluation on $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$
an index type. For $i \in \iota$, evaluation at $i$ is the continuous linear functional
$x \mapsto x_i$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$.

articles.title: A functional on a finitely supported sequence
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex
field and $\iota$ an index type, and let $e_i \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the sequence equal
to $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. For every continuous linear functional $\varphi$ on
$c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, every finite set $s \subseteq \iota$ and every $c : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$,
we have $\varphi(\sum_{i \in s} c_i e_i) = \sum_{i \in s} c_i \, \varphi(e_i)$.

articles.title: Coordinates of a finitely supported sequence
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex
field and $\iota$ an index type, and let $e_i \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the sequence equal
to $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. For every finite set $s \subseteq \iota$, every
$c : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ and every $j \in \iota$, the $j$-th coordinate of
$\sum_{i \in s} c_i e_i$ is $c_j$ if $j \in s$ and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Finitely supported sequences in $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and
$\iota$ an index type, and let $e_i \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the sequence equal to $1$ at
$i$ and $0$ elsewhere. For a finite set $s \subseteq \iota$ and $c : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$, the
finitely supported sequence with coefficients $c$ on $s$ is the element
$\sum_{i \in s} c_i e_i$ of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$.

articles.title: $c_0$ is isometrically isomorphic to the null sequences in $\ell^\infty$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$
be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type. The map that sends
$x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to the same sequence $(x_i)_{i \in \iota}$, viewed in the subspace
of $\ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ of sequences tending to $0$ along the cofinite filter, is a
linear isometric equivalence onto that subspace.

articles.title: The $c_0$ norm is the supremum norm
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and
$\iota$ an index type. For every $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the norm of $x$ equals the
norm $\sup_{i \in \iota} |x_i|$ of $x$ viewed as an element of $\ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$.

articles.title: Sequences in $\ell^\infty$ tending to zero as elements of $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. A bounded sequence
$x \in \ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ whose coordinates $x_i$ tend to $0$ along the
cofinite filter on $\iota$ defines the element of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with the same
coordinates.

articles.title: Value of the functional of an $\ell^1$ sequence on $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. For $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$
and $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the linear functional on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ given by
pairing with $a$ takes the value $\sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$ at $x$.

articles.title: Pairing with an $\ell^1$ sequence as a linear functional on $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$
be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. For
$a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, this is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map
$c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K}) \to \mathbb{K}$ sending $x$ to $\sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$.

articles.title: Coordinates of the sequence supported at one index
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$
or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. For indices $i, j \in \iota$ and
$a \in \mathbb{K}$, the $j$-th coordinate of the element of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ that is
$a$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere equals $a$ if $j = i$ and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Norm of a sequence supported at one index
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. For $i \in \iota$ and $a \in \mathbb{K}$, the
element of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ that is $a$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere has norm $\|a\|$.

articles.title: Sequence supported at one index
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and
let $\iota$ be an index type. For an index $i \in \iota$ and a scalar $a \in \mathbb{K}$, this
is the element of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $a$ and whose other
coordinates are $0$.

articles.title: The subspace of null sequences in $\ell^\infty$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. The sequences $x \in \ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$
whose coordinates $x_i$ tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter on $\iota$ form a
$\mathbb{K}$-linear subspace of $\ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$.

articles.title: Elements of $c_0$ tend to zero along the cofinite filter
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be an index type, and let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be
the space of functions $\iota \to \mathbb{K}$ vanishing at infinity for the discrete
topology on $\iota$. For every $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the coordinates $x_i$ tend to
$0$ along the cofinite filter on $\iota$.

articles.title: Inclusion of $c_0$ in $\ell^\infty$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$
and let $\iota$ be an index type. Every $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ is a bounded sequence,
and this map sends it to the element of $\ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with the same
coordinates $x_i$.

articles.title: Coordinates of a finite truncation
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$
and let $\iota$ be an index type. For a finite set $s \subseteq \iota$, an element
$x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and an index $j \in \iota$, the $j$-th coordinate of the
truncation of $x$ to $s$ equals $x_j$ if $j \in s$ and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Finite truncation of a $c_0$ sequence
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let
$\iota$ be a type, let $s \subseteq \iota$ be a finite set and let $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$.
The truncation of $x$ to $s$ is the element of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ whose $j$-th coordinate is
$x_j$ for $j \in s$ and $0$ for $j \notin s$; it is defined as $\sum_{i \in s} x_i e_i$, where
$e_i$ is the sequence that is $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere.

articles.title: The normalizing scalar times $w$ is $|w|$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$.
For every $w \in \mathbb{K}$, the normalizing scalar $u(w)$ of $w$, which is $0$ if $w = 0$ and
$\overline{w}/|w|$ otherwise, satisfies $u(w)\, w = |w|$, with $|w|$ regarded as an element of
$\mathbb{K}$.

articles.title: The normalizing scalar $\overline{w}/|w|$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$.
For $w \in \mathbb{K}$, the normalizing scalar $u(w) \in \mathbb{K}$ of $w$ is $0$ if $w = 0$ and
$\overline{w}/|w|$ otherwise, so that $u(w)\, w = |w|$.

articles.title: The sequence space $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$
be a type. The space $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ consists of the functions $x : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$
that tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter, that is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ the set
$\{i : |x_i| \ge \varepsilon\}$ is finite, with pointwise operations and the supremum norm
$\|x\|_\infty = \sup_i |x_i|$. It is realized as the space of continuous functions vanishing at
infinity on $\iota$ with the discrete topology; no topology on $\iota$ is assumed.

articles.title: Dual of $\ell^p$ is isometric to $\ell^q$
articles.statement: The dual of `ℓ^p` is isometrically isomorphic to `ℓ^q`.

articles.title: Duality pairing as a sum of coordinatewise products
articles.statement: The pairing is given by the sum of coordinatewise products.

articles.title: Duality pairing is norm-preserving
articles.statement: The pairing is norm-preserving.

articles.title: Every functional on $\ell^p$ comes from an $\ell^q$ sequence
articles.statement:
The pairing is surjective: every continuous linear functional on `ℓ^p` is given
by pairing with some `ℓ^q` sequence.

articles.title: Canonical duality pairing between $\ell^q$ and $\ell^p$
articles.statement:
The canonical pairing `ℓ^q × ℓ^p → 𝕜`, as a continuous linear map
`ℓ^q →L[𝕜] (ℓ^p →L[𝕜] 𝕜)`.

articles.title: $\ell^1$ norm of the coefficients of a functional on $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$
or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type and let $\Phi$ be a continuous linear functional on
$c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$. For $i \in \iota$ let $e_i$ be the sequence that is $1$ at $i$ and $0$
elsewhere. The coefficient sequence $(\Phi(e_i))_{i \in \iota}$, as an element of
$\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, has norm $\sum_{i \in \iota} |\Phi(e_i)|$ at most the operator norm
$\|\Phi\|$.

articles.title: The pairing map $\ell^1 \to c_0^*$ does not increase norms
articles.statement:
**The pairing map $\ell^1 \to c_0^*$ does not increase norms.** Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type, and let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})^*$ be the
space of continuous linear functionals on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$. For every
$a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the image of $a$ under the continuous linear pairing map
$\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K}) \to c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})^*$, which is the functional
$x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$, has operator norm at most $\|a\|_1 = \sum_i |a_i|$.

articles.title: Norm bound for the functional of an $\ell^1$ sequence on $c_0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be a type. For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$,
the image of $a$ under the linear pairing map from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to the continuous
linear functionals on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, which is the functional
$x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$, has operator norm at most $\|a\|_1 = \sum_i |a_i|$.

articles.title: Bound for the $\ell^1$–$c_0$ pairing
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and
let $\iota$ be a type. For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and
$x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, $|\sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i| \le \|a\|_1 \|x\|_\infty$, where
$\|a\|_1 = \sum_i |a_i|$ and $\|x\|_\infty = \sup_i |x_i|$.

articles.title: The normalizing scalar has absolute value at most one
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$. For every $w \in \mathbb{K}$, the normalizing scalar $u(w)$ of $w$, which is $0$ if
$w = 0$ and $\overline{w}/|w|$ otherwise, satisfies $|u(w)| \le 1$.

articles.title: Duality pairing has operator norm at most one
articles.statement: The pairing has operator norm at most one.

articles.title: Summability of the $\ell^1$–$c_0$ pairing
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$
and let $\iota$ be a type. For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and
$x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the family $(a_i x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ is (unconditionally)
summable.

articles.title: Coordinate norms of an $\ell^1$ family are summable
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be any index type. For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the
family of norms $(\|a_i\|)_{i \in \iota}$ is summable.

articles.title: The vector $(1, -1)$ in $\ell^p_2$
articles.statement:
For $p \in [0, \infty]$, write $\ell^p_2$ for the
space $\mathbb{R}^2$ regarded as the $\ell^p$ product of two copies of $\mathbb{R}$ (normed by the
$\ell^p$ norm when $p \ge 1$). The vector $v_p \in \ell^p_2$ is $(1, -1)$, that is, $e_0 - e_1$,
where $e_0 = (1, 0)$ and $e_1 = (0, 1)$ are the standard basis vectors.

articles.title: Sum of $(1, 1)$ and $(1, -1)$ in $\ell^p_2$
articles.statement:
For every $p \in [0, \infty]$, write $\ell^p_2$
for the space $\mathbb{R}^2$ regarded as the $\ell^p$ product of two copies of $\mathbb{R}$. The
vectors $u_p = (1, 1)$ and $v_p = (1, -1)$ of $\ell^p_2$ satisfy $u_p + v_p = 2 e_0$, where
$e_0 = (1, 0)$ is the first standard basis vector.

articles.title: Difference of $(1, 1)$ and $(1, -1)$ in $\ell^p_2$
articles.statement:
For every $p \in [0, \infty]$, write
$\ell^p_2$ for the space $\mathbb{R}^2$ regarded as the $\ell^p$ product of two copies of
$\mathbb{R}$. The vectors $u_p = (1, 1)$ and $v_p = (1, -1)$ of $\ell^p_2$ satisfy
$u_p - v_p = 2 e_1$, where $e_1 = (0, 1)$ is the second standard basis vector.

articles.title: The vector $(1, 1)$ in $\ell^p_2$
articles.statement:
For $p \in [0, \infty]$, write $\ell^p_2$ for the
space $\mathbb{R}^2$ regarded as the $\ell^p$ product of two copies of $\mathbb{R}$ (normed by the
$\ell^p$ norm when $p \ge 1$). The vector $u_p \in \ell^p_2$ is $(1, 1)$, that is, $e_0 + e_1$,
where $e_0 = (1, 0)$ and $e_1 = (0, 1)$ are the standard basis vectors.

articles.title: Norm of $(1, 1) + (1, -1)$ in $\ell^p_2$
articles.statement:
For every $p \in [1, \infty]$, let $\ell^p_2$ be
$\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm, and let $u_p = (1, 1)$ and $v_p = (1, -1)$. Then
$\|u_p + v_p\| = 2$.

articles.title: The $\ell^p$ norm of $(1, -1)$ for finite $p$
articles.statement:
For every real $p$ with $1 \le p < \infty$,
the vector $(1, -1)$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ has $\ell^p$ norm $\|(1, -1)\|_p = 2^{1/p}$, where
$\|(x, y)\|_p = (|x|^p + |y|^p)^{1/p}$.

articles.title: The $\ell^\infty$ norm of $(1, -1)$
articles.statement:
In $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^\infty$ norm
$\|(x, y)\|_\infty = \max(|x|, |y|)$, the vector $(1, -1)$ has norm $\|(1, -1)\|_\infty = 1$.

articles.title: The $\ell^p$ norm of $(1, 1)$ for finite $p$
articles.statement:
For every real $p$ with $1 \le p < \infty$,
the vector $(1, 1)$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ has $\ell^p$ norm $\|(1, 1)\|_p = 2^{1/p}$, where
$\|(x, y)\|_p = (|x|^p + |y|^p)^{1/p}$.

articles.title: The $\ell^\infty$ norm of $(1, 1)$
articles.statement:
In $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^\infty$ norm
$\|(x, y)\|_\infty = \max(|x|, |y|)$, the vector $(1, 1)$ has norm $\|(1, 1)\|_\infty = 1$.

articles.title: The squared $\ell^p$ norm of $(1, 1)$ for finite $p$
articles.statement:
For every real $p$ with
$1 \le p < \infty$, the vector $(1, 1)$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfies $\|(1, 1)\|_p^2 = 2^{2/p}$,
where $\|(x, y)\|_p = (|x|^p + |y|^p)^{1/p}$ is the $\ell^p$ norm.

articles.title: The difference of the parallelogram witnesses has norm two
articles.statement:
For every extended real
$p \in [1, \infty]$, in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm the vectors $u = (1, 1)$ and
$v = (1, -1)$ satisfy $\|u - v\| = 2$.

articles.title: The $\ell^p$ norm on $\mathbb{R}^2$ comes from no inner product unless $p = 2$
articles.statement:
Let
$p \in [1, \infty]$ with $p \neq 2$. Then the normed space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm
carries no real inner product space structure, that is, there is no real inner product with
$\langle x, x \rangle = \|x\|^2$ for every $x$.

Any such inner product would satisfy the parallelogram law, which fails for $(1, 1)$ and
$(1, -1)$.

articles.title: Two distinct $\ell^1$ unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with a unit midpoint
articles.statement:
In
$\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^1$ norm there exist vectors $x \neq y$ with $\|x\| = \|y\| = 1$
and $\|\tfrac{1}{2} (x + y)\| = 1$.

For example, the unit vectors $(1, 0)$ and $(0, 1)$ have midpoint $(1/2, 1/2)$ of norm $1$.

articles.title: Two distinct $\ell^\infty$ unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with a unit midpoint
articles.statement:
In
$\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^\infty$ norm there exist vectors $x \neq y$ with
$\|x\| = \|y\| = 1$ and $\|\tfrac{1}{2} (x + y)\| = 1$.

For example, the unit vectors $(1, 1)$ and $(1, -1)$ have midpoint $(1, 0)$ of norm $1$.

articles.title: $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^1$ norm is not strictly convex
articles.statement:
The real normed space
$\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^1$ norm is not a strictly convex space: not every closed ball of
positive radius centred at the origin is a strictly convex set.

articles.title: $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^\infty$ norm is not strictly convex
articles.statement:
The real normed space
$\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^\infty$ norm is not a strictly convex space: not every closed ball
of positive radius centred at the origin is a strictly convex set.

articles.title: The parallelogram law for $(1, 1)$ and $(1, -1)$ holds only for the $\ell^2$ norm
articles.statement:
Let
$p \in [1, \infty]$ and equip $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm. The vectors $u = (1, 1)$ and
$v = (1, -1)$ satisfy $\|u + v\|^2 + \|u - v\|^2 = 2 (\|u\|^2 + \|v\|^2)$ if and only if
$p = 2$.

articles.title: The parallelogram law fails on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm for $p \neq 2$
articles.statement:
Let
$p \in [1, \infty]$ with $p \neq 2$ and equip $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm. Then the
vectors $u = (1, 1)$ and $v = (1, -1)$ satisfy
$\|u + v\|^2 + \|u - v\|^2 \neq 2 (\|u\|^2 + \|v\|^2)$.

articles.title: Midpoints of distinct $\ell^p$ unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$ have norm less than one
articles.statement:
Let $1 < p < \infty$ and equip $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm. If $x \neq y$ are vectors
with $\|x\| = \|y\| = 1$, then $\|\tfrac{1}{2} (x + y)\| < 1$.

articles.title: $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm is strictly convex for $1 < p < \infty$
articles.statement:
For
$1 < p < \infty$, the real normed space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm is a strictly
convex space: every closed ball of positive radius centred at the origin is a strictly convex
set.

articles.title: Pitt's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let
$1 \le q < p < \infty$. Then every bounded linear operator
$T : \ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K}) \to \ell^q(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is compact.

## Sources

- H. R. Pitt, A Note on Bilinear Forms, J. London Math. Soc. s1-11 (1936), 174–180, DOI 10.1112/JLMS/S1-11.3.174, compactness of operators `ℓ^p → ℓ^q` for `q<p`; textbook Albiac and Kalton, Topics in Banach Space Theory Prop 2.1.6; Lean states `RCLike` `lp _ p →L[𝕜] lp _ q` with `q<p<∞` compact specialization via `IsCompactOperator`.

articles.title: Uniform $\ell^1$ lower bound
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$. A sequence $(y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ has a uniform $\ell^1$ lower bound when
there is a real $c > 0$ such that $\|\sum_i a_i y_i\| \ge c \sum_i |a_i|$ for every finitely
supported sequence $(a_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of scalars in $\mathbb{K}$, both sums running over
the finitely many $i$ with $a_i \ne 0$.

articles.title: Rosenthal's $\ell^1$ theorem
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$ and let $(x_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $E$. Then there is a
strictly increasing $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that either the subsequence
$(x_{\varphi(n)})_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is weakly Cauchy, that is, for every continuous linear
functional $f : E \to \mathbb{K}$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $N$ with
$|f(x_{\varphi(m)}) - f(x_{\varphi(n)})| < \varepsilon$ for all $m, n \ge N$, or
$(x_{\varphi(n)})_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ has a uniform $\ell^1$ lower bound.

Proof: We use the Nash-Williams/Galvin-Prikry Ramsey route, following Rosenthal's 1974 theorem,
Albiac and Kalton, Sections 10.1–10.2, and Farahat's 1974 proof.

## Sources

- H. P. Rosenthal, A Characterization of Banach Spaces Containing l1, PNAS 71 (1974), 2411–2413, DOI 10.1073/pnas.71.6.2411, ℓ¹ dichotomy theorem; Bourgain et al., extensions; Lean states `RCLike` Banach bounded `Set.range` dichotomy with `StrictMono φ` and `HasUniformL1LowerBound` defined via `ℕ →₀ 𝕜` finitely supported coefficients.

articles.title: Basis vectors of the ℓᵖ Schauder basis
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$
and let $1 \le p < \infty$. For every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th basis vector of the Schauder
basis of $\ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ by unit vectors is the unit vector $e_i$, the sequence
equal to $1$ at $i$ and to $0$ elsewhere.

articles.title: Coordinate functionals of the ℓᵖ Schauder basis
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$ and let $1 \le p < \infty$. For every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
$x \in \ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the $i$-th coordinate functional of the Schauder basis of
$\ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ by unit vectors sends $x$ to its $i$-th entry $x_i$.

articles.title: The ℓᵖ partial-sum projections are truncations
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$ and let $1 \le p < \infty$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
$x \in \ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the $n$-th partial-sum projection $P_n$ of the Schauder
basis of $\ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ by unit vectors satisfies $P_n x = \sum_{i < n} x_i e_i$,
where $e_i$ is the unit vector equal to $1$ at $i$ and to $0$ elsewhere; that is, $P_n x$ is the
truncation of $x$ to its first $n$ coordinates.

articles.title: The unit vectors form a Schauder basis of ℓᵖ
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$ and let $1 \le p < \infty$. This is the Schauder basis of
$\ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ whose $i$-th basis vector is the unit vector $e_i$, equal to $1$ at
$i$ and to $0$ elsewhere, and whose $i$-th coordinate functional is the evaluation $x \mapsto x_i$.
In particular every $x \in \ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the limit in norm of its partial sums
$\sum_{i < n} x_i e_i$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Basis vectors of the unconditional ℓᵖ basis
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, let $1 \le p < \infty$ and let $\iota$ be a type. For every $i \in \iota$, the
$i$-th basis vector of the unconditional Schauder basis of $\ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ by unit
vectors is the unit vector $e_i$, the family equal to $1$ at $i$ and to $0$ elsewhere.

articles.title: Coordinate functionals of the unconditional ℓᵖ basis
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, let $1 \le p < \infty$ and let $\iota$ be a type. For every $i \in \iota$ and every
$x \in \ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the $i$-th coordinate functional of the unconditional Schauder
basis of $\ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ by unit vectors sends $x$ to its entry $x_i$.

articles.title: Finite-set projections of the unconditional ℓᵖ basis
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, let $1 \le p < \infty$ and let $\iota$ be a type. For every finite set
$A \subseteq \iota$ and every $x \in \ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the projection $P_A$ of the
unconditional Schauder basis of $\ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ by unit vectors onto the basis vectors
indexed by $A$ satisfies $P_A x = \sum_{i \in A} x_i e_i$, where $e_i$ is the unit vector equal
to $1$ at $i$ and to $0$ elsewhere.

articles.title: The unit vectors form an unconditional Schauder basis of ℓᵖ
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $1 \le p < \infty$ and let $\iota$ be a type. This is the
unconditional Schauder basis of $\ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ whose $i$-th basis vector is the unit
vector $e_i$, equal to $1$ at $i$ and to $0$ elsewhere, and whose $i$-th coordinate functional is
the evaluation $x \mapsto x_i$. In particular every $x \in \ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ is the
limit in norm of the finite partial sums $\sum_{i \in A} x_i e_i$ along the finite sets
$A \subseteq \iota$ directed by inclusion.

articles.title: The ℓᵖ partial-sum projections are contractions
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$ and let $1 \le p < \infty$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
$x \in \ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the $n$-th partial-sum projection $P_n$ of the Schauder
basis of $\ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ by unit vectors satisfies $\|P_n x\| \le \|x\|$.

articles.title: The ℓᵖ partial-sum projections have norm at most one
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$
or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $1 \le p < \infty$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th partial-sum
projection of the Schauder basis of $\ell^p(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ by unit vectors has operator
norm at most $1$.

articles.title: Basis projections of $\ell^p$ are contractive
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be an index set and let $1 \le p < \infty$. Let $e_i$ ($i \in \iota$) be
the unit vectors, which form an unconditional Schauder basis of $\ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$. For
every finite set $A \subseteq \iota$ and every $x \in \ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the basis
projection $P_A x = \sum_{i \in A} x_i e_i$ satisfies $\|P_A x\|_p \le \|x\|_p$.

articles.title: The $\ell^p$ basis projections have operator norm at most $1$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be an index set and let $1 \le p < \infty$. Let $e_i$
($i \in \iota$) be the unit vectors, which form an unconditional Schauder basis of
$\ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$. For every finite set $A \subseteq \iota$, the basis projection
$P_A$, the bounded linear operator on $\ell^p(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ given by
$P_A x = \sum_{i \in A} x_i e_i$, has operator norm $\|P_A\| \le 1$.

articles.title: Pairing $\ell^1$ with a sequence bounded by one
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, and let $(y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb{K}$ with
$|y_i| \le 1$ for every $i$. The pairing with $y$ is the continuous linear functional
$\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K}) \to \mathbb{K}$ given by $x \mapsto \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} y_i x_i$.

articles.title: The $\ell^1$ norm is the sum of the coordinate norms
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$. Every $x \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ satisfies
$\|x\| = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |x_i|$.

articles.title: Pairing with a sequence bounded by one has norm at most one
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $(y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb{K}$
with $|y_i| \le 1$ for every $i$. The continuous linear functional
$x \mapsto \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} y_i x_i$ on $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ has operator norm at
most $1$.

articles.title: The conjugate-sign sequence is bounded by one
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, let
$n' : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be such that every
$i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(j + 1)$ for some $j$. Every term $\sigma_i$ of the
conjugate-sign sequence of $(x_n)$, $n'$ and $M$ satisfies $|\sigma_i| \le 1$.

articles.title: Indices in block $k$ have block index $k$
articles.statement:
Let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be
monotone, and suppose every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(j + 1)$ for some $j$. For all
$k, i \in \mathbb{N}$ with $M(k) \le i < M(k + 1)$, the block index of $i$ (the least $j$ with
$i < M(j + 1)$) is $k$.

articles.title: An index lies in the block it is assigned to
articles.statement:
Let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy
$M(0) = 0$, and suppose every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(j + 1)$ for some $j$. For
every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, if $k$ is the block index of $i$ (the least $k$ with
$i < M(k + 1)$), then $M(k) \le i < M(k + 1)$.
