articles.title: Block index for a cutoff sequence
articles.statement:
Let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be such that
every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(k + 1)$ for some $k$. The block index of
$i \in \mathbb{N}$ is the least $k$ with $i < M(k + 1)$.

When $M$ is monotone and $M(0) = 0$, the block index of $i$ is the unique $k$ with
$M(k) \le i < M(k + 1)$.

articles.title: On block $k$, the conjugate signs recover absolute values
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$,
let $n' : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be monotone and
such that every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(j + 1)$ for some $j$. Let $\sigma$ be the
conjugate-sign sequence of $(x_n)$, $n'$ and $M$. For all $k, i \in \mathbb{N}$ with
$M(k) \le i < M(k + 1)$, we have $\sigma_i \, x_{n'(k)}(i) = |x_{n'(k)}(i)|$.

articles.title: Conjugate-sign sequence of a block decomposition
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$, let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, let
$n' : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and let $M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be such that every
$i \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $i < M(j + 1)$ for some $j$. For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, let $k$ be
the block index of $i$ (the least $k$ with $i < M(k + 1)$) and let $v = x_{n'(k)}(i)$. The
$i$-th term $\sigma_i$ of the conjugate-sign sequence is $0$ if $v = 0$, and
$\overline{v} / |v|$ otherwise.

articles.title: Schur's theorem, norm form
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let
$(x_n)$ be a sequence in $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and let
$x \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. If $F(x_n) \to F(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for every
continuous linear functional $F : \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K}) \to \mathbb{K}$, then
$\|x_n - x\| \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Schur's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(x_n)$ be a sequence
in $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and let $x_0 \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. If
$F(x_n) \to F(x_0)$ for every continuous linear functional $F$ on $\ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$,
that is, if $(x_n)$ converges weakly to $x_0$, then $x_n \to x_0$ in the $\ell^1$ norm.

articles.title: The pairing of $\ell^1$ with sequences bounded by $1$ is summable
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be
$\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $y : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ satisfies $\|y_i\| \le 1$ for
every $i$ and $x \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, then the series $\sum_i y_i x_i$ is
summable.

articles.title: Tails of an $\ell^1$ sequence are absolutely summable
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $b \in \mathbb{N}$, the
series $\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \|x_{j+b}\|$ is summable.

articles.title: Tail of the norm series of an $\ell^1$ sequence
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or
$\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $b \in \mathbb{N}$,
$\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \|x_{j+b}\| = \|x\| - \sum_{i < b} \|x_i\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the $\ell^1$
norm of $x$.

articles.title: Splitting a series into a head, a middle block and a tail
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$
or $\mathbb{C}$, let $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be summable and let $a \le b$ be natural
numbers. Then $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} h(i)$ equals
$\sum_{i < a} h(i) + \sum_{a \le i < b} h(i) + \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} h(j + b)$.

articles.title: Separable real Banach spaces are quotients of ℓ¹
articles.statement:
For every separable real Banach space $E$
there is a surjective bounded linear operator $T \colon \ell^1(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{R}) \to E$.

## Sources

- S. Banach, Theorie des operations lineaires, 1932, `ℓ¹` quotient theorem; Albiac and Kalton, Topics in Banach Space Theory; Lean states separable real Banach specialization with concrete `lp _ 1` domain and surjective bounded linear quotient.

articles.title: Mazur's Problem 65 has a negative answer
articles.statement:
The symmetric hull claim of Scottish Book
Problem 65 is false: there are a real Banach space $E$ and a convex set $W \subseteq E$ with
$0 \in W$ whose closure has empty interior, such that the closure of the convex hull of
$W \cup (-W)$ has nonempty interior.

## Sources

- S. Mazur, Problem 65 of the Scottish Book; typescript Ad 65 records the negative answer, with the counterexample of the set `W` of non-decreasing functions in the space `(C)` of continuous functions: `W` is convex, nowhere dense, and contains `0`, while the symmetric convex set containing `W` contains all functions of bounded variation and is not nowhere dense (indeed, it is dense, since it contains the polynomials). For this `W` (a cone) the `W ∪ -W` hull and the difference-set construction coincide, so the counterexample refutes the corrected claim too.

articles.title: Mazur's symmetric hull claim (Scottish Book Problem 65)
articles.statement:
The claim that for every real
Banach space $E$ and every convex set $W \subseteq E$ with $0 \in W$, if the closure of $W$ has
empty interior (that is, $W$ is nowhere dense), then the closure of the convex hull of
$W \cup (-W)$ also has empty interior. The convex hull of $W \cup (-W)$ is the smallest convex
set containing $W$ that is symmetric about the origin.

The typescript's parenthetical identifies this set with the difference set $W - W$, which is
larger in general; the smallest-set reading is adopted here. For the Ad 65 counterexample $W$
(non-decreasing functions, a cone) the two constructions coincide, so the counterexample still
applies.

articles.title: Bergman coefficients as inner products with monomials
articles.statement: The coefficient of `a` at `n` is the inner product with `eₙ`.

articles.title: Bergman kernel evaluated at its own point
articles.statement:
Evaluation of the kernel at its own point: `f_z(k_z) = (1 - ‖z‖²)⁻¹ ^ 2`,
so the pointwise bound is sharp.

articles.title: Bergman point evaluation is the inner product with the kernel
articles.statement:
The bounded point-evaluation functional acts by the inner product
with the Bergman kernel.

articles.title: Bounded point-evaluation functional on the Bergman space
articles.statement: Point evaluation as a bounded linear functional on `A²(𝔻)`.

articles.title: Bergman point evaluation as a Taylor series
articles.statement: Point evaluation is the Taylor series `∑' n, a n * √(n + 1) * zⁿ`.

articles.title: Bergman evaluation of a monomial
articles.statement: Evaluation of a monomial `c * √(n + 1) * zⁿ` (a single coefficient).

articles.title: Bergman evaluation at the origin
articles.statement: Evaluation at `0` is the constant Taylor coefficient.

articles.title: Point evaluation on the Bergman space
articles.statement: Point evaluation on `A²(𝔻)`: the inner product with the Bergman kernel.

articles.title: Bergman kernel at the origin
articles.statement: The Bergman kernel at `0` is the first standard basis vector.

articles.title: Bergman kernel
articles.statement:
The **Bergman kernel** at `z`: the `ℓ²(ℕ, ℂ)` sequence with
coefficients `√(n + 1) * (conj z)ⁿ`.

articles.title: Inner products of rescaled Bergman monomials are Kronecker deltas
articles.statement:
The coordinate inner products of the rescaled monomials equal the
Kronecker delta.

articles.title: Rescaled Bergman monomial
articles.statement:
The rescaled monomial `eₙ(z) = √(n + 1) zⁿ` for normalized area
measure `dA / π`, represented by the `n`th standard basis vector in the
coefficient model.

articles.title: Bergman space $A^2$ of the unit disc
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ belongs to
the Bergman space $A^2$ when it is analytic on the open unit disc
$\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ and square-integrable on $\mathbb{D}$ with respect to
Lebesgue area measure $dA$: $f$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable on $\mathbb{D}$ and
$\int_{\mathbb{D}} |f|^2 \, dA < \infty$.

articles.title: Invertible non-cyclic functions in the Bergman space $A^2$
articles.statement:
Write $\mathbb{D}$ for the open
unit disc and $dA$ for Lebesgue area measure on it. There is a function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with no zeros in $\mathbb{D}$ such that $f$ and its pointwise
reciprocal $1/f$ both belong to the Bergman space $A^2$, but the polynomial multiples of $f$ are
not dense in $A^2$: there are $g \in A^2$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ with
$\left(\int_{\mathbb{D}} |p f - g|^2 \, dA\right)^{1/2} \ge \varepsilon$ for every complex
polynomial $p$. That is, the Bergman cyclicity conjecture is false.

Borichev and Hedenmalm (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 10 (1997) 761-796) constructed invertible but
non-cyclic functions in the unweighted Bergman spaces $B^p(\mathbb{D})$, $0 < p < \infty$; the case
$p = 2$ gives such an $f$, as stated in Borichev-Hedenmalm-Volberg (arXiv:math/0304318).

## Sources

- Alexander Borichev, Haakan Hedenmalm and Alexander Volberg, Large Bergman spaces: invertibility, cyclicity, and subspaces of arbitrary index, arXiv:math/0304318 (2003), https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0304318.

articles.title: Bergman cyclicity conjecture
articles.statement:
Write $\mathbb{D}$ for the open unit disc and $dA$ for
Lebesgue area measure on it. The statement that for every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
with no zeros in $\mathbb{D}$ such that $f$ and its pointwise reciprocal $1/f$ both belong to the
Bergman space $A^2$, the polynomial multiples of $f$ are dense in $A^2$: for every $g \in A^2$ and
every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a complex polynomial $p$ with
$\left(\int_{\mathbb{D}} |p f - g|^2 \, dA\right)^{1/2} < \varepsilon$.

## Sources

- record `AMR-022-8010`; the record's generalization to other spaces is not part of this statement.

articles.title: Density of polynomial multiples in $A^2$
articles.statement:
Write $\mathbb{D}$ for the open unit disc and
$dA$ for Lebesgue area measure on it. For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, the statement
that the polynomial multiples of $f$ are dense in the Bergman space $A^2$: for every $g \in A^2$
and every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a complex polynomial $p$ with
$\left(\int_{\mathbb{D}} |p f - g|^2 \, dA\right)^{1/2} < \varepsilon$.

articles.title: The open unit disc
articles.statement: The set $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$.

articles.title: Square of the complex geometric series
articles.statement:
The Cauchy product of the geometric series with itself: the series
`∑' n, (n + 1) * qⁿ` sums to `(1 - q)⁻¹ ^ 2`.

articles.title: Square of the real geometric series
articles.statement: The real form of the Cauchy product above.

articles.title: Inner product of two Bergman kernels
articles.statement:
The inner product of two Bergman kernels is the Bergman kernel function
`(1 - z * conj w)⁻¹ ^ 2`.

articles.title: Reproducing property of the Bergman kernel, conjugate form
articles.statement: The reproducing property in the other order: `⟪a, k_z⟫ = conj (f(z))`.

articles.title: Pointwise reciprocal
articles.statement:
For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, the function
$z \mapsto f(z)^{-1}$, with the convention $0^{-1} = 0$ at the zeros of $f$.

articles.title: Bergman kernel coefficients are square-summable
articles.statement: The Bergman kernel coefficients are in `ℓ²` when `z` is in the disc.

articles.title: Operator norm of Bergman point evaluation
articles.statement: The operator norm of point evaluation is `1 / (1 - ‖z‖²)`.

articles.title: Pointwise bound for Bergman space functions
articles.statement: The pointwise bound for `A²` functions: `‖f(z)‖ ≤ ‖f‖ / (1 - ‖z‖²)`.

articles.title: Norm of the Bergman kernel
articles.statement: The norm of the Bergman kernel is `1 / (1 - ‖z‖²)`.

articles.title: Squared norms of the Bergman kernel coefficients
articles.statement:
The squared norms of the Bergman kernel coefficients are
`(n + 1) * ‖z‖ ^ (2 * n)`.

articles.title: Squared norm of the Bergman kernel
articles.statement: The squared norm of the Bergman kernel is `1 / (1 - ‖z‖²)²`.

articles.title: Rescaled Bergman monomials are orthonormal
articles.statement:
The rescaled monomial family satisfies Mathlib's standard orthonormal
predicate.

articles.title: Convergence of the Taylor series of a Bergman space function
articles.statement:
The Taylor series of an `A²` function converges at every
point of the disc.

articles.title: Polynomial density passes to dominating functions in the Dirichlet space
articles.statement:
For all $f$ and $g$
in the Dirichlet space $\mathcal{D}$: if the polynomial multiples $Pg$ are dense in $\mathcal{D}$
in the Dirichlet norm and $|g(z)| \le |f(z)|$ for all $|z| < 1$, then the polynomial multiples
$Pf$ are dense in $\mathcal{D}$ in the Dirichlet norm. This answers Hayman's Problem 8.11
positively.

Resolved true: Richter and Sundberg (Michigan Math. J. 38 (1991) 355-379), and independently
Aleman, proved that in Dirichlet-type spaces $\mathcal{D}(\mu)$, including the classical Dirichlet
space, $|g| \le |f|$ with $g$ cyclic implies $f$ cyclic, where $g$ is cyclic when $Pg$ is dense
(restated in arXiv:2406.06182, Thm 5.12).

## Sources

- Emmanuel Fricain and Romain Lebreton, Cyclicity of the shift operator through Bezout identities, arXiv:2406.06182 (2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06182.

articles.title: Hayman's Problem 8.11: polynomial density under domination
articles.statement:
The statement that for all
$f$ and $g$ in the Dirichlet space $\mathcal{D}$: if the polynomial multiples $Pg$ are dense in
$\mathcal{D}$ in the Dirichlet norm and $|g(z)| \le |f(z)|$ for all $|z| < 1$, then the
polynomial multiples $Pf$ are also dense in $\mathcal{D}$ in the Dirichlet norm.

## Sources

- the open question of `AMR-022-8011` (Hayman, Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 8.11, https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200).

articles.title: Reproducing property of the Dirichlet kernel
articles.statement:
The bounded point-evaluation functional acts by the inner product
with the Dirichlet kernel.

articles.title: Point evaluation as a bounded functional on the Dirichlet space
articles.statement: Point evaluation as a bounded linear functional on `𝒟(𝔻)`.

articles.title: Sharpness of the Dirichlet-space pointwise bound
articles.statement:
Evaluation of the kernel at its own point, in closed form:
`f_z(k_z) = -log (1 - ‖z‖²) / ‖z‖²`, so the pointwise bound is sharp.

articles.title: Dirichlet kernel evaluated at its own point
articles.statement: Evaluation of the kernel at its own point: `f_z(k_z) = ‖k_z‖²`.

articles.title: Dirichlet-space point evaluation as a Taylor series
articles.statement: Point evaluation is the Taylor series `∑' n, a n * zⁿ / √(n + 1)`.

articles.title: Dirichlet-space evaluation of a single monomial
articles.statement: Evaluation of a monomial `c * zⁿ / √(n + 1)` (a single coefficient).

articles.title: Dirichlet-space evaluation at the origin is the constant coefficient
articles.statement: Evaluation at `0` is the constant Taylor coefficient.

articles.title: Point evaluation on the Dirichlet space
articles.statement: Point evaluation on `𝒟(𝔻)`: the inner product with the Dirichlet kernel.

articles.title: Dirichlet kernel at the origin is the first basis vector
articles.statement: The Dirichlet kernel at `0` is the first standard basis vector.

articles.title: Reproducing kernel of the Dirichlet space
articles.statement:
The **Dirichlet kernel** at `z`: the `ℓ²(ℕ, ℂ)` sequence with
coefficients `(conj z)ⁿ / √(n + 1)`.

articles.title: The Dirichlet space
articles.statement:
The Dirichlet space $\mathcal{D}$ consists of the functions
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that are analytic on the open unit disc $\{z : |z| < 1\}$ and have
finite Dirichlet integral: $|f'|^2$ is integrable on the disc with respect to Lebesgue (area)
measure. The values of $f$ outside the disc are unconstrained.

## Sources

- `AMR-022-8011` (Hayman, Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 8.11, https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200).

articles.title: Closed form of $\sum u^n/(n+1)$ for complex $u$ in the unit disc
articles.statement:
The complex form: `∑' n, uⁿ / (n + 1)` sums to `-log (1 - u) / u`
for `u ≠ 0` in the unit disc.

articles.title: Closed form of $\sum r^n/(n+1)$ for real $0<r<1$
articles.statement:
**Closed form of $\sum r^n/(n+1)$ for real $0\lt r<1$.** The power series `∑' n, rⁿ / (n + 1)` sums to `-log (1 - r) / r`
for `0 < r < 1`: factor `1 / r` out of the logarithm series.

articles.title: Logarithmic formula for the inner product of Dirichlet kernels
articles.statement:
The inner product of two Dirichlet kernels is the Dirichlet kernel
function `-log (1 - z * conj w) / (z * conj w)`.

articles.title: Inner product of two Dirichlet kernels as a power series
articles.statement:
The inner product of two Dirichlet kernels is the power series
`∑' n, (z * conj w)ⁿ / (n + 1)`.

articles.title: Conjugate reproducing property of the Dirichlet kernel
articles.statement: The reproducing property in the other order: `⟪a, k_z⟫ = conj (f(z))`.

articles.title: Density in the Dirichlet norm
articles.statement:
A set $S$ of elements of the Dirichlet space $\mathcal{D}$
is dense in the Dirichlet norm when for every $u \in \mathcal{D}$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$
there is $h \in S$ with

$$|h(0) - u(0)|^2 + \int_{|z| < 1} |h'(z) - u'(z)|^2 \, dA(z) < \varepsilon,$$

where $A$ is Lebesgue (area) measure on $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Dirichlet kernel coefficients lie in ℓ²
articles.statement: The Dirichlet kernel coefficients are in `ℓ²` when `z` is in the disc.

articles.title: Closed-form norm of Dirichlet-space point evaluation
articles.statement: The operator norm of point evaluation is `√(-log (1 - ‖z‖²) / ‖z‖²)`.

articles.title: Norm of Dirichlet-space point evaluation at the origin
articles.statement: The operator norm of point evaluation at `0` is `1`.

articles.title: Norm of Dirichlet-space point evaluation equals the kernel norm
articles.statement: The operator norm of point evaluation is the norm of the kernel.

articles.title: Pointwise bound for Dirichlet-space functions
articles.statement: The pointwise bound for `𝒟` functions: `‖f(z)‖ ≤ ‖f‖ * ‖k_z‖`.

articles.title: Norm of the Dirichlet kernel away from the origin
articles.statement: The norm of the Dirichlet kernel is `√(-log (1 - ‖z‖²) / ‖z‖²)`.

articles.title: Norm of the Dirichlet kernel at the origin
articles.statement: The norm of the Dirichlet kernel at `0` is `1`.

articles.title: Squared norms of the Dirichlet kernel coefficients
articles.statement:
The squared norms of the Dirichlet kernel coefficients are
`‖z‖ ^ (2 * n) / (n + 1)`.

articles.title: Dirichlet kernel norm is bounded by the Szegő kernel norm
articles.statement:
The Dirichlet kernel norm is bounded by the Hardy kernel norm:
`‖k_z‖² ≤ 1 / (1 - ‖z‖²)`, via `log x ≤ x - 1` at `x = (1 - ‖z‖²)⁻¹`.

articles.title: Squared norm of the Dirichlet kernel away from the origin
articles.statement: The squared norm of the Dirichlet kernel is `-log (1 - ‖z‖²) / ‖z‖²`.

articles.title: Squared norm of the Dirichlet kernel at the origin
articles.statement: The squared norm of the Dirichlet kernel at `0` is `1`.

articles.title: Polynomial multiples of a function in the Dirichlet space
articles.statement:
For $g$ in the Dirichlet
space $\mathcal{D}$, the set $Pg$ consists of the functions $h \in \mathcal{D}$ for which there is
a polynomial $p$ with complex coefficients such that $h(z) = p(z) g(z)$ for all $|z| < 1$; only
values on the open unit disc are compared.

## Sources

- `AMR-022-8011` (Hayman, Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 8.11, with $Pg$ as defined in Problem 8.10), https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Absolute convergence of Taylor series in the Dirichlet space
articles.statement:
The Taylor series of a `𝒟` function converges absolutely at every
point of the disc.

articles.title: Square-summability of the Dirichlet kernel coefficients
articles.statement:
The Dirichlet kernel coefficients are summable in the `ℓ²` sense:
`∑' n, (‖z‖²)ⁿ / (n + 1)` converges, by comparison with the geometric series.

articles.title: Fatou's theorem on radial limits
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic and
bounded on the open unit disc $|z| < 1$. Then for Lebesgue-almost every $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ the
radial limit $\lim_{r \to 1^-} f(r e^{i\theta})$ exists in $\mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- Fatou radial limit theorem for H∞, P. Fatou, Acta Math. 30 (1906); see Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis, Bounded Analytic Functions; Lean is bounded holomorphic on ball 0 1 with a.e. radial limit via volume.restrict Icc 0 (2π) and 𝓝[<] 1.

articles.title: The open unit disc
articles.statement:
The open unit disc
$\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, the open ball of radius $1$ about $0$ in
$\mathbb{C}$, taken as a space in its own right whose points are the points of the disc.

articles.title: The ring $H^\infty$ as a subring of functions on the disc
articles.statement:
$H^\infty$ is the subring of
the ring of all complex-valued functions on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D}$, under pointwise
addition and multiplication, consisting of the functions that belong to $H^\infty$: those that
agree on $\mathbb{D}$ with a function $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ complex differentiable on
$\mathbb{D}$ and are bounded on $\mathbb{D}$.

## Sources

- [AMR-022-5024], Research Problems in Function Theory, Problem 5.24.

articles.title: Elements of $H^\infty$
articles.statement:
The space whose points are the members of the subring $H^\infty$
of complex-valued functions on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D}$, that is, the bounded functions
on $\mathbb{D}$ that agree on $\mathbb{D}$ with a function complex differentiable there.

## Sources

- [AMR-022-5024], Research Problems in Function Theory, Problem 5.24.

articles.title: Membership in $H^\infty$ of the unit disc
articles.statement:
A complex-valued function $f$ on the open unit
disc $\mathbb{D}$ belongs to $H^\infty$ when there is a function $F : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
that is complex differentiable on $\mathbb{D}$ and satisfies $f(z) = F(z)$ for every
$z \in \mathbb{D}$, and there is a real number $C \ge 0$ with $|f(z)| \le C$ for every
$z \in \mathbb{D}$.

## Sources

- [AMR-022-5024], Research Problems in Function Theory, Problem 5.24.

articles.title: McVoy–Rubel theorem on finitely generated ideals of $H^\infty$
articles.statement:
For any two finitely
generated ideals $I$ and $J$ of the commutative ring $H^\infty$ of bounded holomorphic functions
on the open unit disc, the intersection $I \cap J$ is finitely generated. This answers Rubel's
Problem 5.24 positively.

Resolved by McVoy and Rubel (J. Funct. Anal. 21 (1976) 76-87), who proved that $H^\infty$ of the
unit disc is a coherent ring. Restated in Mortini, arXiv:1606.05568, and Hayman-Lingham
Update 5.24.

## Sources

- R. Mortini, Noncoherent uniform algebras in C^n (2016), arXiv:1606.05568, https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.05568.

articles.title: Rubel's problem on intersections of finitely generated ideals in $H^\infty$
articles.statement:
The
statement that for any two finitely generated ideals $I$ and $J$ of the commutative ring
$H^\infty$ of bounded holomorphic functions on the open unit disc, the intersection $I \cap J$ is
finitely generated.

Rubel asked whether this statement is true.

## Sources

- [AMR-022-5024], Research Problems in Function Theory, Problem 5.24 (L. A. Rubel).

articles.title: Fock coefficients as inner products with normalized monomials
articles.statement: The coefficient of `a` at `n` is the inner product with `eₙ`.

articles.title: Coherent state in the Fock space
articles.statement:
The **coherent state** at `z`: the normalized Fock kernel,
`ĉ_z = Real.exp (-‖z‖² / 2) • k_z`.

articles.title: Reproducing property of the Fock kernel
articles.statement:
The bounded point-evaluation functional acts by the inner product
with the Fock kernel.

articles.title: Point evaluation as a bounded functional on the Fock space
articles.statement: Point evaluation as a bounded linear functional on the Fock space.

articles.title: Fock-space point evaluation as a Taylor series
articles.statement: Point evaluation is the Taylor series `∑' n, a n * zⁿ / √(n!)`.

articles.title: Fock kernel evaluated at its own point
articles.statement:
Evaluation of the kernel at its own point: `f_z(k_z) = Real.exp ‖z‖²`,
so the pointwise bound is sharp.

articles.title: Fock-space evaluation of a single monomial
articles.statement:
Evaluation of a monomial `c * zⁿ / √(n!)` (a single Taylor
coefficient).

articles.title: Fock-space evaluation at the origin is the constant coefficient
articles.statement: Evaluation at `0` is the constant Taylor coefficient.

articles.title: Point evaluation on the Fock space
articles.statement:
Point evaluation on the Fock space: the inner product with the
Fock kernel.

articles.title: Fock kernel at the origin is the first basis vector
articles.statement: The Fock kernel at `0` is the first standard basis vector.

articles.title: Reproducing kernel of the Fock space
articles.statement:
The **Fock kernel** at `z`: the `ℓ²(ℕ, ℂ)` sequence with coefficients
`(conj z)ⁿ / √(n!)`.

articles.title: Normalized Fock monomials are orthonormal standard basis vectors
articles.statement:
The rescaled monomials `eₙ(z) = zⁿ / √(n!)`, i.e. the standard basis
vectors of the coefficient model, are orthonormal.

articles.title: Normalized monomials in the Fock space
articles.statement:
The normalized monomial `eₙ(z) = zⁿ / √(n!)`, represented by the `n`th
standard basis vector in the Taylor-coefficient model of Fock space.

articles.title: Inner product of two coherent states
articles.statement: The inner product of two coherent states.

articles.title: Inner product of two Fock kernels is an exponential
articles.statement:
The inner product of two Fock kernels is the Fock kernel function
`Complex.exp (z * conj w)`.

articles.title: Conjugate reproducing property of the Fock kernel
articles.statement: The reproducing property in the other order: `⟪a, k_z⟫ = conj (f(z))`.

articles.title: Fock kernel coefficients lie in ℓ²
articles.statement:
The Fock kernel coefficients are in `ℓ²` for every `z : ℂ`, since
`∑' n, ‖z‖ ^ (2 * n) / n! = Real.exp ‖z‖²`.

articles.title: Coherent states are unit vectors
articles.statement: Coherent states are unit vectors.

articles.title: Norm of Fock-space point evaluation
articles.statement: The operator norm of point evaluation is `Real.exp (‖z‖² / 2)`.

articles.title: Pointwise bound for Fock-space functions
articles.statement:
The pointwise bound for Fock-space functions:
`‖f(z)‖ ≤ ‖f‖ * Real.exp (‖z‖² / 2)`.

articles.title: Norm of the Fock kernel
articles.statement: The norm of the Fock kernel is `Real.exp (‖z‖² / 2)`.

articles.title: Gaussian overlap of coherent states
articles.statement:
The overlap of two coherent states is Gaussian:
`‖⟪ĉ_z, ĉ_w⟫‖ = Real.exp (-‖z - w‖² / 2)`.

articles.title: Modulus of the inner product of two Fock kernels
articles.statement:
The norm of the inner product of two Fock kernels is
`Real.exp (z * conj w).re`.

articles.title: Squared norms of the Fock kernel coefficients
articles.statement:
The squared norms of the Fock kernel coefficients are
`‖z‖ ^ (2 * n) / n!`.

articles.title: Squared norm of the Fock kernel
articles.statement: The squared norm of the Fock kernel is `Real.exp ‖z‖²`.

articles.title: Normalized Fock monomials form an orthonormal family
articles.statement: The normalized monomial family satisfies Mathlib's standard orthonormal predicate.

articles.title: Absolute convergence of Taylor series in the Fock space
articles.statement:
The Taylor series of a Fock-space function converges absolutely at
every point of `ℂ`.

articles.title: Taylor coefficients of a Hardy-space function are bounded by its norm
articles.statement:
Taylor coefficients of an `H²` function are bounded by its norm: a
single squared coefficient is at most the sum of all of them.

articles.title: Newman's theorem: no bounded projection onto the Hardy space
articles.statement:
Let $L^1(\mathbb{T})$ be
the space of integrable complex functions on the circle $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ with
its normalized Haar measure, and let $H^1 \subseteq L^1(\mathbb{T})$ be the boundary Hardy space.
There is no continuous $\mathbb{C}$-linear map $\pi : L^1(\mathbb{T}) \to H^1$ with $\pi(f) = f$
for every $f \in H^1$.

## Sources

- D. J. Newman, 'The nonexistence of projections from L^1 to H^1', Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.; W. Rudin, Fourier Analysis on Groups; Yongxi Lin, Hardy Space and Hartogs Triangle, Theorem 2.8. Problem `H1_not_closedComplemented` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The boundary Hardy space H¹
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ carry its Haar
measure normalized to total mass $1$. The Hardy space $H^1$ is the complex linear subspace of
$L^1(\mathbb{T})$ consisting of those $f$ whose Fourier coefficients
$\hat f(n) = \int_{\mathbb{T}} f(t) e^{-2\pi i n t} dt$ vanish for all integers $n < 0$.

articles.title: Reproducing property of the Szegő kernel
articles.statement:
The bounded point-evaluation functional acts by the inner product
with the Szegő kernel.

articles.title: Point evaluation as a bounded functional on the Hardy space
articles.statement: Point evaluation as a bounded linear functional on `H²(𝔻)`.

articles.title: Hardy-space point evaluation as a Taylor series
articles.statement: Point evaluation is the Taylor series `∑' n, a n * zⁿ`.

articles.title: Hardy-space evaluation of a single monomial
articles.statement: Evaluation of a monomial `c * zⁿ` (a single Taylor coefficient).

articles.title: Hardy-space evaluation at the origin is the constant coefficient
articles.statement: Evaluation at `0` is the constant Taylor coefficient.

articles.title: Point evaluation on the Hardy space
articles.statement: Point evaluation on `H²(𝔻)`: the inner product with the Szegő kernel.

articles.title: Conjugate reproducing property of the Szegő kernel
articles.statement: The reproducing property in the other order: `⟪a, k_z⟫ = conj (f(z))`.

articles.title: Inner product of two Szegő kernels
articles.statement:
The inner product of two Szegő kernels is the Szegő kernel function
`1 / (1 - z * conj w)`.

articles.title: Szegő kernel coefficients lie in ℓ²
articles.statement: The Szegő kernel coefficients are in `ℓ²` when `z` is in the disc.

articles.title: Norm of Hardy-space point evaluation
articles.statement: The operator norm of point evaluation is `1 / √(1 - ‖z‖²)`.

articles.title: Pointwise bound for Hardy-space functions
articles.statement: The pointwise bound for `H²` functions: `‖f(z)‖ ≤ ‖f‖ / √(1 - ‖z‖²)`.

articles.title: Squared norms of the Szegő kernel coefficients
articles.statement:
The squared norms of the Szegő kernel coefficients form a geometric
progression with ratio `‖z‖²`.

articles.title: Squared norm of the Szegő kernel
articles.statement: The squared norm of the Szegő kernel is `1 / (1 - ‖z‖²)`.

articles.title: Norm of the Szegő kernel
articles.statement: The norm of the Szegő kernel is `1 / √(1 - ‖z‖²)`.

articles.title: Absolute convergence of Taylor series in the Hardy space
articles.statement:
The Taylor series of an `H²` function converges absolutely at every
point of the disc.

articles.title: Szegő kernel at the origin is the first basis vector
articles.statement: The Szegő kernel at `0` is the first standard basis vector.

articles.title: Szegő kernel of the Hardy space
articles.statement:
The **Szegő kernel** at `z`: the `ℓ²(ℕ, ℂ)` sequence with
coefficients `(conj z)ⁿ`.

articles.title: Regularity of a lacunary series on the unit disc
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be the lacunary series
$f(z) = \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-j} z^{2^j}$. Then $f$ is holomorphic on the open unit disc
$\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ and continuous on its closure, the closed unit disc
$\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1\}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; Series expansions of functions of one complex variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_09`.

articles.title: A lacunary power series
articles.statement:
For $z \in \mathbb{C}$, let
$f(z) = \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-j} z^{2^j}$, where $f(z)$ is taken to be $0$ when the series is
not summable.

articles.title: F. and M. Riesz theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a complex Borel measure on the circle
$\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. If $\int_{\mathbb{T}} e^{2\pi i n z} \, d\mu(z) = 0$ for
every integer $n \ge 1$, then $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Haar probability
measure on $\mathbb{T}$.

## Sources

- W. Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis; N. K. Nikolski, Operators, Functions, and Systems: An Easy Reading, Volume I: Hardy, Hankel, and Toeplitz. Problem `riesz_brothers_theorem` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Argument principle on a closed disc
articles.statement:
Let $c \in \mathbb{C}$, $R > 0$, and let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be meromorphic on the closed disc $|z - c| \le R$ with finite order
at every point of that disc (so $f$ vanishes identically near no point). Suppose the order of $f$
is zero at every point of the circle $|z - c| = R$. Then the integral of $f'/f$ over the circle
$|z - c| = R$, traversed once counterclockwise, equals $2\pi i$ times the sum of the orders of $f$
at the points of the open disc $|z - c| < R$ (zeros counted positively and poles negatively, with
multiplicity).

articles.title: Argument principle on a closed disc, with an integrability hypothesis
articles.statement:
Let $c \in \mathbb{C}$,
$R > 0$, and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be meromorphic on the closed disc $|z - c| \le R$
with finite order at every point of that disc. Suppose the order of $f$ is zero at every point of
the circle $|z - c| = R$ and $f'/f$ is integrable on that circle. Then the integral of $f'/f$ over
the circle, traversed once counterclockwise, equals $2\pi i$ times the sum of the orders of $f$ at
the points of the open disc $|z - c| < R$ (zeros counted positively and poles negatively, with
multiplicity).

## Sources

- L. V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., §5.2. It follows from `argumentPrinciple_closedBall_general`; the hypothesis `hint` is unused and keeps the source's shape.

articles.title: Casorati–Weierstrass theorem
articles.statement:
Let $c \in \mathbb{C}$, $r > 0$, and let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on the punctured disc $0 < |z - c| < r$ and not
meromorphic at $c$ (that is, $c$ is neither a removable singularity nor a pole of $f$). Then the
image of the punctured disc $0 < |z - c| < r$ under $f$ is dense in $\mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- L. V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., isolated singularities.

articles.title: A holomorphic function with holomorphic conjugate is constant
articles.statement:
Let
$U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a connected open set and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be
holomorphic on $U$. If the conjugate function $z \mapsto \overline{f(z)}$ is also holomorphic on
$U$, then $f$ is constant on $U$: there is $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = c$ for all $z \in U$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; General properties of functions of one complex variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_04`.

articles.title: Complex conjugation is nowhere complex-differentiable
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
be the function $f(z) = \bar z$. Then $f$ is not complex-differentiable at any point
$z \in \mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; General properties of functions of one complex variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_57`.

articles.title: Fundamental theorem of contour integration
articles.statement:
Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open and let
$F, f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be such that $F$ is complex-differentiable at every $z \in U$
with $F'(z) = f(z)$. Let $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ be a path from $a$ to $b$ whose image
lies in $U$ and which is continuously differentiable on $[0, 1]$, with derivative $\gamma'$
(one-sided at the endpoints). If $t \mapsto f(\gamma(t))\,\gamma'(t)$ is integrable on $[0, 1]$,
then $\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz = F(b) - F(a)$, where
$\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz = \int_0^1 f(\gamma(t))\,\gamma'(t)\,dt$.

## Sources

- L. V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, §1.1 to §1.3 (line integrals).

articles.title: ML estimate for contour integrals
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and let
$\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ be a path from $a$ to $b$ which is continuously differentiable
on $[0, 1]$, with derivative $\gamma'$ (one-sided at the endpoints). Let $M$ and $L$ be real
numbers with $|f(\gamma(t))| \le M$ and $|\gamma'(t)| \le L$ for every $t \in [0, 1]$. If
$t \mapsto f(\gamma(t))\,\gamma'(t)$ is integrable on $[0, 1]$, then
$\left|\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz\right| \le ML$, where
$\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz = \int_0^1 f(\gamma(t))\,\gamma'(t)\,dt$.

The parameter interval has length one, so $L$ bounds the length of $\gamma$.

## Sources

- L. V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, §1.1 to §1.3 (line integrals).

articles.title: The reciprocal function has no antiderivative on an annulus
articles.statement:
Let
$U = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : 1 < |z| < 2\}$. There is no function $F : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
that is complex differentiable at every $z \in U$ with $F'(z) = 1/z$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; General properties of functions of one complex variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_67`.

articles.title: Cauchy–Goursat theorem for rectangles
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex Banach space, let $R$ be a
rectilinear rectangle and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$ be complex differentiable on the closed
rectangle spanned by the corners of $R$ (the carrier of $R$). Then the boundary integral of $f$
over $R$ is $0$.

articles.title: Cauchy kernel with the pole outside a rectangle
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a rectilinear rectangle and
let $w$ be a complex number that does not lie in the closed rectangle spanned by the corners of
$R$ (the carrier of $R$). Then the boundary integral of $z \mapsto 1/(z - w)$ over $R$ is $0$.

articles.title: Gluing rectangles along a horizontal side
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex Banach space, let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to E$ and let $x_0, x_1, y_0, y_1, y_2$ be real numbers such that the maps
$y \mapsto f(x_0 + iy)$ and $y \mapsto f(x_1 + iy)$ are continuous on $\mathbb{R}$. For real
$a, b, c, d$ write $R(a, b, c, d)$ for the rectangle with corners $a + ic$ and $b + id$. Then the
boundary integral of $f$ over $R(x_0, x_1, y_0, y_2)$ equals the sum of the boundary integrals of
$f$ over $R(x_0, x_1, y_0, y_1)$ and over $R(x_0, x_1, y_1, y_2)$.

No ordering of $y_0, y_1, y_2$ is assumed: the common horizontal side cancels and the vertical
integrals concatenate as oriented integrals.

articles.title: Rectangle integral of $1/z$ around the origin
articles.statement:
Let $a, b, T$ be real numbers with
$a < 0 < b$ and $T > 0$. Then the boundary integral of $z \mapsto 1/z$ over the rectangle with
corners $a - iT$ and $b + iT$ equals $2\pi i$.

articles.title: Rectangle integral of the Cauchy kernel at an interior point
articles.statement:
Let $x_0, x_1, y_0, y_1$ be
real numbers and let $w$ be a complex number with $x_0 < \operatorname{Re} w < x_1$ and
$y_0 < \operatorname{Im} w < y_1$. Then the boundary integral of $z \mapsto 1/(z - w)$ over the
rectangle with corners $x_0 + iy_0$ and $x_1 + iy_1$ equals $2\pi i$.

articles.title: Translating the Cauchy kernel to the origin
articles.statement:
For all real numbers $x_0, x_1, y_0, y_1$ and
every complex number $w$, the boundary integral of $z \mapsto 1/(z - w)$ over the rectangle with
corners $x_0 + iy_0$ and $x_1 + iy_1$ equals the boundary integral of $z \mapsto 1/z$ over the
rectangle with corners $(x_0 - \operatorname{Re} w) + i(y_0 - \operatorname{Im} w)$ and
$(x_1 - \operatorname{Re} w) + i(y_1 - \operatorname{Im} w)$.

articles.title: Gluing rectangles along a vertical side
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex Banach space, let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to E$ and let $x_0, x_1, x_2, y_0, y_1$ be real numbers such that the maps
$x \mapsto f(x + iy_0)$ and $x \mapsto f(x + iy_1)$ are continuous on $\mathbb{R}$. For real
$a, b, c, d$ write $R(a, b, c, d)$ for the rectangle with corners $a + ic$ and $b + id$. Then the
boundary integral of $f$ over $R(x_0, x_2, y_0, y_1)$ equals the sum of the boundary integrals of
$f$ over $R(x_0, x_1, y_0, y_1)$ and over $R(x_1, x_2, y_0, y_1)$.

No ordering of $x_0, x_1, x_2$ is assumed: the common vertical side cancels and the horizontal
integrals concatenate as oriented integrals.

articles.title: Boundary integral over a rectangle
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex Banach space and let $R$ be a
rectilinear rectangle with first corner $z$ and second corner $w$. The boundary integral of a
function $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$ over $R$ is

$$\int_{\operatorname{Re} z}^{\operatorname{Re} w} f(x + i \operatorname{Im} z)\,dx -
\int_{\operatorname{Re} z}^{\operatorname{Re} w} f(x + i \operatorname{Im} w)\,dx +
i \int_{\operatorname{Im} z}^{\operatorname{Im} w} f(\operatorname{Re} w + iy)\,dy -
i \int_{\operatorname{Im} z}^{\operatorname{Im} w} f(\operatorname{Re} z + iy)\,dy,$$

where each integral is an oriented Bochner interval integral, so $\int_a^b = -\int_b^a$.

The corner order determines the sign; when $\operatorname{Re} z \le \operatorname{Re} w$ and
$\operatorname{Im} z \le \operatorname{Im} w$ this is the integral of $f$ over the positively
oriented boundary of the rectangle.

articles.title: Rectangle integral of $1/s$ with the pole outside
articles.statement:
Let $a, b, T$ be real numbers with
$0 < a \le b$ and $T > 0$. Then

$$\int_a^b \frac{dx}{x - iT} - \int_a^b \frac{dx}{x + iT} +
i \left( \int_{-T}^{T} \frac{dy}{b + iy} - \int_{-T}^{T} \frac{dy}{a + iy} \right) = 0,$$

that is, the integral of $1/s$ over the positively oriented boundary of the rectangle with
corners $a - iT$ and $b + iT$ vanishes.

articles.title: Rectangle integral of $1/s$ around the origin
articles.statement:
Let $a, b, T$ be real numbers with
$a < 0 < b$ and $T > 0$. Then

$$\int_a^b \frac{dx}{x - iT} - \int_a^b \frac{dx}{x + iT} +
i \left( \int_{-T}^{T} \frac{dy}{b + iy} - \int_{-T}^{T} \frac{dy}{a + iy} \right) = 2\pi i,$$

that is, the integral of $1/s$ over the positively oriented boundary of the rectangle with
corners $a - iT$ and $b + iT$ equals $2\pi i$.

articles.title: Carrier of an axis-parallel rectangle
articles.statement:
For an axis-parallel rectangle with opposite
corners $z$ and $w$, its carrier is the closed rectangle of all $u \in \mathbb{C}$ such that
$\operatorname{Re} u$ lies in the closed interval with endpoints $\operatorname{Re} z$ and
$\operatorname{Re} w$, and $\operatorname{Im} u$ lies in the closed interval with endpoints
$\operatorname{Im} z$ and $\operatorname{Im} w$.

articles.title: Rectangle filling supported in a set
articles.statement:
Let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. A rectilinear cycle
$\Gamma$, read as a filling by rectangles, is supported in $G$ when, for every rectangle $r$ whose
coefficient in $\Gamma$ is nonzero, the closed carrier of $r$ is contained in $G$.

articles.title: Rectilinear cycles homologous in a set
articles.statement:
Let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. Two rectilinear
cycles $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are homologous in $G$ when the rectangle filling of
$\Gamma - \Lambda$ is supported in $G$: every rectangle with nonzero coefficient in
$\Gamma - \Lambda$ has its closed carrier contained in $G$.

articles.title: Difference of horizontal integrals of the reciprocal
articles.statement:
Let $a \le b$ and $T \ne 0$ be
real numbers. Then
$\int_a^b \frac{dx}{x - iT} - \int_a^b \frac{dx}{x + iT}
= 2i\left(\arctan\frac{b}{T} - \arctan\frac{a}{T}\right)$.

articles.title: Index of a rectilinear cycle
articles.statement:
For a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$ and a point
$w \in \mathbb{C}$, the index of $\Gamma$ about $w$ is
$\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma \frac{dz}{z - w}$, the contour integral over $\Gamma$ of
$z \mapsto (z - w)^{-1}$, multiplied by $(2\pi i)^{-1}$.

With the conventions $0^{-1} = 0$ and that a non-integrable integral is $0$, the formula also
has a value when $w$ lies on the boundary of a rectangle occurring in $\Gamma$; no geometric
winding-number claim is made there.

articles.title: Winding index as an additive map
articles.statement:
For a fixed point $w \in \mathbb{C}$, the map sending a
rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$ to its index about $w$ is an additive group homomorphism from
rectilinear cycles to $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Rectangle index vanishes outside the rectangle
articles.statement:
For an axis-parallel rectangle $r$ and a
point $w \in \mathbb{C}$ outside the closed carrier of $r$, the index about $w$ of the cycle
consisting of the boundary of $r$ is $0$.

articles.title: Contour integration as an additive map
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex Banach space and
$f : \mathbb{C} \to E$. The map sending a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$ to the contour integral of
$f$ over $\Gamma$ is an additive group homomorphism from rectilinear cycles to $E$.

articles.title: Additivity of the contour integral in the cycle
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex Banach space and
$f : \mathbb{C} \to E$. For rectilinear cycles $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$, the contour integral of
$f$ over $\Gamma + \Lambda$ equals the integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ plus the integral of $f$
over $\Lambda$.

articles.title: Arctangent integral
articles.statement:
For real numbers $a$, $b$ and $d$ with $d \ne 0$,
$\int_a^b \frac{d}{x^2 + d^2}\,dx = \arctan\frac{b}{d} - \arctan\frac{a}{d}$.

articles.title: Homologous rectilinear cycles have equal integrals
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex Banach space,
let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$ be complex differentiable on $G$. If
$\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are rectilinear cycles that are homologous in $G$, that is, the closed
rectangle of every rectangle occurring in $\Gamma - \Lambda$ with nonzero coefficient is contained
in $G$, then the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ equals the contour integral of $f$ over
$\Lambda$.

articles.title: Cauchy–Goursat theorem for rectilinear cycles
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex Banach space, let
$G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$ be complex differentiable on $G$. If
$\Gamma$ is a rectilinear cycle whose rectangle filling is supported in $G$, that is, the closed
rectangle of every rectangle occurring in $\Gamma$ with nonzero coefficient is contained in $G$,
then the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ is $0$.

articles.title: Reversing a cycle negates its integral
articles.statement:
For every rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$, every
complex Banach space $E$ and every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$, the contour integral of $f$
over $-\Gamma$ is the negative of the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$.

articles.title: Integral over a difference of cycles
articles.statement:
For rectilinear cycles $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$, a
complex Banach space $E$ and a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$, the contour integral of $f$ over
$\Gamma - \Lambda$ equals the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ minus the contour integral of
$f$ over $\Lambda$.

articles.title: Contour integral over a rectilinear cycle
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex Banach space and
$f : \mathbb{C} \to E$. For a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$, a finite formal sum $\sum_r n_r\, r$ of
rectangles $r$ with integer coefficients $n_r$, the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ is
$\sum_r n_r \int_{\partial r} f$, where $\int_{\partial r} f$ is the boundary integral of $f$
over the oriented rectangle $r$.

articles.title: Integral of an odd function over a symmetric interval
articles.statement:
If $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$
satisfies $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for every real $x$, then $\int_{-T}^{T} f(x)\,dx = 0$ for every real
$T$.

articles.title: Rectangle with given coordinate bounds
articles.statement:
For real numbers $x_0, x_1, y_0, y_1$, this is the
rectilinear rectangle whose first corner is $x_0 + i y_0$ and whose second corner is
$x_1 + i y_1$.

articles.title: The cycle of a single rectangle
articles.statement:
For a rectilinear rectangle $r$, this is the rectilinear
cycle in which $r$ has coefficient $1$ and every other rectangle has coefficient $0$, that is, the
boundary of $r$ with the orientation given by its corner order.

articles.title: Rectilinear cycle
articles.statement:
A rectilinear cycle is a finitely supported function from rectilinear
rectangles to $\mathbb{Z}$, that is, a finite formal sum $\sum_r n_r\, r$ of rectilinear
rectangles $r$ with integer coefficients $n_r$, read as the corresponding integer combination of
oriented rectangle boundaries.

A negative coefficient reverses the orientation of the corresponding boundary.

articles.title: Rectilinear rectangle
articles.statement:
A rectilinear rectangle is an axis-parallel rectangle in the complex
plane, recorded by an ordered pair of complex numbers $z$ and $w$, its first and second corner,
which are opposite corners of the rectangle.

Degenerate rectangles, in which $z$ and $w$ have the same real part or the same imaginary part, are
allowed. The corners and their order determine the orientation of the boundary integral over the
rectangle, and the boundary integral over a degenerate rectangle is zero.

articles.title: Integral of $1/(c + iy)$ over a symmetric interval
articles.statement:
For real numbers $c \ne 0$ and
$T \ge 0$, $\int_{-T}^{T} \frac{1}{c + iy}\,dy = 2\arctan(T/c)$, where the integrand is complex
valued and the integral is taken over the real variable $y$.

articles.title: A holomorphic function not identically zero has finitely many zeros in a disc
articles.statement:
Let
$P \in \mathbb{C}$ and $r > 0$, write $D(P,r)$ for the open disc and $\overline{D}(P,r)$ for the
closed disc of center $P$ and radius $r$, and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic
on some open set containing $\overline{D}(P,r)$. If $f$ does not vanish identically on $D(P,r)$,
then $f$ has only finitely many zeros in $D(P,r)$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; General properties of functions of one complex variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_26`.

articles.title: Great Picard theorem
articles.statement:
Suppose $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has an essential isolated
singularity at $c \in \mathbb{C}$. Then there is at most one $w \in \mathbb{C}$ for which some
$r > 0$ makes the set $\{z : 0 < |z - c| < r,\ f(z) = w\}$ finite; that is, with at most one
exception, $f$ takes every complex value infinitely often on every punctured disc around $c$.

## Sources

- Great Picard theorem, E. Picard 1879; see Ahlfors, Complex Analysis; Lean is essential isolated singularity version with finite-fiber exceptional set subsingleton, at most one value finitely often near c.

articles.title: Essential isolated singularity
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has an
essential isolated singularity at $c \in \mathbb{C}$ when $f$ is holomorphic on some punctured
disc $0 < |z - c| < r$ with $r > 0$, $f(z)$ has no finite limit as $z \to c$ with $z \ne c$, and
$|f(z)|$ does not tend to $\infty$ as $z \to c$ with $z \ne c$.

articles.title: Classification of isolated singularities
articles.statement:
Let $c \in \mathbb{C}$, let $r > 0$, and let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on the punctured disc
$\{z \in \mathbb{C} : 0 < |z - c| < r\}$. Then at least one of the following holds: there is a
function $g$ holomorphic on the disc $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z - c| < r\}$ that agrees with $f$ on
the punctured disc (removable singularity); or $|f(z)| \to \infty$ as $z \to c$ with $z \ne c$
(pole); or for every $r' > 0$ the image under $f$ of the punctured disc
$\{z \in \mathbb{C} : 0 < |z - c| < r'\}$ is dense in $\mathbb{C}$ (essential singularity,
Casorati–Weierstrass).

## Sources

- L. V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, §3.1 and §3.2 (removable singularities; zeros, poles and the Casorati-Weierstrass theorem).

articles.title: Laurent expansion on an annulus
articles.statement:
Let $c \in \mathbb{C}$, let $r$ and $R$ be real numbers, and
let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on the annulus
$A = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : r < |z - c| < R\}$. Then there are coefficients $a_n \in \mathbb{C}$
for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that for every $z \in A$ the series
$\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a_n (z - c)^n$ is unconditionally summable with sum $f(z)$. Here
$0^n = 0$ for $n < 0$, which matters only at $z = c$ when $r < 0$.

## Sources

- L. V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., Ch. 5, §1.3 (the Laurent series).

articles.title: Looman–Menchoff theorem
articles.statement:
Let $s \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open and let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous on $s$. Write $u = \operatorname{Re} f$ and
$v = \operatorname{Im} f$ as functions of $z = x + iy$, and suppose that at every $z \in s$ the
partial derivatives $u_x(z)$, $u_y(z)$, $v_x(z)$, $v_y(z)$ exist and satisfy the Cauchy–Riemann
equations $u_x(z) = v_y(z)$ and $u_y(z) = -v_x(z)$. Then $f$ is complex differentiable on $s$.

Proof: Baire category gives a square with uniform axis-wise Lipschitz bounds on the
exceptional set. A Goursat rectangle estimate and Morera's theorem eliminate that set.

## Sources

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Looman%E2%80%93Menchoff_theorem (statement id `looman-menchoff-s1`, canonical name "Looman-Menchoff theorem").

articles.title: Locally uniformly bounded sequences are uniformly bounded on compact subsets
articles.statement:
Let
$(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is locally
uniformly bounded on $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. Then for every compact set $K \subseteq U$ there is
a real $C \ge 0$ with $|F_n(y)| \le C$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $y \in K$.

articles.title: A uniformly bounded sequence on an open set is locally uniformly bounded
articles.statement:
Let
$U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open, let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions
$\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and let $C \ge 0$ be real. If $|F_n(y)| \le C$ for all
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $y \in U$, then $(F_n)$ is locally uniformly bounded on $U$.

articles.title: Locally uniformly bounded sequence of functions
articles.statement:
Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ and let
$(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$. The sequence is
locally uniformly bounded on $U$ when every $x \in U$ has an open neighbourhood $V \subseteq U$
and a real $C \ge 0$ such that $|F_n(y)| \le C$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $y \in V$.

articles.title: Montel's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open and let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a
sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, each holomorphic on $U$, that is locally
uniformly bounded on $U$. Then there are a strictly increasing map
$\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, holomorphic
on $U$, such that $F_{\varphi(n)} \to f$ locally uniformly on $U$ as $n \to \infty$.

## Sources

- Montel's theorem on normal families, P. Montel 1912/1927; see Ahlfors, Functions of One Complex Variable II; Lean is locally uniformly bounded holomorphic family with strictly monotone subsequence locally uniform convergent to holomorphic limit, open U form.

articles.title: Vitali's convergence theorem
articles.statement:
Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open and preconnected, and let
$(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, each holomorphic
on $U$, that is locally uniformly bounded on $U$. Let $S \subseteq U$ have an accumulation point
$x_0 \in U$, and let $g : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $F_n(z) \to g(z)$ as $n \to \infty$
for every $z \in S$. Then there is a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, holomorphic on $U$,
with $f(z) = g(z)$ for all $z \in S$, such that $F_n \to f$ locally uniformly on $U$.

## Sources

- Vitali convergence theorem, G. Vitali 1903; see Hille, Analytic Function Theory Vol II and Conway II; Lean is open preconnected U locally uniformly bounded with AccPt accumulation and pointwise limit on S extends to locally uniform holomorphic convergence, Montel-related strengthening.

articles.title: Coordinate axes
articles.statement:
The coordinate axes of $\mathbb{C}$: the union of the real axis and the
imaginary axis.

articles.title: Continuous functions holomorphic off the coordinate axes are entire
articles.statement:
Let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous on all of $\mathbb{C}$ and holomorphic on the
complement of the coordinate axes. Then $f$ is holomorphic on all of $\mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; General properties of functions of one complex variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_27`.

articles.title: Imaginary axis
articles.statement:
The imaginary axis is the set
$\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z = 0\}$.

articles.title: Real axis
articles.statement: The real axis is the set $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im} z = 0\}$.

articles.title: Residue theorem on a disc
articles.statement:
Let $c\in\mathbb{C}$ and $R>0$, and let $S$ be a finite set of
points of the open disc $\{z:|z-c|\lt R\}$. For each $s\in S$ let $r_s>0$ be such that the closed
disc $\{z:|z-s|\le r_s\}$ lies in $\{z:|z-c|\lt R\}$ and contains no point of $S$ other than $s$.
Let $f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be complex differentiable on $\{z:|z-c|\le R\}\setminus S$ and
integrable on the circle $|z-c|=R$ and on each circle $|z-s|=r_s$. Then, with all circles
oriented counterclockwise,

$$\oint_{|z-c|=R} f(z)\,dz=\sum_{s\in S}\oint_{|z-s|=r_s} f(z)\,dz.$$

Each integral on the right is $2\pi i$ times the residue of $f$ at $s$.

## Sources

- L. V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, §5.1 (the residue theorem).

articles.title: Rouché's theorem on a disc
articles.statement:
Let $c \in \mathbb{C}$ and $R > 0$, and let $f$ and $g$ be analytic
at every point of the closed disc $|z - c| \le R$. If $|g(z)| < |f(z)|$ for every $z$ on the circle
$|z - c| = R$, then $f$ and $f + g$ have the same number of zeros in the open disc $|z - c| < R$,
counted with multiplicity: the divisors of $f$ and of $f + g$ on the open disc have equal sums.

## Sources

- E. Rouché, Mémoire sur la série de Lagrange, J. École Polytechnique 22 (1862), 193-224

articles.title: Rouché's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $R > 0$, let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be meromorphic on
$\mathbb{C}$ and in normal form (at every point $f$ is either analytic, or has a pole and takes
the value $0$ there), and let $g : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic on $\mathbb{C}$.
If $|g(z)| < |f(z)|$ for every $z$ with $|z| = R$, then $f + g$ and $f$ have the same number
of zeros in the closed disk $|z| \le R$, counted with multiplicity: the sum over the points of
the disk of the positive part of the order of $f + g$ equals the same sum for $f$.

## Sources

- E. Rouché, *Mémoire sur la série de Lagrange*, J. École Polytechnique 22 (1862) (Rouché's theorem). Problem `rouche` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Schwarz reflection principle
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on the
open upper half-plane $\{z : \operatorname{Im} z > 0\}$, continuous on the closed upper half-plane
$\{z : \operatorname{Im} z \ge 0\}$, and real-valued on the real axis. Then there is an entire
function $g$ that agrees with $f$ on the closed upper half-plane and satisfies
$g(\bar z) = \overline{g(z)}$ for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schwarz_reflection_principle.

articles.title: A three-circles inequality for circles tangent at the origin
articles.statement:
Let
$f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function and, for $r>0$, let
\[
A(r)=\sup\{\lvert f(z)\rvert:\lvert z-r\rvert=r\}.
\]
Then
\[
A(1)^{2}\le A(2)\,A\!\left(\frac{2}{3}\right).
\]

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_99`.

articles.title: Every countable dense set is a preimage of any other under an entire function
articles.statement:
For any two
countable dense subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\mathbb{C}$, there is an entire function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, $f(z) \in B$ if and only
if $z \in A$; that is, $f^{-1}(B) = A$.

Hayman's update to Problem 2.31 reports that Barth and Schneider constructed such functions.

## Sources

- K. F. Barth and W. J. Schneider, Entire functions mapping arbitrary countable dense sets and their complements onto each other, J. London Math. Soc. (2) 4 (1972), 482-488, https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms/s2-4.3.482.

articles.title: Erdős's problem on countable dense preimages
articles.statement:
This is the statement that for any two
countable dense subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\mathbb{C}$, there is an entire function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, $f(z) \in B$ if and only
if $z \in A$; that is, $f^{-1}(B) = A$.

## Sources

- Research Problems in Function Theory, Problem 2.31 (record AMR-022-2031).

articles.title: Entire solutions of the Fermat cubic are constant
articles.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be entire functions
with $f(z)^3 + g(z)^3 = 1$ for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$. Then $f$ and $g$ are constant.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Entire and meromorphic functions of one complex variable, and related topics), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_61`.

articles.title: A $1$-periodic entire function bounded by $C e^{|\operatorname{Im} s|}$ is constant
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be entire with $f(s + 1) = f(s)$ for all $s \in \mathbb{C}$,
and suppose there is a real constant $C$ such that $|f(s)| \le C e^{|\operatorname{Im} s|}$ for
every $s$ with $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$. Then $f$ is constant.

The two-sided bound cannot be weakened to the one-sided $|f(s)| = O(e^{\operatorname{Im} s})$ as
$\operatorname{Im} s \to \infty$: the function $f(s) = e^{2 \pi i s}$ is entire and $1$-periodic,
satisfies $|f(s)| = e^{-2 \pi \operatorname{Im} s} \le e^{\operatorname{Im} s}$ for
$\operatorname{Im} s \ge 0$, and is not constant.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI`, Lemma 17.14, corrected; the book prints the one-sided bound, under which the lemma is false.

articles.title: Injective entire functions are affine
articles.statement:
If $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is entire and
injective, then there are $a, b \in \mathbb{C}$ with $a \ne 0$ such that $f(z) = az + b$ for all
$z \in \mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_37`.

articles.title: A nonzero entire power series with infinitely many zeros
articles.statement:
There is a sequence
$(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ of complex numbers, not all zero, such that the power series
$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k z^k$ converges absolutely for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ and its sum
vanishes at infinitely many points $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; Entire and meromorphic functions of one complex variable, and related topics), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_14`.

articles.title: Hayman–Kjellberg theorem on continua receding to infinity
articles.statement:
Write $M(f, r)$ for the Wiman
maximum modulus of a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ at radius $r$. For every entire,
transcendental function $f$ and every closed, connected, unbounded set
$\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, the limit superior, as $|z| \to \infty$ with $z \in \Gamma$, of the
extended real ratio $\log |f(z)| / \log M(f, |z|)$ is at least $-1$. Here the ratio is taken to
be $-\infty$ where $f(z) = 0$, and $0$ where $f(z) \ne 0$ and $\log M(f, |z|) = 0$.

Hayman and Kjellberg (Studies in Pure Mathematics, Birkhauser 1983) proved that for entire $f$ and
every $K > 1$ all components of $\{z : \log |f(z)| + K \log M(f, |z|) < 0\}$ are bounded, so the
absolute constant in Hayman–Lingham Problem 2.35 is $A = 1$.

## Sources

- A. Eremenko and J. K. Langley, Meromorphic functions of one complex variable. A survey, arXiv:0801.0692 (2008), https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.0692; Walter K. Hayman and Eleanor F. Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition), arXiv:1809.07200v2 (2018), https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Lower bound $-1$ for the log-modulus ratio along continua
articles.statement:
Write $M(f, r)$ for the Wiman
maximum modulus of a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ at radius $r$. This is the statement
that for every entire, transcendental function $f$ and every continuum $\Gamma$ receding to
infinity (a closed, connected, unbounded subset of $\mathbb{C}$), the limit superior, as
$|z| \to \infty$ with $z \in \Gamma$, of the extended real ratio $\log |f(z)| / \log M(f, |z|)$
is at least $-1$. Here the ratio is taken to be $-\infty$ where $f(z) = 0$, and $0$ where
$f(z) \ne 0$ and $\log M(f, |z|) = 0$.

Transcendence is the standing hypothesis of Hayman's problem; without it the zero function would
be a counterexample, its ratio being constantly $-\infty$.

## Sources

- problem record AMR-022-2035.

articles.title: Entire functions
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is entire when it is complex
differentiable at every point of $\mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- the problem record gives $f$ entire only as ambient context from Hayman; it is taken here as an explicit hypothesis.

articles.title: Ratio of $\log |f|$ to the logarithm of the maximum modulus
articles.statement:
For a function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a point $z \in \mathbb{C}$, this is the extended real number
equal to $-\infty$ if $f(z) = 0$, and otherwise to the real number
$\log |f(z)| / \log M(f, |z|)$, where $M(f, r)$ is the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$, $\log 0$ is
taken to be $0$, and division by $0$ gives $0$.

articles.title: Continua receding to infinity
articles.statement:
A set $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a continuum receding
to infinity when it is closed, connected and unbounded.

Here a continuum is read as a closed connected set and receding to infinity as unbounded;
compactness is not required, since an unbounded set is never compact.

articles.title: Hayman auxiliary function $A$
articles.statement:
For a function $G : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real
number $r$, $A(r)$ is the real part of $r\,G'(r)/G(r)$, where $G'$ is the complex derivative of
$G$.

articles.title: Hayman auxiliary function $B$
articles.statement:
For a function $G : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real
number $r$, $B(r) = r\,A'(r)$, where $A$ is the Hayman auxiliary function of $G$, viewed as a
real function of $r$, and $A'$ is its derivative.

articles.title: Hayman's coefficient asymptotic (finite radius)
articles.statement:
Let $G : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be
Hayman admissible on $(R_0, \rho)$, with Hayman auxiliary functions $A$ and $B$. Let
$(c_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be complex numbers such that $\sum_{n \ge 0} c_n z^n$ converges absolutely to
$G(z)$ for every complex $z$ with $|z| < \rho$, and let $(r_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be real numbers such
that for all sufficiently large $n$, $r_n \in (R_0, \rho)$, $A(r_n) = n$, and $r_n$ is the only
$r \in (R_0, \rho)$ with $A(r) = n$. Then, as $n \to \infty$,

$$c_n \sim \frac{G(r_n)}{r_n^n \sqrt{2\pi B(r_n)}}.$$

Proof: The saddle converges to the finite radius, Cauchy's coefficient integral is split at the
admissibility cutoff, and the central Gaussian term and decaying tails are normalized separately.

## Sources

- arXiv:1906.07169v2, tex lines 495-506.

articles.title: Hayman-admissible function (finite radius)
articles.statement:
Let $G : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, let
$R_0$ and $\rho$ be real numbers, write $G'$ for the complex derivative of $G$ and $A$, $B$ for
the Hayman auxiliary functions of $G$, and say that a property holds for $r$ near $\rho$ if there
is $\eta > 0$ such that it holds for every $r \in (R_0, \rho)$ with $r > \rho - \eta$. Then $G$ is
Hayman admissible on $(R_0, \rho)$ when $0 < R_0 < \rho$; $G$ is analytic on the open disk
$|z| < \rho$; for every $r \in (R_0, \rho)$, $G(r)$ is a positive real number and
$r\,G'(r)/G(r)$ is real; $A(r) \to \infty$ and $B(r) \to \infty$ as $r$ tends to $\rho$ within
$(R_0, \rho)$; and there is a function $\delta : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$0 < \delta(r) < \pi$ for $r$ near $\rho$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all $r$ near
$\rho$, every real $\theta$ with $|\theta| \le \delta(r)$ satisfies the locality estimate

$$\left|G(re^{i\theta}) - G(r)\,e^{i\theta A(r) - \theta^2 B(r)/2}\right|
\le \varepsilon \left|G(r)\,e^{i\theta A(r) - \theta^2 B(r)/2}\right|,$$

and every real $\theta$ with $\delta(r) \le |\theta| < \pi$ satisfies the decay estimate
$|G(re^{i\theta})| \le \varepsilon\,|G(r)|/\sqrt{B(r)}$.

The capture, locality and decay conditions follow the Flajolet-Sedgewick formulation rather than
the abbreviated maximum-modulus restatement (Jiyou Li, "Asymptotic Estimate for the Multinomial
Coefficients", Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), Article 20.1.3, Lemma [Hayman] `lem2`),
whose maximum-modulus condition is insufficient as stated and is not used.

articles.title: Bounded holomorphic functions on the punctured plane are constant
articles.statement:
Let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{0\}$, and suppose that
there is a real number $C$ with $|f(z)| \le C$ for every $z \ne 0$. Then there is a constant
$c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = c$ for every $z \ne 0$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; Entire and meromorphic functions of one complex variable, and related topics), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_84`.

articles.title: An entire function of sublinear growth is constant
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
be an entire function such that $f(z)/z \to 0$ as $|z| \to \infty$. Then $f$ is constant: there
is $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = c$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Entire and meromorphic functions of one complex variable, and related topics), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_28`.

articles.title: An entire function with a polynomial derivative is a polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive
integer and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be an entire function. If there is a complex
polynomial $p$ such that the $k$th derivative of $f$ satisfies $f^{(k)}(z) = p(z)$ for all
$z \in \mathbb{C}$, then there is a complex polynomial $q$ such that $f(z) = q(z)$ for all
$z \in \mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; Entire and meromorphic functions of one complex variable, and related topics), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_90`.

articles.title: Mittag-Leffler theorem, discrete-subspace form
articles.statement:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a closed set
that is discrete in the subspace topology, and for each $s \in S$ let $c_s$ be a finitely supported
sequence of complex coefficients. Then there is a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is
holomorphic on $\mathbb{C} \setminus S$, meromorphic on all of $\mathbb{C}$, and such that for every
$s \in S$ the difference between $f$ and the principal part at $s$ with coefficients $c_s$ is
analytic at $s$.

articles.title: Mittag-Leffler theorem
articles.statement:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a closed set such that every $z \in S$
has a radius $\varepsilon > 0$ for which the punctured disk $\{w : 0 < |w - z| < \varepsilon\}$
contains no point of $S$, and for each $s \in S$ let $c_s$ be a finitely supported sequence of
complex coefficients. Then there is a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is holomorphic
on $\mathbb{C} \setminus S$, meromorphic on all of $\mathbb{C}$, and such that for every $s \in S$
the difference between $f$ and the principal part at $s$ with coefficients $c_s$ is analytic at
$s$.

## Sources

- Mittag-Leffler theorem, G. Mittag-Leffler, Acta Math. 4 (1884); see Rudin; Lean is closed discrete S with punctured-ball isolation, prescribed finite principal parts via Finsupp, global meromorphic existence holomorphic on Sᶜ.

articles.title: The principal part is analytic away from its pole
articles.statement:
For every $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and every
finitely supported sequence $c$ of complex coefficients, the principal part at $s$ with
coefficients $c$ is analytic at every point $z \neq s$.

articles.title: The principal part is meromorphic
articles.statement:
For every $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and every finitely
supported sequence $c$ of complex coefficients, the principal part at $s$ with coefficients $c$ is
meromorphic at every point of $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Principal part with finitely many coefficients
articles.statement:
For a point $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and a finitely
supported sequence $c = (c_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ of complex coefficients, the principal part at
$s$ with coefficients $c$ is the function $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ given by
$z \mapsto \sum_k c_k (z - s)^{-(k+1)}$, the sum running over the finitely many $k$ with
$c_k \neq 0$.

At $z = s$ every term is taken to be $0$ (the convention $0^{-n} = 0$), so the function has value
$0$ there.

articles.title: No non-exponential solution of the Rényi–Vincze conditions
articles.statement:
There are no function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and real numbers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ such that $f$ is not the
function $z \mapsto c\,e^z$ for any real $c > 0$; $a_n \ge 0$ for every $n$; $a_n \ne 0$ for
infinitely many $n$; for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} a_n z^n$ has sum
$f(z)$; $f$ is entire; and either $\int_0^\infty a_n x^n / f(x)\,dx = 1$ for every $n \ge 0$, or
$\int_0^\infty f(\rho x) / f(x)\,dx = 1/(1-\rho)$ for every real $\rho$ with $0 < \rho < 1$.

Miles and Williamson (J. London Math. Soc. (2) 33 (1986) 110-116) proved that a transcendental
entire $f$ with positive coefficients and $\int_0^\infty a_n x^n / f(x)\,dx = 1$ for all $n$ is
$c\,e^z$. The first integral condition forces every $a_n > 0$, and the second reduces to the
first.

## Sources

- Antonio Greco and Andrea Loi, Radial balanced metrics on the unit disk, arXiv:0803.3711 (2008), https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.3711.

articles.title: Hayman Problem 2.32: a non-exponential solution of the Rényi–Vincze conditions
articles.statement:
There
exist a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and real numbers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ such that
$f$ is not the function $z \mapsto c\,e^z$ for any real $c > 0$; $a_n \ge 0$ for every $n$;
$a_n \ne 0$ for infinitely many $n$; for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ the series
$\sum_{n \ge 0} a_n z^n$ has sum $f(z)$; $f$ is entire; and either
$\int_0^\infty a_n x^n / f(x)\,dx = 1$ for every $n \ge 0$ (condition (2.6)), or
$\int_0^\infty f(\rho x) / f(x)\,dx = 1/(1-\rho)$ for every real $\rho$ with $0 < \rho < 1$
(condition (2.6)').

## Sources

- AMR-022-2032, Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 2.32 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200, source labels 2.6 and 2.6', A. Renyi, St. Vincze).

articles.title: Normalized spherical area
articles.statement:
For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and real $r$, the
normalized spherical area $A(f, r)$ of $f$ on the disk $|z| < r$ is $\frac{1}{\pi}$ times the
Lebesgue integral of the spherical density of $f$ over the open disk
$\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < r\}$ (the integral is taken to be $0$ if the density is not
integrable there).

articles.title: Hayman's spherical-area ratio conjecture is false
articles.statement:
Not every function
$f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is meromorphic on all of $\mathbb{C}$ and nonconstant
(complex differentiable at two points where it takes different values) has bounded root counts
and satisfies $\liminf_{r \to \infty} n(f, r)/A(f, r) = 1$, where $n(f, r)$ is the maximum
valence and $A(f, r)$ the normalized spherical area of $f$ on the disk $|z| < r$.

Toppila constructed a nonconstant meromorphic function $f$ with
$\liminf_{r \to \infty} n(f, r)/A(f, r) \ge 80/79$, and Hinkkanen and Miles (arXiv:2401.13808,
2024, Theorem 1.1) give one with $\liminf_{r \to \infty} n(f, r)/A(f, r) \ge 1.07328$.

## Sources

- A. Hinkkanen and J. Miles, Maximum and Average Valence of Meromorphic Functions, arXiv preprint (2024), arXiv:2401.13808, https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.13808.

articles.title: Hayman's spherical-area ratio conjecture
articles.statement:
The statement that every function
$f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is meromorphic on all of $\mathbb{C}$ and nonconstant
(complex differentiable at two points where it takes different values) has bounded root counts
(for every real $r$, the numbers of roots of $f(z) = a$ in $|z| < r$, counted with
multiplicity, are bounded above as $a$ ranges over $\mathbb{C}$) and satisfies

$$\liminf_{r \to \infty} \frac{n(f, r)}{A(f, r)} = 1,$$

where $n(f, r)$ is the supremum over $a \in \mathbb{C}$ of the number of roots of $f(z) = a$ in
$|z| < r$ counted with multiplicity, and $A(f, r)$ is the normalized spherical area of $f$ on
$|z| < r$.

For such $f$ it is known that $1 \le \liminf_{r \to \infty} n(f, r)/A(f, r) \le e$; Hayman asked
whether $e$ can be replaced by $1$. The statement is recorded as a proposition and is not
asserted.

## Sources

- problem record AMR-022-1016 (W. K. Hayman).

articles.title: Bounded root counts
articles.statement:
A function $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has bounded root
counts if for every real $r$ the root counts of $f$ in radius $r$, that is, the numbers of roots
of $f(z) = a$ in $|z| < r$ counted with multiplicity, are bounded above as $a$ ranges over
$\mathbb{C}$.

This guarantees that the supremum over $a$ defining the maximum valence of $f$ in radius $r$ is
taken over a bounded set.

articles.title: Germ-wise nonconstant function
articles.statement:
A function $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is
nonconstant if there are points $u, v \in \mathbb{C}$ at which $f$ is complex differentiable and
$f(u) \ne f(v)$.

This excludes pointwise-modified constant functions (for example $f(0) = 1$ and $f(z) = 0$ for
$z \ne 0$), which are meromorphic with zero derivative density but represent the constant zero
germ.

articles.title: Maximum valence
articles.statement:
For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and real $r$, $n(f, r)$ is the
supremum in $\mathbb{R}$, over all $a \in \mathbb{C}$, of the root count of $f$ at $a$ in radius
$r$, that is, of the number of roots of $f(z) = a$ in $|z| < r$ counted with multiplicity.

This is a conditional supremum of real numbers, so it is meaningful only when these root counts
are bounded above as $a$ varies; see bounded root counts.

articles.title: Root count
articles.statement:
For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, $a \in \mathbb{C}$ and real $r$, the
root count of $f$ at $a$ in radius $r$ is the number of roots of $f(z) = a$ in the open disk
$|z| < r$, counted with multiplicity: the sum over $z \in \mathbb{C}$ of the positive part of
