the divisor of $f - a$ on that disk at $z$ (the sum is taken to be $0$ if infinitely many terms
are nonzero).

articles.title: Spherical density
articles.statement:
For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the
spherical density of $f$ at $z$ is $|f'(z)|^2 / (1 + |f(z)|^2)^2$, where $f'(z)$ is the complex
derivative of $f$ at $z$, taken to be $0$ where $f$ is not differentiable.

articles.title: Turán's three-value question has a negative answer
articles.statement:
There is a function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, meromorphic on $\mathbb{C}$, such that for every $w \in \mathbb{C}$
there is a point at which $f - w$ has finite meromorphic order, together with three distinct
values $w_1, w_2, w_3$ of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$ such that for every real
$r > 0$ there is a natural number $C$ for which, for each $i$ and every open disc of radius $r$,
the multiplicities of $w_i$ as a value of $f$ at the points of any finite subset of the disc add
up to at most $C$; and yet $f$ does not have bounded value distribution.

A. A. Gol'dberg (Izv. Vyssh. Uchebn. Zaved. Mat. 1972) answered Turan's question negatively, as
recorded in Hayman-Lingham Update 2.28; the Weierstrass sigma-function is another
counterexample: it has boundedly many $w$-points per disc for every bounded set of $w$ but has
order $2$, so it does not have bounded value distribution.

## Sources

- W. K. Hayman and E. F. Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), arXiv:1809.07200, https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Turán's three-value question
articles.statement:
The statement that every function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with the following properties has bounded value distribution:
$f$ is meromorphic on $\mathbb{C}$; for every $w \in \mathbb{C}$ there is a point at which
$f - w$ has finite meromorphic order; and there are three distinct values $w_1, w_2, w_3$ of
the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$ such that for every real $r > 0$ there is a
natural number $C$ for which, for each $i$ and every open disc of radius $r$, the
multiplicities of $w_i$ as a value of $f$ at the points of any finite subset of the disc add
up to at most $C$.

## Sources

- Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 2.28 [AMR-022-2028], <https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200>, question by P. Turán.

articles.title: Bounded value distribution
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has bounded value
distribution if for every real $r > 0$ there is a natural number $C$ such that, for every value
$w$ of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$ and every open disc of radius $r$, the
multiplicities of $w$ as a value of $f$ at the points of any finite subset of the disc add up
to at most $C$.

The source states this for functions meromorphic in the plane; the definition itself does not
assume meromorphy.

## Sources

- Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 2.28 [AMR-022-2028], <https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200>.

articles.title: Multiplicity of a pole
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$. The
multiplicity of $z$ as a pole of $f$, that is, the multiplicity of the value $\infty$ at $z$, is
$-n$ if $f$ has finite meromorphic order $n < 0$ at $z$, and $0$ otherwise. In particular it is
$0$ unless $f$ has a pole at $z$.

## Sources

- Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 2.28 [AMR-022-2028], <https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200>.

articles.title: Multiplicity of a value on the Riemann sphere
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and
$z \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $w$ be a point of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$.
The multiplicity of $w$ as a value of $f$ at $z$ is the multiplicity of $z$ as a root of
$f = w$ when $w$ is finite, and the multiplicity of $z$ as a pole of $f$ when $w = \infty$.

## Sources

- Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 2.28 [AMR-022-2028], <https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200>.

articles.title: Multiplicity of a root of $f = w$
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and
$w, z \in \mathbb{C}$. The multiplicity of $z$ as a root of the equation $f = w$ is an extended
natural number: it is $\infty$ if $f(t) = w$ for every $t \neq z$ in some neighbourhood of $z$;
otherwise it is $n$ if $f - w$ has meromorphic order $n \ge 0$ at $z$, and it is $0$ if that
order is negative or $f - w$ is not meromorphic at $z$.

It depends only on the values of $f$ on a punctured neighbourhood of $z$, so changing $f(z)$
does not change it. It is $0$ when $f$ has a pole at $z$, and when $f - w$ is analytic at $z$
with $f(z) \neq w$.

## Sources

- Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 2.28 [AMR-022-2028], <https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200>.

articles.title: Weierstrass theorem on prescribed simple zeros
articles.statement:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a closed set
all of whose points are isolated: for each $z \in S$ there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that no point
$w \ne z$ of $S$ satisfies $|w - z| < \varepsilon$. Then there is an entire function $f$ whose zeros
are exactly the points of $S$, all of them simple: $f'(z) \ne 0$ for every $z \in S$.

## Sources

- Weierstrass factorization theorem 1876; see Rudin; Lean is simple-zero corollary with closed discrete prescribed zero set S and entire f with exact zeros S and nonvanishing derivative on S.

articles.title: The Taylor terms are bounded above
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor
coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $r$ be real. Then the set of Taylor terms
$\{|a_n|\,|r|^n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is bounded above.

articles.title: The logarithmic majorant is $C^2$
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor
coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$ be the
logarithm of its radial Taylor majorant at radius $e^x$ (with $\log 0 = 0$). Then $\Phi$ is
twice continuously differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Cubing a Wiman 2/3 bound
articles.statement:
Let $M$ and $\mu$ be real numbers with $M \ge 0$,
$\mu \ge 0$ and $\log \mu \ge 0$, where $\log$ is the real logarithm with $\log 0 = 0$.
If $M \le \mu (\log \mu)^{2/3}$, then $M^3 \le \mu^3 (\log \mu)^2$.

articles.title: Derivative of the logarithmic majorant as a mean
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function whose
Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let
$\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. For real $x$, let $\nu_x$ be the coefficient
measure tilted at $x$, the probability measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with
$\nu_x(\{n\}) = |a_n| e^{nx} / \sum_{m \ge 0} |a_m| e^{mx}$. Then
$\Phi'(x) = \int n \, d\nu_x(n)$, the mean of $n$ under $\nu_x$.

articles.title: Absorbing constants into the exponent gap
articles.statement:
For every real $C > 0$ there is a real $U > 1$
such that for all reals $\mu$ and $A$ with $U \le \mu \le A$ and
$A \le C \mu \bigl(1 + (\log A)^{81/128}\bigr)$, we have $A \le \mu (\log \mu)^{2/3}$.

The gap $2/3 - 81/128 > 0$ between the exponents absorbs the constant $C$ of the corrected
Rosenbloom estimate once the maximum term $\mu$ is large.

articles.title: The maximum term eventually exceeds one
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function that is not a
polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term
$\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then there is $R$ such that $\mu(r) > 1$ for all real $r \ge R$.

articles.title: The logarithm of the maximum term is eventually positive
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function
that is not a polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term
$\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then there is $R$ such that $\log \mu(r) > 0$ for all real
$r \ge R$.

articles.title: Eventual regularity of the logarithmic majorant
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a transcendental entire
function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let
$\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. Then $\Phi$ is twice continuously differentiable
on $\mathbb{R}$, $\Phi'(x) \to \infty$ as $x \to \infty$, and there is a real $x_0$ such that
$\Phi(x) > 0$ for every $x \ge x_0$ and both $\Phi$ and $\Phi'$ are nondecreasing on
$[x_0, \infty)$.

articles.title: The Wiman exceptional set has finite measure
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function,
let $M_f$ be its radial majorant and let $g(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. For $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ let
$E_f(x_0)$ be the Wiman exceptional set, the set of $x \ge x_0$ with $g(x)^{9/8} \le g'(x)$ or
$g'(x)^{9/8} \le g''(x)$. There is $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $E_f(x_0)$ has finite Lebesgue
measure and $g''(x) \le g(x)^{81/64}$ for every $x \ge x_0$ outside $E_f(x_0)$.

The exponent $81/64 = (9/8)^2$ comes from composing the two growth bounds.

articles.title: The maximum modulus is attained
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function and let $r \ge 0$. Then
there is a point $z$ with $|z| = r$ such that $|f(w)| \le |f(z)|$ for every $w$ with $|w| = r$,
and the maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|w| = r} |f(w)|$ equals $|f(z)|$.

articles.title: Wiman's inequality with exponent $2/3$ at arbitrarily large radii
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a
transcendental entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, maximum modulus
$M(r) = \sup_{|z| = |r|} |f(z)|$ and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_{n \ge 0} |a_n| |r|^n$. Then
for every real $R$ there is a real $r > R$ with $M(r) \le \mu(r) (\log \mu(r))^{2/3}$.

## Sources

- Filevych (2003), Matematychni Studii 20(2), 215–221. This is a strict corollary of, not the full theorem stated in, that paper.

articles.title: The maximum term is attained by a Taylor term
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor
coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real
$r$ there is an $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $|a_n|\,|r|^n = \mu(r)$.

articles.title: Taylor expansion of an entire function
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor
coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin. For every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the series
$\sum_{n \ge 0} a_n z^n$ converges unconditionally to $f(z)$.

articles.title: Transcendental entire functions have infinitely many Taylor coefficients
articles.statement: A transcendental entire function has infinitely many nonzero Taylor coefficients.

articles.title: Exponential moments of the Wiman coefficient measure are finite
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire
function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, which gives each
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ mass $|a_n|$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. For every real $x$, the function
$n \mapsto e^{xn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$.

articles.title: The exponential-integrability set of the Wiman coefficient measure is the whole line
articles.statement:
Let
$f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. The set
of real $t$ for which $n \mapsto e^{tn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$ is all of
$\mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Exponential moments of the Wiman coefficient measure equal the Wiman majorant
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be
an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$ at $0$, and let $\mu_f$ be its
Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$,

$$\int e^{xn}\,d\mu_f(n) = M_f(e^x),$$

where $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n|\,|r|^n$ is the Wiman majorant of $f$.

articles.title: The Wiman tilted measure is a probability measure
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function such that
$f^{(n)}(0)/n! \ne 0$ for some $n$, and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on
$\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$, the Wiman tilted measure of $f$ at $x$, which has density
$n \mapsto e^{xn} / \int e^{xm}\,d\mu_f(m)$ with respect to $\mu_f$, is a probability measure.

articles.title: Transcendental functions
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is
transcendental when there is no complex polynomial $p$ with $f(z) = p(z)$ for all
$z \in \mathbb{C}$.

No analyticity is assumed; results about transcendental entire functions assume it separately.

articles.title: Second derivative of the logarithmic majorant as a variance
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire
function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let
$\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. For real $x$, let $\nu_x$ be the coefficient
measure tilted at $x$, the probability measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with
$\nu_x(\{n\}) = |a_n| e^{nx} / \sum_{m \ge 0} |a_m| e^{mx}$. Then $\Phi''(x)$ is the variance
of $n$ under $\nu_x$.

articles.title: The logarithmic majorant has nonnegative second derivative
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire
function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let
$\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. Then $\Phi''(x) \ge 0$ for every real $x$.

articles.title: Every real parameter is interior to the exponential-integrability set
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an
entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. Every real $x$
lies in the interior of the set of real $t$ for which $n \mapsto e^{tn}$ is integrable with
respect to $\mu_f$.

articles.title: Values on a circle are bounded by the maximum modulus
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
be continuous, let $r$ be a real number and let $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|z| = r$. Then
$|f(z)| \le M(f, r)$, where $M(f, r)$ is the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.

articles.title: Power-growth exceptional set
articles.statement:
For a function $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and real
numbers $p$ and $x_0$, this is the set of real numbers $x \ge x_0$ such that
$h(x)^p \le h'(x)$, where $h(x)^p$ is the real power and $h'(x)$ is the derivative of $h$ at
$x$, taken to be $0$ where $h$ is not differentiable.

articles.title: Summability of the radial Taylor terms
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor
coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin. For every real $r$, the series
$\sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ converges.

articles.title: The maximum term of a transcendental entire function tends to infinity
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an
entire function that is not a polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin
and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then $\mu(r) \to \infty$ as $r \to \infty$.

articles.title: The maximum term tends to infinity along logarithmic radii
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a transcendental
entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term
$\mu(r) = \sup_{n \ge 0} |a_n| |r|^n$. Then $\mu(e^x) \to \infty$ as $x \to \infty$.

articles.title: The power-growth exceptional set has finite measure
articles.statement:
Let $p > 1$ and $x_0$ be real
numbers, and let $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuously differentiable, with
$h(x) > 0$ for all $x \ge x_0$ and $h$ nondecreasing on $[x_0, \infty)$. Then the
power-growth exceptional set of $h$, the set of $x \ge x_0$ with $h(x)^p \le h'(x)$, has finite
Lebesgue measure.

articles.title: The Wiman growth is the cumulant generating function of the coefficient measure
articles.statement:
Let $f$
be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every
real $x$, the cumulant generating function of $n \mapsto n$ under $\mu_f$ at $x$, namely
$\log \int e^{xn}\,d\mu_f(n)$, equals the Wiman growth $G_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$, where $M_f$ is
the Wiman majorant of $f$.

articles.title: A nonzero Taylor coefficient makes the Wiman coefficient measure nonzero
articles.statement:
Let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. If $a_n \ne 0$ for some $n$, then the
Wiman coefficient measure $\mu_f$ of $f$ is not the zero measure.

articles.title: Point masses of the Wiman coefficient measure
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and
$a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Wiman coefficient measure $\mu_f$ of $f$
gives the singleton $\{n\}$ mass $\mu_f(\{n\}) = |a_n|$.

articles.title: Wiman coefficient measure
articles.statement:
For $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients
$a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$ at $0$, the Wiman coefficient measure of $f$ is the measure
$\mu_f = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n|\,\delta_n$ on $\mathbb{N}$, which gives each $n$ mass $|a_n|$.

articles.title: Wiman exceptional set
articles.statement:
For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with radial majorant
$M_f$, let $g(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. For $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$, the Wiman exceptional set $E_f(x_0)$
is the union of the power-growth bad sets of $g$ and of $g'$ with exponent $9/8$ above $x_0$,
that is, the set of $x \ge x_0$ with $g(x)^{9/8} \le g'(x)$ or $g'(x)^{9/8} \le g''(x)$.

articles.title: Wiman growth function
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ have Taylor coefficients
$a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, and let $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ be its
radial majorant, taken to be $0$ when the series diverges. For a real number $x$, the Wiman
growth of $f$ at $x$ is $\log M_f(e^x)$, the logarithm of the radial majorant at radius $e^x$,
with the convention $\log 0 = 0$.

articles.title: Majorant bound off an exceptional set
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function with
Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$, maximum
term $\mu_f(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and logarithmic majorant $g_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. There are
reals $C > 0$ and $x_0$ such that the Wiman exceptional set $E_f(x_0)$ has finite Lebesgue measure
and, for every real $x \ge x_0$ with $x \notin E_f(x_0)$,
$M_f(e^x) \le C\,\mu_f(e^x)\,\bigl(1 + g_f(x)^{81/128}\bigr)$.

articles.title: Corrected Rosenbloom estimate
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients
$a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$, maximum term
$\mu_f(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and logarithmic majorant $g_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. For every real
$x$, $M_f(e^x) \le 8\,\mu_f(e^x)\,\bigl(1 + \sqrt{g_f''(x)}\bigr)$.

The additive $1$ keeps the estimate valid when $g_f''(x) = 0$.

articles.title: The radial majorant is nonnegative
articles.statement:
For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with
Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin and every real number $r$, the radial
majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ (taken to be $0$ when the series diverges)
satisfies $0 \le M_f(r)$.

articles.title: Radial majorant
articles.statement:
For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients
$a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin and a real number $r$, the radial majorant of $f$ at $r$ is
$M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$, the sum of the radial Taylor terms at radius $|r|$.
By convention $M_f(r) = 0$ when this series diverges.

articles.title: Wiman maximum modulus at the absolute value of the radius
articles.statement:
For every function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at
radius $|r|$ equals the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.

articles.title: The maximum modulus is at most the radial Taylor majorant
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function
with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and let $r \ge 0$. Then the maximum modulus
$M(r) = \sup_{|z| = r} |f(z)|$ satisfies $M(r) \le \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| r^n$.

articles.title: The Wiman maximum modulus is even in the radius
articles.statement:
For every function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at
radius $-r$ equals the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.

articles.title: Wiman maximum modulus
articles.statement:
For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real number
$r$, the Wiman maximum modulus $M(f, r)$ is the supremum of $|f(z)|$ over all $z \in \mathbb{C}$
with $|z| = |r|$.

Here the supremum of a set of real numbers that is not bounded above is taken to be $0$.

articles.title: Wiman maximum term at the absolute value of the radius
articles.statement:
For every function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at
radius $|r|$ equals the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $r$.

articles.title: Bounding the maximum term
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$
at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For all real $r$ and $c$,
$\mu(r) \le c$ if and only if $|a_n|\,|r|^n \le c$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Cauchy's inequality for the maximum term
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor
coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and maximum modulus
$M(r) = \sup_{|z| = |r|} |f(z)|$. Then $\mu(r) \le M(r)$ for every real $r > 0$.

articles.title: The Wiman maximum term is even in the radius
articles.statement:
For every function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at
radius $-r$ equals the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $r$.

articles.title: Wiman maximum term
articles.statement:
For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real number $r$,
the Wiman maximum term $\mu(f, r)$ is the supremum over $n \in \mathbb{N}$ of the Wiman terms
$|a_n| \, |r|^n$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ is the $n$th Wiman Taylor coefficient of $f$.

Here the supremum of a set of real numbers that is not bounded above is taken to be $0$.

articles.title: Moment generating function of the coefficient measure
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with
Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, and let $\mu_f$ be its coefficient measure on
$\mathbb{N}$, which has mass $|a_n|$ at $n$. For every real $x$, the moment generating function of
$n \mapsto n$ under $\mu_f$ at $x$, namely $\int e^{xn}\,d\mu_f(n)$, equals the radial majorant
$M_f(e^x)$, where $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$.

articles.title: Wiman Taylor coefficient
articles.statement:
For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$th Taylor coefficient of $f$ at the origin is
$a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$, where $f^{(n)}$ is the $n$th iterated complex derivative of $f$.

Here the derivative at a point where a function is not complex differentiable is taken to be
$0$. For an entire function these are the coefficients of its Taylor series at $0$.

articles.title: Wiman term at the absolute value of the radius
articles.statement:
For every function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, every real number $r$ and every natural number $n$, the Wiman term
of $f$ at radius $|r|$ and index $n$ equals the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$.

articles.title: Each radial Taylor term is at most the radial majorant
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with
Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, and let
$M_f(r) = \sum_{k \ge 0} |a_k| \, |r|^k$ be its radial majorant. For every real $r$ and every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, $|a_n| \, |r|^n \le M_f(r)$.

articles.title: Each Taylor term is at most the maximum term
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor
coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_k |a_k|\,|r|^k$. For every real
$r$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $|a_n|\,|r|^n \le \mu(r)$.

articles.title: Wiman term at a negated radius
articles.statement:
For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, every
real number $r$ and every natural number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $-r$ and index $n$
equals the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$.

articles.title: Radial Taylor terms are nonnegative
articles.statement:
For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, every real $r$ and every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, we have $0 \le |a_n| \, |r|^n$.

articles.title: Wiman term
articles.statement:
For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, a real number $r$ and a natural
number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$ is the real number $|a_n| \, |r|^n$,
where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ is the $n$th Taylor coefficient of $f$ at the origin. It is the
modulus of the $n$th Taylor term of $f$ on the circle of radius $|r|$.

Using $|r|$ makes a negative input denote the same radius as its absolute value, so the Wiman
term is always nonnegative.

articles.title: Atomic form of the tilted coefficient measure
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor
coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and Taylor terms
$T_n(r) = |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $x$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ equals
$\sum_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \frac{T_n(e^x)}{M_f(e^x)}\,\delta_n$, the measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with mass
$T_n(e^x) / M_f(e^x)$ at each $n$ (with the convention $t/0 = 0$).

articles.title: Atoms of the tilted coefficient measure
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor
coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and Taylor terms
$T_n(r) = |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $x$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the tilted coefficient
measure $\mu_{f,x}$ gives the singleton $\{n\}$ mass $T_n(e^x) / M_f(e^x)$ (with the convention
$t/0 = 0$).

articles.title: Tilted coefficient measure
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ have Taylor coefficients
$a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, and let $\mu_f$ be its coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, with mass $|a_n|$
at $n$. For a real number $x$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ is the exponential tilt of
$\mu_f$ by $n \mapsto xn$: the measure with density $e^{xn} / \int e^{xm}\,d\mu_f(m)$ with respect
to $\mu_f$.

articles.title: Entire functions with zeros and ones on two distinct lines exist
articles.statement:
There exist an entire
function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and two distinct straight lines $l \ne m$ in
$\mathbb{C}$ such that every zero of $f$ lies on $l$, every solution of $f(z) = 1$ lies on $m$,
and $f$ has infinitely many zeros and infinitely many solutions of $f(z) = 1$. Here a straight
line is a set $\{a + tv : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ with $a, v \in \mathbb{C}$ and $v \ne 0$.

For example, $e^z - 1$ has the zeros $2\pi i k$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, on the imaginary axis and
the solutions $\log 2 + 2\pi i k$ of $e^z - 1 = 1$ on a parallel line. Baker (Math. Z. 86
(1964)) and Kobayashi (Kodai Math. J. 2 (1979)) showed that for parallel lines the only
transcendental examples are $f = P(e^{az})$ with $P$ a polynomial and $a$ a constant.

## Sources

- Walter Bergweiler, Alexandre Eremenko and Aimo Hinkkanen, Entire functions with two radially distributed values, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 165 (2018) 93-108, arXiv:1509.03283, https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.03283.

articles.title: Zeros and ones of an entire function on two distinct lines
articles.statement:
This is the statement that
there exist an entire function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and two distinct straight lines
$l \ne m$ in $\mathbb{C}$ such that every zero of $f$ lies on $l$, every solution of $f(z) = 1$
lies on $m$, and $f$ has infinitely many zeros and infinitely many solutions of $f(z) = 1$. Here
a straight line is a set $\{a + tv : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ with $a, v \in \mathbb{C}$ and $v \ne 0$.

## Sources

- Research Problems in Function Theory, Problem 2.24 (record AMR-022-2024).

articles.title: Straight lines in the complex plane
articles.statement:
A set $s \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a straight line if
there are $a, v \in \mathbb{C}$ with $v \ne 0$ such that $s = \{a + tv : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$.

## Sources

- Research Problems in Function Theory, Problem 2.24 (record AMR-022-2024).

articles.title: Functions whose ones lie in a given set
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has
all its ones in a set $m \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ if every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = 1$ lies
in $m$.

## Sources

- Research Problems in Function Theory, Problem 2.24 (record AMR-022-2024).

articles.title: Functions whose zeros lie in a given set
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has
all its zeros in a set $l \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ if every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = 0$ lies
in $l$.

## Sources

- Research Problems in Function Theory, Problem 2.24 (record AMR-022-2024).

articles.title: Zeros of $1+\sum_{n\ge 1}(z/n)^n$ in a disc
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be the entire function

$$F(z)=1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac{z}{n}\right)^{n}.$$

For every real $R>0$, $F$ has only finitely many zeros in the open disc
$\{z\in\mathbb{C} : |z|\lt R\}$, and the number of these zeros counted with multiplicity is at
most $4R$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Entire and meromorphic functions of one complex variable, and related topics), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_91`.

articles.title: The entire function $1+\sum_{n\ge 1}(z/n)^n$
articles.statement:
This is the function
$F:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ given by

$$F(z)=1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac{z}{n}\right)^{n}.$$

articles.title: Nonconstant holomorphic functions of modulus one on the unit circle cover the unit disc
articles.statement:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ be a connected open set containing the closed unit disc
$\{z:|z|\le 1\}$, and let $f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on $U$ and non-constant on
$U$. If $|f(z)|=1$ whenever $|z|=1$, then every $w$ with $|w|<1$ is $f(z)$ for some $z\in U$; that
is, $f(U)$ contains the open unit disc.

The connectedness of $U$ is added to the source statement, which asks only for an open set: for
$U=\{z:|z|<2\}\cup\{z:|z-10|<1\}$, with $f=1$ on the first disc and $f(z)=z$ on the second, $f$
is non-constant and holomorphic on $U$ and has modulus one on the unit circle, but $f(U)$ does not
contain the open unit disc.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; General properties of functions of one complex variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_25`, with the change above.

articles.title: A Möbius map from the unit disk onto the upper half-plane
articles.statement:
The function
$\phi(z) = i\,\frac{1-z}{1+z}$ maps the open unit disk $D = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$
bijectively onto the upper half-plane $U = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im} z > 0\}$: it
maps $D$ into $U$, it is injective on $D$, and every point of $U$ is $\phi(z)$ for some $z \in D$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_63`.

articles.title: Bloch's theorem
articles.statement:
There is a constant $B > 0$ with the following property. Let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$
with $f'(0) = 1$. Then there are an open connected set $V \subseteq \mathbb{D}$ and a point
$w \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $f$ is injective on $V$ and $f(V)$ is the open disc
$\{\zeta : |\zeta - w| < B\}$.

## Sources

- A. Bloch, Les théorèmes de M. Valiron sur les fonctions entières et la théorie de l'uniformisation, Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse 17 (1925), 1–22, DOI 10.5802/afst.335; see Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, Univalent Functions; Lean is universal B > 0 exact schlicht disc f '' V = ball w B for open connected V, stronger than Landau.

articles.title: Sup norm of a polynomial on the unit circle
articles.statement:
For a complex polynomial $Q$, this is the
real number $\sup_{|z| = 1} |Q(z)|$, the supremum of $|Q(z)|$ over all $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with
$|z| = 1$.

## Sources

- [AMR-022-6028] Problem 6.28.

articles.title: Normalized univalent functions with their Taylor coefficients
articles.statement:
An element of the class
$S$ is a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ together with a sequence $(a_m)_{m \ge 0}$ of
complex numbers such that $f$ is holomorphic and injective on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ of
all $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|z| < 1$, $f(0) = 0$, $f'(0) = 1$, $a_0 = 0$, $a_1 = 1$, and for every
$z \in \mathbb{D}$ the series $\sum_{m \ge 0} a_m z^m$ is unconditionally summable with sum $f(z)$.

## Sources

- [AMR-022-6028] Problem 6.28.

articles.title: Hadamard product circle bound for univalent functions
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every
function $f(z) = \sum_{m \ge 0} a_m z^m$ of the class $S$ of normalized univalent functions on the
unit disk, and every complex polynomial $P(z) = \sum_k p_k z^k$ of degree at most $n$,

$$
\sup_{|z| = 1} \Bigl| \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k p_k z^k \Bigr| \le n \sup_{|z| = 1} |P(z)|.
$$

Robertson's conjecture implies the bound (Sheil-Small, J. Reine Angew. Math. 258 (1973)), and de
Branges (Acta Math. 154 (1985)) proved Milin's conjecture, hence Robertson's. Both facts are
recorded in Hayman-Lingham (arXiv:1809.07200, Problem 6.28, Update 6.1).

## Sources

- Walter K. Hayman and Eleanor F. Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition), arXiv:1809.07200v2 (2018), https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Statement of the Hadamard product circle bound
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, every function $f(z) = \sum_{m \ge 0} a_m z^m$ of the class $S$ of normalized
univalent functions on the unit disk, and every complex polynomial $P(z) = \sum_k p_k z^k$ of
degree at most $n$,

$$
\sup_{|z| = 1} \Bigl| \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k p_k z^k \Bigr| \le n \sup_{|z| = 1} |P(z)|.
$$

## Sources

- [AMR-022-6028] Problem 6.28, where it is posed as an open question.

articles.title: Truncated Hadamard product with a polynomial
articles.statement:
For a sequence $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ of complex
numbers, a complex polynomial $P(z) = \sum_k p_k z^k$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the
polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k p_k z^k$: the coefficient-wise (Hadamard) product of $P$ with the
power series $\sum_k a_k z^k$, truncated at degree $n$.

## Sources

- [AMR-022-6028] Problem 6.28.

articles.title: The open unit disc $D$
articles.statement:
The set $D=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ is the open disc of radius $1$
about $0$.

articles.title: Growth bound for holomorphic maps from the unit disc into a vertical strip
articles.statement:
Let
$D=\{z:|z|<1\}\subset\mathbb{C}$ be the unit disk and $g:D\to\mathbb{C}$ be a holomorphic
function such that $g(0)=0$ and $|\operatorname{Re} g(z)|<1$ for any $z\in D$. Then for any
$z\in D$,
\[
|g(z)|\le \frac{2}{\pi}\log\frac{1+|z|}{1-|z|}.
\]

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_86`.

articles.title: Agreement of two motions on a set
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ be the open unit disc, $E$ a set of
complex numbers, and $F$ and $G$ functions assigning complex numbers $F(w, z)$ and $G(w, z)$ to
each pair of complex numbers $w, z$. Then $G$ agrees with $F$ on $E$ when $G(w, z) = F(w, z)$
for every $w \in E$ and every $z \in \mathbb{D}$.

articles.title: Holomorphic motions of planar sets extend to the plane
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ be the open unit
disc, $E$ a set of complex numbers and $F$ a function assigning a complex number $F(w, z)$ to
each pair of complex numbers $w, z$, such that (a) for every $z \in \mathbb{D}$ the map
$w \mapsto F(w, z)$ is injective on $E$, (b) for every $w \in E$ the map $z \mapsto F(w, z)$ is
analytic on $\mathbb{D}$, and (c) $F(w, 0) = w$ for every $w \in E$. Then there is a function
$G$ of the same kind that satisfies (a), (b) and (c) with $E$ replaced by $\mathbb{C}$ and has
$G(w, z) = F(w, z)$ for all $w \in E$ and all $z \in \mathbb{D}$.

This answers the extension problem for holomorphic motions affirmatively. It follows from
Słodkowski’s extended λ-lemma: every holomorphic motion over the unit disk extends to a
holomorphic motion of the Riemann sphere.

## Sources

- Zbigniew Słodkowski, Holomorphic motions and polynomial hulls, Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 111 (1991), 347–355, https://doi.org/10.2307/2048323.

articles.title: Extension problem for holomorphic motions
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ be the open unit disc. The
proposition asserts the following. Let $E$ be a set of complex numbers and $F$ a function
assigning a complex number $F(w, z)$ to each pair of complex numbers $w, z$, such that (a) for
every $z \in \mathbb{D}$ the map $w \mapsto F(w, z)$ is injective on $E$, (b) for every
$w \in E$ the map $z \mapsto F(w, z)$ is analytic on $\mathbb{D}$, and (c) $F(w, 0) = w$ for
every $w \in E$. Then there is a function $G$ of the same kind that satisfies (a), (b) and (c)
with $E$ replaced by $\mathbb{C}$ and has $G(w, z) = F(w, z)$ for all $w \in E$ and all
$z \in \mathbb{D}$.

Conditions (a), (b) and (c) say that $F$ is a holomorphic motion of $E$ over $\mathbb{D}$; the
question, due to Sullivan, Thurston and Royden, is whether every such motion extends to a
holomorphic motion of the whole plane.

## Sources

- AMR-022-7082, Problem 7.82.

articles.title: Holomorphic dependence of a motion on the parameter
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ be the open unit
disc, $E$ a set of complex numbers and $F$ a function assigning a complex number $F(w, z)$ to
each pair of complex numbers $w, z$. Condition (b) holds for $E$ and $F$ when, for every
$w \in E$, the map $z \mapsto F(w, z)$ is analytic on $\mathbb{D}$.

This is condition (b) of Problem 7.82 in AMR-022-7082.

articles.title: Injectivity at each parameter of the disc
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ be the open unit disc, $E$ a
set of complex numbers and $F$ a function assigning a complex number $F(w, z)$ to each pair of
complex numbers $w, z$. Condition (a) holds for $E$ and $F$ when, for every $z \in \mathbb{D}$,
the map $w \mapsto F(w, z)$ is injective on $E$.

This is condition (a) of Problem 7.82 in AMR-022-7082.

articles.title: Motion equal to the identity at parameter zero
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a set of complex numbers and
$F$ a function assigning a complex number $F(w, z)$ to each pair of complex numbers $w, z$.
Condition (c) holds for $E$ and $F$ when $F(w, 0) = w$ for every $w \in E$.

This is condition (c) of Problem 7.82 in AMR-022-7082.

articles.title: Open unit disc
articles.statement:
The open unit disc $\mathbb{D}$ is the set of complex numbers $z$ with
$|z| < 1$, the open ball of radius $1$ about $0$ in $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Surjectivity for half-plane self-maps that are real on the real axis
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathbb{C}_{+} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im} z > 0\}$ be the open upper half-plane and
$\overline{\mathbb{C}_{+}} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im} z \ge 0\}$ the closed one. Let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous on $\overline{\mathbb{C}_{+}}$ with
$f(\overline{\mathbb{C}_{+}}) \subseteq \overline{\mathbb{C}_{+}}$, suppose $f(x)$ is real for
every real $x$, and suppose $f$ is holomorphic on $\mathbb{C}_{+}$ and not constant on
$\mathbb{C}_{+}$. Then $f(\mathbb{C}_{+}) = \mathbb{C}_{+}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_71`.

articles.title: Derivative bound at $i$ for a self-map of the upper half-plane
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathbb{H}=\{z\in\mathbb{C} : \mathrm{Im}\,z>0\}$ be the upper half-plane, and let $f$ be a
complex function that is holomorphic on $\mathbb{H}$, maps $\mathbb{H}$ into $\mathbb{H}$, and
satisfies $f(i)=e^{2\pi i/3}$. Then $|f'(i)|\le\sqrt{3/2}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_62`.

articles.title: Schwarz lemma on the upper half-plane
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathbb{H}=\{z\in\mathbb{C} : \mathrm{Im}\,z>0\}$ be the upper half-plane, and let $F$ be a
complex function that is holomorphic on $\mathbb{H}$, satisfies $|F(z)|\le 1$ for every
$z\in\mathbb{H}$, and vanishes at $i$. Then for every $z\in\mathbb{H}$,

$$|F(z)|\le\left|\frac{z-i}{z+i}\right|.$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_20`.

articles.title: Iterates of a self-map of the upper half-plane fixing $i$
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathbb{H}=\{z\in\mathbb{C} : \mathrm{Im}\,z>0\}$ be the upper half-plane, and let $f$ be a
complex function that is holomorphic on $\mathbb{H}$, maps $\mathbb{H}$ into $\mathbb{H}$, and
satisfies $f(i)=i$ and $f(2i)=\frac{15}{8}i$. Then the iterates $f^{\circ n}(2i)$ converge to $i$
as $n\to\infty$, where $f^{\circ n}$ is the $n$-fold composite of $f$ with itself.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_34`.

articles.title: The boundary of a normalized univalent image of the disc is within distance one of the origin
articles.statement:
**The boundary of a normalized univalent image of the disc is within distance one of the
origin.** Let $D=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the unit disk and suppose $f:D\to\mathbb{C}$ is an
injective holomorphic function with $f(0)=0$ and $f'(0)=1$. Let $\Omega=f(D)$ and let
$\partial\Omega$ be its boundary. Then
$\mathrm{dist}(0,\partial\Omega)=\inf\{|z|:z\in\partial\Omega\}\le 1$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_18`.

articles.title: Koebe quarter theorem
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic and injective on the
open unit disk $\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$, with $f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = 1$. Then the image
$f(\mathbb{D})$ contains the open disk $\{w : |w| < 1/4\}$.

## Sources

- Koebe quarter theorem, conjectured by P. Koebe in 1907 and proved by L. Bieberbach, Sitzungsberichte der Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften (1916), 940–955; see Pommerenke, Univalent Functions; Lean is normalized schlicht inclusion ball (0:ℂ) (1/4) ⊆ f '' ball 0 1.

articles.title: Closed upper half-plane
articles.statement: The closed upper half-plane `{z : 0 ≤ Im z}`.

articles.title: Complement of a compact hull is connected
articles.statement: The complement of a compact `ℍ`-hull is connected.

articles.title: Hydrodynamic normalization with half-plane capacity
articles.statement:
`g` is hydrodynamically normalized at infinity with half-plane capacity `a`: `g(z) - z → 0`
and `z (g(z) - z) → a` as `z → ∞`, i.e. `g(z) = z + a/z + o(1/z)`.

articles.title: Forward extension of a Loewner trajectory
articles.statement:
The Loewner trajectory from `z` extends in `ℍ` beyond time `t`. This is the intrinsic
maximal-lifetime condition used to determine the unswallowed domain.

articles.title: Chordal Schramm–Loewner evolution
articles.statement:
`(D, g)` is chordal SLE`_κ` in `ℍ` from `0` to `∞`: `κ ≥ 0`, `B` is a standard Brownian
motion and almost surely `g` solves the maximal Loewner equation with driving function `√κ B`.
This is a definition only; existence of SLE is not proved.

articles.title: Compact hull in the upper half-plane
articles.statement:
A compact `ℍ`-hull: a bounded subset `K` of `ℍ`, relatively closed in `ℍ`, whose complement
`ℍ \ K` is open and simply connected.

articles.title: Solution of the Loewner equation at a time
articles.statement: `t ↦ g_t(z)` satisfies the Loewner equation `∂_t g_t(z) = 2 / (g_t(z) - W_t)` at time `t`.

articles.title: Solution of the Loewner equation on a set of times
articles.statement: `t ↦ g_t(z)` satisfies the Loewner equation on `s` (derivatives within `s`).

articles.title: The upper half-plane is simply connected
articles.statement: The complex upper half-plane is simply connected.

articles.title: Standard real Brownian motion
articles.statement:
A standard real Brownian motion indexed by `ℝ` (used for `t ≥ 0`): `B_0 = 0` a.s., continuous
paths a.s., Gaussian, with independent increments `B_t - B_s ~ N(0, t - s)`.

See also Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.IsPreBrownianReal` (time `ℝ≥0`, finite-dimensional laws).

articles.title: Chordal Loewner vector field
articles.statement: The chordal Loewner vector field `w ↦ 2 / (w - W_t)` at time `t`.

articles.title: Real axis in the complex plane
articles.statement: The real axis `{z : Im z = 0}` in `ℂ`.

articles.title: Loewner equation without domain restriction
articles.statement:
`g_0 = id` and `t ↦ g_t(z)` solves the Loewner equation for every `z ∈ ℂ` and every `t ≥ 0`,
with no domain restriction (compare `SatisfiesMaximalLoewnerEquation`, where `z` ranges over the
unswallowed domain `D_t`).

articles.title: Maximal chordal Loewner evolution
articles.statement:
The maximal chordal Loewner evolution with domains `D_t`. The domains are exactly the points
whose trajectories extend beyond `t`, and `g_t : D_t → ℍ` is a conformal bijection.

articles.title: SLE driving function
articles.statement: The SLE`_κ` driving function `W_t = √κ B_t(ω)`.

articles.title: Half-plane capacity rate of a Loewner family
articles.statement: The family `g_t` has half-plane capacity `a t` for every `t ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Additivity of half-plane capacity under composition
articles.statement: Half-plane capacity is additive under composition: `hcap(f ∘ g) = hcap(f) + hcap(g)`.

articles.title: Reflection across the imaginary axis
articles.statement: The reflection `z ↦ -z̄` across the imaginary axis.

articles.title: Increasing family of compact hulls
articles.statement: An increasing family `(K_t)` of compact `ℍ`-hulls.

articles.title: Local existence for the chordal Loewner equation
articles.statement:
For continuous `W` and `Im z > 0` there
are `ε > 0` and `g` with `g 0 = z`, `ġ(t) = 2 / (g(t) - W_t)` on `[0, ε]` (one-sided derivatives
at the endpoints), and `g(t) ∈ ℍ` on `[0, ε]` (Lawler 2005, Chapter 4).

articles.title: Local existence and uniqueness for the chordal Loewner equation
articles.statement:
Local existence and uniqueness for the chordal Loewner equation: the solution from
`loewner_local_existence` is the unique continuous solution on `[0, ε]` with right derivatives on
`[0, ε)` that stays in `ℍ`.

articles.title: Lipschitz Picard–Lindelöf flow confined to a ball
articles.statement:
Picard–Lindelöf local flow, Lipschitz in the initial point, with every trajectory in
`closedBall x₀ a`: a strengthening of Mathlib's
`IsPicardLindelof.exists_forall_mem_closedBall_eq_hasDerivWithinAt_lipschitzOnWith` by the ball
bound.

articles.title: Picard–Lindelöf theorem with solutions confined to a ball
articles.statement:
Picard–Lindelöf with the solution confined to `closedBall x₀ a`: a strengthening of Mathlib's
`IsPicardLindelof.exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt₀` by the bound
`α t ∈ closedBall x₀ a` for all `t`.

articles.title: Closed half-plane above a horizontal line
articles.statement: The closed strip `{w ∈ ℂ : δ ≤ Im w}`.

articles.title: Concatenated curve of two Loewner solutions
articles.statement: The concatenation of `g` on `[0, S]` with a solution `h` started from `g_S(z)` at time `S`.

articles.title: Concatenation of Loewner forward solutions
articles.statement: The concatenation of two forward solutions, a forward solution on `[0, S + T]`.

articles.title: Times before the Loewner lifetime
Admissible duration for the Loewner equation
articles.statement: `T > 0` and there is a forward solution from `z` on `[0, T]`.

articles.title: The unswallowed domain is simply connected
articles.statement: The unswallowed domain is simply connected.

articles.title: Forward solution of the Loewner equation
articles.statement:
A solution `t ↦ g_t(z)` of the Loewner equation on `[0, T]` (one-sided derivatives at the
endpoints) with `g_0(z) = z` and `g_t(z) ∈ ℍ` for `t ∈ [0, T]`.

articles.title: Lifetime of a point under the Loewner flow
articles.statement: The lifetime `T_z ∈ [0, ∞]` of `z`: the supremum of admissible durations.

articles.title: Maximal Loewner trajectory
articles.statement:
The maximal solution `t ↦ g_t(z)` for `0 ≤ t < T_z` (independent of choices by uniqueness);
it is `z` outside `[0, T_z)`.

articles.title: Maximal solution of the chordal Loewner equation
articles.statement:
For continuous `W` and `z ∈ ℍ`, the
lifetime `T_z` is positive, `g_0(z) = z`, `g_t(z) ∈ ℍ` for `0 ≤ t < T_z`, the equation holds at
`t = 0` from the right and at every `0 < t < T_z` (Lawler 2005, Chapter 4).

articles.title: Loewner map as a homeomorphism onto the half-plane
articles.statement: `g_t` as a homeomorphism `H_t ≃ₜ ℍ`.

articles.title: Inverse of the maximal Loewner map
articles.statement: The inverse `g_t⁻¹ : ℍ → H_t` (`0` outside `ℍ`).

articles.title: Maximal Loewner maps solve the maximal Loewner equation
articles.statement: The canonical maximal family has the exact lifetime domains and conformal Loewner maps.

articles.title: Maximal Loewner maps
articles.statement: The Loewner map `g_t(z)`, the maximal solution at time `t`.

articles.title: Loewner hulls are compact hulls
articles.statement:
For continuous `W` and `t ≥ 0`, the Loewner hull `K_t` is a compact `ℍ`-hull (Lawler 2005,
Chapter 4; the capacity normalization is not proved).

articles.title: Loewner hull
articles.statement: The Loewner hull `K_t = ℍ \ H_t` of points swallowed by time `t`.

articles.title: Unswallowed domain equals the forward-extension domain
articles.statement: The lifetime-defined unswallowed domain is exactly the intrinsic forward-extension domain.

articles.title: Unswallowed domain of the Loewner flow
articles.statement: The domain `H_t = {z ∈ ℍ : t < T_z}` of points not swallowed by time `t`.

articles.title: Positivity persists under a nonnegative derivative
articles.statement:
A continuous function on `[0, T]` that is positive at `0` and has a nonnegative derivative at
every interior point where it is positive stays positive on `[0, T]`.

articles.title: Reflection of a Loewner forward solution
articles.statement: The reflected solution `-conj g_t(z)`, a forward solution for the driving function `-W`.

articles.title: Restriction of a Loewner forward solution
articles.statement: The restriction of a forward solution to `[0, S]`, `S ≤ T`.

articles.title: Chosen admissible Loewner duration
articles.statement: A chosen admissible duration exceeding `t`, for `t` before the lifetime.

articles.title: Chosen Loewner forward solution
articles.statement: A chosen forward solution on `[0, selectedLoewnerDuration ht]`.

articles.title: Time shift of a Loewner forward solution
articles.statement:
The solution restarted at time `s`: `u ↦ g_{s+u}(z)`, for the driving function
`u ↦ W(s + u)`.

articles.title: No proper holomorphic map from the unit disc to the complex plane
articles.statement:
Let
$\Delta := \{z\in\mathbb{C}\mid |z|<1\}$ be the unit disc in the complex plane. There is no proper
holomorphic map $f:\Delta\to\mathbb{C}$, where proper means that the preimage under $f$ of every
compact subset of $\mathbb{C}$ is a compact subset of $\Delta$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_41`.

articles.title: A sharp radius of convexity for starlike functions of order 1/2 exists
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ be
the open unit disc in $\mathbb{C}$. Call $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ a normalized starlike
function of order $1/2$ if $f$ is holomorphic and injective on $\mathbb{D}$, $f(0) = 0$,
$f'(0) = 1$, and $\operatorname{Re}(z f'(z)/f(z)) \ge 1/2$ for every $z \in \mathbb{D}$ with
$z \ne 0$ and $f(z) \ne 0$. Call $P : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ a Carathéodory function if $P$
is holomorphic on $\mathbb{D}$, $P(0) = 1$, and $\operatorname{Re} P(z) > 0$ for every
$z \in \mathbb{D}$. Call a real number $\rho$ a good radius if
$\operatorname{Re}(1 + z f''(z)/f'(z)) > 0$ for every normalized starlike function $f$ of order
$1/2$ and every $z$ with $0 < |z| < \rho$ and $f'(z) \ne 0$, and
$\operatorname{Re}\big((P(z) + 1)/2 + z P'(z)/(P(z) + 1)\big) > 0$ for every Carathéodory
function $P$ and every $z$ with $|z| < \rho$. Then there is a good radius $r$ with
$0 < r \le 1$ such that no real $r'$ with $r < r' \le 1$ is a good radius.

MacGregor (Proc. AMS 14 (1963) 71-76, Theorem 1) proved that the sharp radius of convexity of
normalized starlike functions of order $1/2$ is $\sqrt{2\sqrt{3}-3} \approx 0.681$; this value is
such a radius $r$. The statement above does not assert the value of $r$.

## Sources

- B. Bhowmik and S. Biswas, Radius of convexity of certain classes of functions defined by convolution, preprint (2026), arXiv:2606.20872, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20872.

articles.title: Conjecture: a sharp radius of convexity for starlike functions of order 1/2
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathbb{D}$ be the open unit disc in $\mathbb{C}$. Call $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ a
normalized starlike function of order $1/2$ if $f$ is holomorphic and injective on $\mathbb{D}$,
$f(0) = 0$, $f'(0) = 1$, and $\operatorname{Re}(z f'(z)/f(z)) \ge 1/2$ for every $z \in \mathbb{D}$
with $z \ne 0$ and $f(z) \ne 0$. Call $P : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ a Carathéodory function if
$P$ is holomorphic on $\mathbb{D}$, $P(0) = 1$, and $\operatorname{Re} P(z) > 0$ for every
$z \in \mathbb{D}$. Call a real number $\rho$ a good radius if
$\operatorname{Re}(1 + z f''(z)/f'(z)) > 0$ for every normalized starlike function $f$ of order
$1/2$ and every $z$ with $0 < |z| < \rho$ and $f'(z) \ne 0$, and
$\operatorname{Re}\big((P(z) + 1)/2 + z P'(z)/(P(z) + 1)\big) > 0$ for every Carathéodory
function $P$ and every $z$ with $|z| < \rho$. The conjecture is the proposition that there is a
good radius $r$ with $0 < r \le 1$ such that no real number $r'$ with $r < r' \le 1$ is a good
radius.

This is Problem 6.22 of Hayman, Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), source record
AMR-022-6022.

## Sources

- https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200

articles.title: Admissible maps into the unit disc
articles.statement:
For a set $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, the
admissible family of $\Omega$ is the set of functions $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that are
complex differentiable on $\Omega$, injective on $\Omega$, satisfy $f(0) = 0$, and map $\Omega$
into the open unit disc $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$.

articles.title: Existence of an extremal injective map into the unit disc
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be the open unit disc
$\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, let $\Omega \subseteq D$ be open and connected with
$0 \in \Omega$, and let $F$ be the family of functions $f$ that are holomorphic and injective on
$\Omega$, map $\Omega$ into $D$, and satisfy $f(0) = 0$. Then some $g \in F$ attains the supremum
of $|f'(0)|$ over $F$:

$$|g'(0)| = \sup_{f \in F} |f'(0)|.$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_22`.

articles.title: Riemann mapping theorem
articles.statement:
Let $U$ be a simply connected open subset of $\mathbb{C}$ with
$U \ne \mathbb{C}$, and let $z_0 \in U$. Then there is a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$,
holomorphic on $U$, that maps $U$ bijectively onto the open unit disc $\{w : |w| < 1\}$, with
$f(z_0) = 0$ and $f'(z_0)$ a positive real number. It is unique on $U$: every function
$g : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with the same four properties agrees with $f$ at every point of $U$.

## Sources

- same as Riemann mapping; B. Riemann thesis 1851; W. F. Osgood Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 1 (1900), 310–314, DOI 10.2307/1986285; C. Carathéodory Math. Ann. 72 (1912), 107–144, DOI 10.1007/BF01456892; Ahlfors; Lean adds f z₀=0 positive real derivative via im=0 re>0 and EqOn uniqueness on U.

articles.title: Open unit disc
articles.statement:
The open unit disc is the set of complex numbers $z$ with $|z| < 1$, the
open ball of radius $1$ about $0$ in $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Robertson's conjecture holds for real-coefficient and close-to-convex functions
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$. For all functions $f, h : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
such that $f$ belongs to the class $S$ (analytic at every point of $\mathbb{D}$, injective on
$\mathbb{D}$, $f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = 1$), $h$ is a normalized odd square root of $f(z^2)$ (analytic
at every point of $\mathbb{D}$, with $h(z)^2 = f(z^2)$ and $h(-z) = -h(z)$ for all
$z \in \mathbb{D}$, $h(0) = 0$ and $h'(0) = 1$), and $f$ has real Taylor coefficients at $0$ or is
close-to-convex, the Taylor coefficients $c_k = h^{(k)}(0)/k!$ of $h$ at $0$ satisfy
$|c_1|^2 + |c_3|^2 + \dots + |c_{2n-1}|^2 \le n$ for every integer $n \ge 1$.

De Branges' 1985 proof of the Milin conjecture implies the Robertson bound for every normalized
univalent function, hence for the real-coefficient and close-to-convex subclasses formalized here.

## Sources

- de Branges, L., A proof of the Bieberbach conjecture, Acta Math. 154 (1985), 137-152, https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02392821.

articles.title: Robertson's conjecture for real-coefficient and close-to-convex functions
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$. The statement that for all functions
$f, h : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that $f$ belongs to the class $S$ (analytic at every point
of $\mathbb{D}$, injective on $\mathbb{D}$, $f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = 1$), $h$ is a normalized odd
square root of $f(z^2)$ (analytic at every point of $\mathbb{D}$, with $h(z)^2 = f(z^2)$ and
$h(-z) = -h(z)$ for all $z \in \mathbb{D}$, $h(0) = 0$ and $h'(0) = 1$), and $f$ has real Taylor
coefficients at $0$ or is close-to-convex, the Taylor coefficients $c_k = h^{(k)}(0)/k!$ of $h$ at
$0$ satisfy $|c_1|^2 + |c_3|^2 + \dots + |c_{2n-1}|^2 \le n$ for every integer $n \ge 1$.

Resolved true: de Branges (1985) proved the bound for every function in $S$ via the Milin
conjecture.

## Sources

- AMR-022-6039, Hayman Problem 6.39, arXiv:1809.07200.

articles.title: Real Taylor coefficients at the origin
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has real
Taylor coefficients at $0$ when, for every natural number $n$, the value $f^{(n)}(0)$ of its $n$-th
iterated derivative at $0$ is real (equivalently, every Taylor coefficient $f^{(n)}(0)/n!$ is real).

## Sources

- AMR-022-6039, Hayman Problem 6.39, arXiv:1809.07200.

articles.title: Close-to-convex functions
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is close-to-convex
when it belongs to the class $S$ (analytic at every point of the open unit disc
$\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, injective on $\mathbb{D}$, $f(0) = 0$ and
$f'(0) = 1$) and there are a starlike function $g$ and a real number $\alpha$ such that
$\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e^{i\alpha} z f'(z) / g(z)\bigr) > 0$ for every $z \in \mathbb{D}$ with
$z \ne 0$. Here $g$ is starlike when it belongs to $S$ and
$\operatorname{Re}\bigl(z g'(z) / g(z)\bigr) > 0$ for every $z \in \mathbb{D}$ with $z \ne 0$.

## Sources

- AMR-022-6039, Hayman Problem 6.39, arXiv:1809.07200.

articles.title: Normalized odd square roots
articles.statement:
Given $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, a function
$h : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is a normalized odd square root $h(z) = f(z^2)^{1/2}$ when, on the
open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, $h$ is analytic at every point and
satisfies $h(z)^2 = f(z^2)$ and $h(-z) = -h(z)$ for all $z \in \mathbb{D}$, and moreover $h(0) = 0$
and $h'(0) = 1$.

## Sources

- AMR-022-6039, Hayman Problem 6.39, arXiv:1809.07200.

articles.title: Normalized univalent functions (class $S$)
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
belongs to the class $S$ when it is analytic at every point of the open unit disc
$\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, injective on $\mathbb{D}$, and satisfies $f(0) = 0$
and $f'(0) = 1$.

## Sources

- AMR-022-6039, Hayman Problem 6.39, arXiv:1809.07200.

articles.title: Starlike univalent functions
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is starlike when it
belongs to the class $S$ (analytic at every point of the open unit disc
$\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, injective on $\mathbb{D}$, $f(0) = 0$ and
$f'(0) = 1$) and $\operatorname{Re}\bigl(z f'(z) / f(z)\bigr) > 0$ for every $z \in \mathbb{D}$
with $z \ne 0$.

## Sources

- AMR-022-6039, Hayman Problem 6.39, arXiv:1809.07200.

articles.title: Taylor coefficients at the origin
articles.statement:
For a function $h : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a
natural number $n$, $c_n(h) = h^{(n)}(0) / n!$, where $h^{(n)}$ is the $n$-th iterated derivative
of $h$. For $h$ analytic near $0$ this is the $n$-th Taylor coefficient of $h$ at $0$; Robertson's
problem uses it at odd $n$.

## Sources

- AMR-022-6039, Hayman Problem 6.39, arXiv:1809.07200.

articles.title: Robertson's bound
articles.statement:
For a function $h : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients
$c_k = h^{(k)}(0)/k!$ at $0$ and a natural number $n$, the Robertson bound for $h$ at $n$ is the
inequality $|c_1|^2 + |c_3|^2 + \dots + |c_{2n-1}|^2 \le n$ (for $n = 0$ the sum is empty).

## Sources

- AMR-022-6039, Hayman Problem 6.39, arXiv:1809.07200.

articles.title: Open unit disc
articles.statement:
The open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ in the
complex plane.

## Sources

- AMR-022-6039, Hayman Problem 6.39, arXiv:1809.07200.

articles.title: Schwarz–Pick lemma, derivative form
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open
unit disc. If $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{D}$ is holomorphic, then

\[
\frac{|f'(z)|}{1-|f(z)|^2}\le \frac{1}{1-|z|^2}\qquad\text{for all } z\in\mathbb{D}.
\]

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; Geometric function theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_86`.

articles.title: Schwarz–Pick lemma
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on the open unit disc
$\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$ and map $\mathbb{D}$ into itself. Then for all $z, w \in \mathbb{D}$,
$|f(z) - f(w)| / |1 - \overline{f(w)}\, f(z)| \le |z - w| / |1 - \bar w z|$.

## Sources

- Schwarz–Pick lemma, G. Pick (1916), building on Schwarz's lemma; see Ahlfors; Lean is holomorphic self-map of disc pseudo-hyperbolic distance nonincreasing inequality with star conj.

articles.title: Leung's theorem on successive coefficients of starlike functions
articles.statement:
Let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$,
with $f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = 1$, injective on $\mathbb{D}$, and starlike, meaning that
$\operatorname{Re}\bigl(z f'(z) / f(z)\bigr) > 0$ for every $z \ne 0$ in $\mathbb{D}$. Let
$a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ be the Taylor coefficients of $f$ at $0$. Then
$\bigl| |a_{n+1}| - |a_n| \bigr| \le 1$ for every natural number $n \ge 1$.

This answers Problem 6.46 of Hayman and Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory (2018),
affirmatively. It was proved by Y. Leung (Bull. London Math. Soc. 10 (1978), 193-196) and
independently by D. H. Hamilton.

## Sources

- Moduli difference of initial inverse logarithmic coefficients for starlike and convex functions (2026), arXiv:2603.17600, https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17600.

articles.title: Hayman's successive coefficient problem for starlike functions
articles.statement:
The statement that for
every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ in the class $S$ (analytic on the open unit disc
$\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$, with $f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = 1$, and injective on $\mathbb{D}$)
that is moreover starlike ($\operatorname{Re}\bigl(z f'(z) / f(z)\bigr) > 0$ for every $z \ne 0$
in $\mathbb{D}$), the Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ of $f$ at $0$ satisfy
$\bigl| |a_{n+1}| - |a_n| \bigr| \le 1$ for every natural number $n \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Hayman and Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 6.46, https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Normalized univalent functions (the class $S$)
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
is in the class $S$ when it is analytic on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$,
satisfies $f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = 1$, and is injective on $\mathbb{D}$.

## Sources

- Hayman and Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 6.46, https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Starlike functions on the unit disc
articles.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is
starlike when it is analytic on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$ and, for every
$z \ne 0$ in $\mathbb{D}$, $f(z) \ne 0$ and $\operatorname{Re}\bigl(z f'(z) / f(z)\bigr) > 0$.

## Sources

- Hayman, Research Problems in Function Theory (2018), Problem 6.46, https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200.

articles.title: Diameter bound for the derivative at the center of the disc
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be the open unit disc
in $\mathbb{C}$ and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on $D$. Then the diameter
$d = \sup_{z,w \in D} |f(z) - f(w)|$ of the image $f(D)$, which may be $+\infty$, satisfies
$2|f'(0)| \le d$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functions of a complex variable; General properties of functions of one complex variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_78`.

articles.title: Constant functions have zero complex Hessian
articles.statement:
For every real constant $c$, the function
$u : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ with constant value $c$ has complex Hessian equal to the zero
$n \times n$ matrix at every point $z \in \mathbb{C}^n$.

articles.title: Complex Hessian
articles.statement:
Let $u : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}^n$, write
$e_1, \dots, e_n$ for the standard basis of $\mathbb{C}^n$, write $i$ for the imaginary unit, and
for $a, b \in \mathbb{C}^n$ write $D^2u(z)(a, b)$ for the real Hessian of $u$ at $z$. The complex
Hessian of $u$ at $z$ is the $n \times n$ complex matrix whose $(j, k)$ entry is

$$
u_{j\bar k}(z) = \frac{D^2u(z)(e_j, e_k) + D^2u(z)(i e_j, i e_k) +
i \left(D^2u(z)(e_j, i e_k) - D^2u(z)(i e_j, e_k)\right)}{4}.
$$

When $u$ is of class $C^2$, in real coordinates $z_j = x_j + i y_j$ this is
$\partial^2 u / \partial z_j \partial \bar z_k =
(u_{x_j x_k} + u_{y_j y_k} + i (u_{x_j y_k} - u_{y_j x_k})) / 4$.

articles.title: Constant functions have zero real Hessian
articles.statement:
For every real constant $c$, the function
$u : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ with constant value $c$ has real Hessian $D^2u(z)(a, b) = 0$ for
all $z, a, b \in \mathbb{C}^n$.

articles.title: Real Hessian
articles.statement:
For a function $u : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, with $\mathbb{C}^n$
viewed as a real normed space, write $Du(w)$ for the real Fréchet derivative of $u$ at $w$. For
points $z, a, b \in \mathbb{C}^n$, the real Hessian $D^2u(z)(a, b)$ is the real number obtained
by taking the real Fréchet derivative at $z$ of the map $w \mapsto Du(w)$, applying it to $a$,
and applying the result to $b$.

As usual in Mathlib, a derivative that does not exist is taken to be zero.

articles.title: Vanishing of the Wirtinger derivative at points of complex differentiability
articles.statement:
Let
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$. If $f$ is complex differentiable at $z$,
then the Wirtinger derivative $\partial f / \partial \bar z$ of $f$ vanishes at $z$.

articles.title: The Wirtinger derivative with respect to z̄
articles.statement:
For $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and
$z \in \mathbb{C}$, the Wirtinger derivative of $f$ at $z$ is
$\frac{\partial f}{\partial \bar z}(z) = \frac{1}{2}\bigl(Df(z)(1) + i\,Df(z)(i)\bigr)$, where
$Df(z)$ is the real derivative of $f$ at $z$, taken to be $0$ when $f$ is not real differentiable
at $z$. When $f$ is real differentiable at $z$, this equals
$\frac{1}{2}\bigl(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}(z) + i\,\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}(z)\bigr)$.

articles.title: Holomorphic functions on open subsets of ℂⁿ have continuous derivative
articles.statement:
Let $n \in
\mathbb{N}$, let $s$ be an open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$ and let $f : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$
be complex differentiable at every point of $s$. Then the complex derivative $x \mapsto Df(x)$,
with values in the complex linear maps $\mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$, is continuous on $s$. Here
$\mathbb{C}^n$ carries the Euclidean norm.

articles.title: Cauchy–Riemann criterion for complex differentiability
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to
\mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$. If $f$ is real differentiable at $z$ and its Wirtinger
derivative $\partial f / \partial \bar z$ vanishes at $z$, then $f$ is complex differentiable at
$z$.

articles.title: Solving the ∂̄-equation for compactly supported C¹ data
articles.statement:
Let $g : \mathbb{C} \to
\mathbb{C}$ be real differentiable on all of $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous real derivative and
compact support. Then there is a function $u : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, real differentiable on
all of $\mathbb{C}$, whose Wirtinger derivative satisfies
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial \bar z}(z) = g(z)$ for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Hartogs extension theorem
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 2$, let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n$ be open and
connected, and let $K \subseteq U$ be compact with $U \setminus K$ connected. Then for every
function $f : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ that is holomorphic on $U \setminus K$ there is a
function $F : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ that is holomorphic on $U$ and agrees with $f$ on
$U \setminus K$. Here $\mathbb{C}^n$ carries the Euclidean norm.

Proof: The compactly supported Cauchy–Green equation in one coordinate, combined with a smooth
cutoff and one-variable identity continuation.

## Sources

- Hartogs extension phenomenon, F. Hartogs, Math. Ann. 62 (1906); see Hörmander, An Introduction to Complex Analysis in Several Variables; Lean is ℂⁿ n ≥ 2 finite-dimensional form via EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) with U open connected K compact U\K connected.

articles.title: Osgood's lemma for functions bounded on open sets
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex normed space and
let $f(z, w)$ be a complex-valued function of $z \in E$ and $w \in \mathbb{C}$ such that
$z \mapsto f(z, w)$ is complex differentiable on all of $E$ for every $w \in \mathbb{C}$ and
$w \mapsto f(z, w)$ is complex differentiable on all of $\mathbb{C}$ for every $z \in E$. Let
$U \subseteq E$ and $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open sets and $M$ a real number with
$|f(z, w)| \le M$ for all $z \in U$ and $w \in V$. Then $f$, as a function on
$E \times \mathbb{C}$, is complex differentiable at every point $(z_0, w_0)$ with $z_0 \in U$ and
$w_0 \in V$.

articles.title: Osgood's lemma at the origin
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a complex normed space and let $f(z, w)$ be a
complex-valued function of $z \in E$ and $w \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $z \mapsto f(z, w)$ is
complex differentiable on all of $E$ for every $w \in \mathbb{C}$ and $w \mapsto f(z, w)$ is
complex differentiable on all of $\mathbb{C}$ for every $z \in E$. If there is a real number $M$
with $|f(z, w)| \le M$ whenever $\|z\| \le 1$ and $|w| \le 1$, then $f$, as a function on
$E \times \mathbb{C}$, is complex differentiable at $(0, 0)$.

articles.title: Holomorphic dependence of Cauchy coefficients on a parameter
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a
finite-dimensional complex normed space, let $z_0 \in E$, $w_0 \in \mathbb{C}$, $A > 0$, $B > 0$
and $M \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $f(z, w)$ be a complex-valued function of $z \in E$ and
$w \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $z \mapsto f(z, w)$ is complex differentiable on all of $E$ for every
$w$ and $w \mapsto f(z, w)$ is complex differentiable on all of $\mathbb{C}$ for every $z$.
Suppose $|f(z, w)| \le M$ whenever $\|z - z_0\| \le A$ and $|w - w_0| \le B$. Then for every
$k \in \mathbb{N}$ the $k$-th Cauchy coefficient of $f(z, \cdot)$ about $w_0$ on the circle of
radius $B/2$,

$$a_k(z) = \frac{1}{2\pi i} \oint_{|w - w_0| = B/2} \frac{f(z, w)}{(w - w_0)^{k+1}} \, dw,$$

is a complex differentiable function of $z$ on the open ball $\|z - z_0\| < A/2$.

articles.title: Hartogs' lemma for sub-mean-value functions
articles.statement:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $c \in \mathbb{C}^n$,
$R > 0$ and $C \ge 0$. For $\rho \ge 0$ write
$\overline{P}(c, \rho) = \{x \in \mathbb{C}^n : |x_j - c_j| \le \rho \text{ for all } j\}$ for the
closed polydisc, and for $x \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and $w \in \mathbb{C}$ write $x_{j \leftarrow w}$
for $x$ with its $j$-th coordinate replaced by $w$. Let $(u_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ be real-valued
functions on $\mathbb{C}^n$ such that each $u_k$ is continuous on $\overline{P}(c, R)$,
$0 \le u_k(x) \le C$ for all $k$ and all $x \in \overline{P}(c, R)$, and $u_k(x) \to 0$ as
$k \to \infty$ for every $x \in \overline{P}(c, R)$. Suppose moreover that for every $k$, every
$x \in \overline{P}(c, R)$, every coordinate $j$ and every $r > 0$ such that
$x_{j \leftarrow z} \in \overline{P}(c, R)$ for all $z$ with $|z - x_j| \le r$,

$$u_k(x) \le \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} u_k(x_{j \leftarrow x_j + r e^{i\theta}}) \, d\theta.$$

Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $K$ such that $u_k(x) \le \varepsilon$ for all
$k \ge K$ and all $x \in \overline{P}(c, R/4)$.

articles.title: Iterated integral over a polydisc
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a function
$u : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, a centre $c \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and a radius $R \in \mathbb{R}$,
the iterated polydisc integral $I(u, c, R)$ is defined by recursion on $n$. For $n = 0$ it is
$u(c)$. For $n = m + 1$, writing $c = (c_0, c_1, \dots, c_m)$, it is

$$I(u, c, R) = \int_{|z - c_0| \le R} I\big(u(z, \cdot), (c_1, \dots, c_m), R\big) \, dz,$$

where $u(z, \cdot)$ is the function $y \mapsto u(z, y)$ on $\mathbb{C}^m$ and $dz$ is Lebesgue
measure on $\mathbb{C}$. Thus, for $c = (c_0, \dots, c_{n-1})$ and $D_j$ the closed disc
$|z - c_j| \le R$,

$$I(u, c, R) = \int_{D_0} \cdots \int_{D_{n-1}} u(z_0, \dots, z_{n-1}) \, dz_{n-1} \cdots dz_0.$$

Each integral is a Bochner integral, taken to be $0$ when the integrand is not integrable.

articles.title: Sub-mean-value inequality on a polydisc
articles.statement:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let
$u : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous, let $c \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and $R > 0$. Write
$\overline{P}(c, R) = \{x \in \mathbb{C}^n : |x_j - c_j| \le R \text{ for all } j\}$ for the
closed polydisc, and for $x \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and $w \in \mathbb{C}$ write $x_{j \leftarrow w}$
for $x$ with its $j$-th coordinate replaced by $w$. Suppose that for every
$x \in \overline{P}(c, R)$, every coordinate $j$ and every $r$ with $0 < r \le R$,

$$u(x) \le \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} u(x_{j \leftarrow x_j + r e^{i\theta}}) \, d\theta.$$

Then $(\pi R^2)^n \, u(c) \le I(u, c, R)$, where $\pi R^2$ is the area of a disc of radius $R$
and $I(u, c, R)$ is the iterated polydisc integral of $u$ about $c$ with radius $R$.

articles.title: Sub-mean-value inequality for the positive logarithm of a holomorphic function
articles.statement:
Let
$c \in \mathbb{C}$, $R > 0$ and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic at every point of
the closed disc $|z - c| \le R$. Then

$$\log^+ |f(c)| \le \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} \log^+ |f(c + R e^{i\theta})| \, d\theta,$$

where $\log^+ t = \max(0, \log t)$.

articles.title: Hartogs' theorem on separate analyticity
articles.statement:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let
$f : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ be such that for every point $x \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and every
coordinate $i$, the function $z \mapsto f(x_1, \dots, x_{i-1}, z, x_{i+1}, \dots, x_n)$ is
complex differentiable on all of $\mathbb{C}$. Then $f$ is complex differentiable on all of
$\mathbb{C}^n$.

No continuity or boundedness of $f$ is assumed.

Proof: induction on the number of variables. Baire category gives a polydisc where $f$ is
bounded, where Osgood's lemma makes it holomorphic; Hartogs' lemma on sub-mean-value functions
then makes the Cauchy expansion in the last variable converge locally uniformly.

## Sources

- Hartogs separate analyticity (Osgood–Hartogs); see Hörmander; Lean is scalar-valued entire separately holomorphic via Function.update slices implies jointly Differentiable ℂ, finite-dimensional ℂⁿ specialization.

articles.title: Cauchy's estimate for Taylor coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be
complex differentiable on all of $\mathbb{C}$, let $c \in \mathbb{C}$, $R > 0$ and
$M \in \mathbb{R}$ with $|f(z)| \le M$ for all $z$ with $|z - c| = R$. Then for every
$k \in \mathbb{N}$ the $k$-th coefficient of the Cauchy power series of $f$ about $c$ on the
circle of radius $R$,

$$a_k = \frac{1}{2\pi i} \oint_{|w - c| = R} \frac{f(w)}{(w - c)^{k+1}} \, dw,$$

satisfies $|a_k| \le M R^{-k}$.

articles.title: Weierstrass preparation theorem
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional normed vector space over
$\mathbb{C}$ and let $f : E \times \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic at $0$. Suppose that for
some $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and some $g : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ analytic at $0$ with $g(0) \ne 0$,
$f(0, w) = w^d g(w)$ for all $w$ in a neighbourhood of $0$. Then there are functions
$a_0, \dots, a_{d-1} : E \to \mathbb{C}$, each analytic at $0$ with $a_j(0) = 0$, a function
$u : E \times \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ analytic at $0$ with $u(0) \ne 0$, and an open set
$U \subseteq E \times \mathbb{C}$ containing $0$ such that
$f(z, w) = u(z, w) \bigl(w^d + \sum_{j=0}^{d-1} a_j(z) w^j\bigr)$ for all $(z, w) \in U$.

## Sources

- Weierstrass preparation theorem in several complex variables; see Hörmander; Lean is finite-dimensional E × ℂ product form, order d slice factorization w^d g w, Weierstrass polynomial with vanishing coefficients and unit u, local open U, fixed field ℂ specialization.

articles.title: Eneström–Kakeya theorem
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_n$ be positive real
numbers. Then every complex zero $z$ of the polynomial $f(z) = a_0 + a_1 z + \dots + a_n z^n$
satisfies $\rho_1 \le |z| \le \rho_2$, where $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ are the minimum and the maximum
of the ratios $a_k / a_{k+1}$ for $0 \le k \le n - 1$.

## Sources

- Karl Dilcher and Larry Ericksen, "Polynomials Whose Coefficients Are Stern Numbers," Journal of Integer Sequences 24 (2021), Article 21.10.3, Theorem 4.1 (quoted there as the classical Eneström–Kakeya theorem). <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL24/Dilcher/dilcher51.tex>

articles.title: Complementary polynomial on the unit circle
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a complex polynomial with
$|P(z)| \le 1$ for every complex number $z$ with $|z| = 1$. Then there is a complex polynomial $Q$
with $\deg Q \le \deg P$ such that $|P(z)|^2 + |Q(z)|^2 = 1$ for every $z$ with $|z| = 1$. Here
the degree of the zero polynomial is taken to be $0$.

## Sources

- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-025-05302-9. Problem `exists_complementary_polynomial_on_unit_circle` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Littlewood polynomials
articles.statement:
A polynomial $P$ over a ring $F$, of degree $n$ (with the zero
polynomial taken to have degree $0$), is a Littlewood polynomial if each of its coefficients of
$X^0, X^1, \ldots, X^n$ is $1$ or $-1$.

articles.title: Flat Littlewood polynomials exist
articles.statement:
There exist real constants $\Delta > \delta > 0$ such
that for every natural number $n \ge 2$ there is a Littlewood polynomial $P$ with complex
