coefficients and of degree $n$ such that $\delta \sqrt{n} \le |P(z)| \le \Delta \sqrt{n}$ for all
$z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|z| = 1$.

## Sources

- P. Balister, B. Bollobás, R. Morris, J. Sahasrabudhe, and M. Tiba, `Flat Littlewood polynomials exist`, Annals of Math, 192 (3) 2020. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_flat_littlewood_poly` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Jentzsch's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ be complex numbers such that the power series
$\sum_{k \ge 0} a_k z^k$ has radius of convergence $1$, and for $n \ge 0$ let
$s_n(z) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k z^k$ be its $n$-th partial sum. Then for every complex $z$ with
$|z| = 1$, every real $\varepsilon > 0$ and every natural number $N$, there are $n \ge N$ and a
root $w$ of the polynomial $s_n$ with $|w - z| < \varepsilon$.

Source: Dilcher and Ericksen, "Polynomials Whose Coefficients Are Stern Numbers", Theorem 4.3
(Jentzsch), https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL24/Dilcher/dilcher51.tex, lines 381-388.

articles.title: The admissible radii are bounded below
articles.statement:
The set of admissible radii is bounded below.

Zero is a lower bound, since every admissible radius is positive.

articles.title: Admissible radius in Sendov's problem
articles.statement:
A real number $R$ is an admissible radius if
$R > 0$ and, for every integer $n \ge 2$ and every complex polynomial $f$ of degree $n$ whose
zeros all lie in the closed unit disk $|z| \le 1$, every zero $\lambda$ of $f$ has a critical
point within distance $R$, that is, a zero $c$ of the derivative $f'$ with
$|c - \lambda| \le R$.

articles.title: Lower bound one for the Sendov radius
articles.statement:
This is the proposition that the Sendov radius is at
least $1$.

The polynomials $z^n - 1$ with $n \ge 2$ give this lower bound.

articles.title: Enlarging an admissible radius
articles.statement:
If $R$ is an admissible radius and $R \le S$, then $S$ is
an admissible radius.

articles.title: Sendov's conjecture holds
articles.statement:
Sendov's conjecture is true: the Sendov radius is at most $1$.

Sendov's conjecture was resolved in 2026 by Lech Mazur's computer-assisted proof.

## Sources

- Lech Mazur, A Computer-Assisted Proof of Sendov's Conjecture, ProofAtlas, August 5, 2026, https://www.proofatlas.ai/papers/sendov-conjecture/SENDOV_CONJECTURE_PROOF_AUGUST_5_2026.pdf; teorth/sendov, Sendov's conjecture in Lean, https://github.com/teorth/sendov/blob/1ddea92d89f951a0a7cbbffa6c267cf7e6640b1d/Sendov/Conjecture.lean.

articles.title: Sendov's conjecture
articles.statement:
Sendov's conjecture is the proposition that the Sendov radius is at
most $1$.

articles.title: Admissible radii bound the Sendov radius
articles.statement:
If $R$ is an admissible radius, then the Sendov
radius is at most $R$.

articles.title: The Sendov radius
articles.statement:
The Sendov radius is the infimum, as a real number, of the set of
admissible radii in Sendov's problem.

By the convention for infima of real numbers, it would be $0$ if no radius were admissible.

articles.title: Upper bound two for the Sendov radius
articles.statement:
This is the proposition that the Sendov radius is at
most $2$.

The geometric bound from the Gauss–Lucas theorem gives this upper bound.

articles.title: Convexity via the tangent-plane inequality
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real Banach space, let
$X \subseteq E$ be an open convex set, and let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{R}$ be twice continuously
differentiable on $X$. Then $f$ is convex on $X$ if and only if
$f(x) \ge f(a) + Df(a)(x - a)$ for all $a, x \in X$, where $Df(a)$ is the Fréchet derivative of
$f$ at $a$ within $X$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functional analysis; Measures, integration, derivative, holomorphy), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_95`.

articles.title: Caristi fixed-point theorem
articles.statement:
Let $(X, d)$ be a nonempty complete metric space and let
$\varphi : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be lower semicontinuous and bounded below. If a map $T : X \to X$
satisfies $d(x, T x) \le \varphi(x) - \varphi(T x)$ for every $x \in X$, then $T$ has a fixed
point: there is $x \in X$ with $T x = x$.

## Sources

- J. Caristi, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 215 (1976), 241-251, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9947-1976-0394329-4.

articles.title: Ekeland variational principle without a nonemptiness assumption
articles.statement:
Let $(X, d)$ be a complete
metric space, let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be lower semicontinuous and bounded below, and let
$\varepsilon > 0$. If $x_0 \in X$ satisfies $f(x_0) \le f(x) + \varepsilon$ for every $x \in X$,
then there is $x_\varepsilon \in X$ with $f(x_\varepsilon) \le f(x_0)$,
$d(x_\varepsilon, x_0) \le 1$, and $f(x_\varepsilon) < f(y) + \varepsilon\, d(x_\varepsilon, y)$
for every $y \ne x_\varepsilon$.

The space $X$ is not separately assumed nonempty, since the point $x_0$ already lies in it.

articles.title: Ekeland variational principle
articles.statement:
Let $(X, d)$ be a nonempty complete metric space, let
$f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be lower semicontinuous and bounded below, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. If
$x_0 \in X$ satisfies $f(x_0) \le f(x) + \varepsilon$ for every $x \in X$, then there is
$x_\varepsilon \in X$ with $f(x_\varepsilon) \le f(x_0)$, $d(x_\varepsilon, x_0) \le 1$, and
$f(x_\varepsilon) < f(y) + \varepsilon\, d(x_\varepsilon, y)$ for every $y \ne x_\varepsilon$.

## Sources

- I. Ekeland, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 47 (1974), 324-353, DOI 10.1016/0022-247X(74)90025-0. It follows from `ekeland_variational_principle_general`; the instance `[Nonempty X]` is unused and keeps the source's shape.

articles.title: Euler–Lagrange equation
articles.statement:
Let $a < b$ be real numbers, let $L(t, y, v)$ be a real function
of three real variables that is twice continuously differentiable on $\mathbb{R}^3$, and let
$x : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be twice continuously differentiable. Write
$\partial L / \partial y$ and $\partial L / \partial v$ for the partial derivatives of $L$ in its
second and third arguments. If $x$ is a variational extremum of the action of $L$ on $(a, b)$,
then for every $t \in (a, b)$

$$
\frac{\partial L}{\partial y}(t, x(t), x'(t))
= \frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s = t} \frac{\partial L}{\partial v}(s, x(s), x'(s)).
$$

## Sources

- L. Euler (1744) and J.-L. Lagrange (1755). Listed as §44 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `euler_lagrange_equation` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Variational extremum
articles.statement:
Let $a, b$ be real numbers and let $L(t, y, v)$
be a real function of three real variables. A function $x : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a
variational extremum of the action of $L$ on $(a, b)$ if $x$ is continuously differentiable and,
for every infinitely differentiable function $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ of compact support
whose closed support lies in the open interval $(a, b)$, the derivative at $\varepsilon = 0$ of

$$
\varepsilon \mapsto \int_{(a, b)}
L\big(t, x(t) + \varepsilon h(t), x'(t) + \varepsilon h'(t)\big)\,dt
$$

is $0$.

By convention, a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$, and so is the integral of a
function that is not integrable.

articles.title: Partial derivative of the Lagrangian in velocity
articles.statement:
For a real function $L(t, y, v)$
of three real variables, a function $x : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a real number $t$, this
is the value $\frac{\partial L}{\partial v}(t, x(t), x'(t))$, the derivative at $v = x'(t)$ of
the function $v \mapsto L(t, x(t), v)$.

By convention, a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$, both for $x'(t)$ and for
the derivative in $v$.

articles.title: Partial derivative of the Lagrangian in position
articles.statement:
For a real function $L(t, y, v)$
of three real variables, a function $x : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a real number $t$, this
is the value $\frac{\partial L}{\partial y}(t, x(t), x'(t))$, the derivative at $y = x(t)$ of
the function $y \mapsto L(t, y, x'(t))$.

By convention, a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$, both for $x'(t)$ and for
the derivative in $y$.

articles.title: The biconjugate lies below the function
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology
and let $f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$ never take the value $-\infty$. Then $f^{**}(x) \le f(x)$
for every $x \in E$, where $f^{**}$ is the Fenchel biconjugate of $f$.

This is the easy direction of the Fenchel–Moreau theorem.

articles.title: Fenchel biconjugate
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology and let
$f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$. The biconjugate of $f$ at $x \in E$ is the extended real number
$f^{**}(x) = \sup_L \big(L(x) - f^*(L)\big)$, where $L$ ranges over the continuous linear
functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$ and $f^*$ is the Fenchel conjugate of $f$.

articles.title: Fenchel conjugate
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology and let
$f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$. The Fenchel conjugate of $f$ at a continuous linear functional
$L : E \to \mathbb{R}$ is the extended real number $f^*(L) = \sup_{y \in E} \big(L(y) - f(y)\big)$.

articles.title: Fenchel–Moreau theorem
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a locally convex real topological vector space, not
necessarily Hausdorff. Let $f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be lower semicontinuous, never equal to
$-\infty$, not identically $+\infty$, and convex in the sense that the set
$\{(x, r) \in E \times \mathbb{R} : f(x) \le r\}$ is convex. Then for every $x \in E$,
$f(x) = \sup_L \big(L(x) - \sup_{y \in E} (L(y) - f(y))\big)$, where $L$ ranges over the
continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$; that is, $f$ equals its Fenchel biconjugate.

## Sources

- Werner Fenchel, *Convex Cones, Sets, and Functions: From Notes by D. W. Blackett of Lectures at Princeton University, 1951*, Princeton University Department of Mathematics, 1953, Open Library OL1430688W; and Jean-Jacques Moreau, "Fonctions convexes duales et points proximaux," C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 255 (1962), 2897–2899, zbMATH 0118.10502.

articles.title: Lower semicontinuous functions have closed epigraphs
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a topological space and
let $f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be lower semicontinuous. Then the set
$\{(x, r) \in E \times \mathbb{R} : f(x) \le r\}$ is closed in $E \times \mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Sublinear rate of gradient descent for smooth convex functions
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a
finite-dimensional real inner product space, let $L > 0$, and let $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$ be
convex and differentiable with $L$-Lipschitz gradient $\nabla f$. Let $x^\star \in E$ be a global
minimizer of $f$, let $0 < \eta \le 1/L$, and let $(x_k)_{k \ge 0}$ be any sequence in $E$ with
$x_{k+1} = x_k - \eta \nabla f(x_k)$ for all $k$. Then for every $k \ge 1$,
$f(x_k) - f(x^\star) \le \|x_0 - x^\star\|^2 / (2 \eta k)$.

Proof: The descent lemma and first-order convexity inequality are proved on affine lines. They
bound each objective gap by a difference of squared distances to $x^\star$; telescoping and the
monotonicity of $f(x_k)$ in $k$ give the rate, as in L. Vandenberghe, ECE236C lecture notes
"Gradient method" (Spring 2022), slides 1.23-1.26.

## Sources

- Y. Nesterov, Introductory Lectures on Convex Optimization, Section 2.1; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent.

articles.title: The gradient descent exponent
articles.statement:
The gradient descent exponent is the supremum, in the
extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$, of the set of real numbers $c$ such that some step schedule
$s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ achieves a uniform last-iterate rate with exponent $c$. In
particular, it is $-\infty$ if there is no such $c$, and $+\infty$ if these exponents are
unbounded above.

## Sources

- OptimizationProblems, `constants/35a.md` (constant C35).

articles.title: Silver ratio
articles.statement:
The silver ratio is the real number $\rho = 1 + \sqrt{2}$.

It is the ratio used by the stepsize-hedging (silver) step schedule.

articles.title: Gradient descent with zero step sizes stays put
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real Hilbert space,
$f : E \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x_0 \in E$. If every step size is $0$, then for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$
the $k$-th gradient descent iterate of $f$ from $x_0$ equals $x_0$.

articles.title: Gradient descent with a step schedule
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real Hilbert space,
$f : E \to \mathbb{R}$, $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ a sequence of step sizes and $x_0 \in E$.
The gradient descent trajectory of $f$ from $x_0$ with steps $s$ is the sequence
$(x_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ starting at $x_0$ with $x_{k+1} = x_k - s_k \nabla f(x_k)$.

Here $\nabla f(x)$ is taken to be $0$ at points $x$ where $f$ is not differentiable.

articles.title: Constant unit steps achieve exponent one
articles.statement:
The step schedule with every step size equal to
$1$ achieves a uniform last-iterate rate with exponent $1$.

This follows from the fixed-step descent theorem; it is a lower bound for the gradient descent
exponent, not its conjectured optimal value.

articles.title: Uniform last-iterate rate of a step schedule
articles.statement:
A step schedule
$s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ achieves a uniform last-iterate rate with exponent
$c \in \mathbb{R}$ if there are a real number $C > 0$ and an integer $K \ge 1$ with the following
property. For every $d \in \mathbb{N}$, every convex differentiable function
$f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ whose gradient is $1$-Lipschitz for the Euclidean norm, every
$x^\star \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $f(x^\star) \le f(x)$ for all $x$, every $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and
every integer $k \ge K$, the $k$-th gradient descent iterate $x_k$ of $f$ from $x_0$ with steps
$s$ satisfies

$$f(x_k) - f(x^\star) \le \frac{C \lVert x_0 - x^\star \rVert^2}{k^c}.$$

The constants $C$ and $K$ are chosen before, and do not depend on, $d$, $f$, $x^\star$, $x_0$
and $k$.

articles.title: Convex functions with $1$-Lipschitz gradient
articles.statement:
A function $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$ on a real
Hilbert space $E$ is unit-smooth convex if it is convex, differentiable, and its gradient is
$1$-Lipschitz: $\lVert \nabla f(x) - \nabla f(y) \rVert \le \lVert x - y \rVert$ for all
$x, y \in E$.

articles.title: The gradient descent exponent is at least one
articles.statement:
The gradient descent exponent is at
least $1$.

articles.title: Silver exponent
articles.statement:
The silver exponent is $\log_2 \rho = \log \rho / \log 2$, where
$\rho = 1 + \sqrt{2}$ is the silver ratio.

It is the catalogue's proposed optimal value of the gradient descent exponent.

articles.title: Silver step schedule
articles.statement:
The silver step schedule is the sequence
$s_t = 1 + \rho^{\nu_2(t + 1) - 1}$ for $t \in \mathbb{N}$, where $\rho = 1 + \sqrt{2}$ is the
silver ratio and $\nu_2(n)$ is the exponent of $2$ in the prime factorization of $n$.

The exponent $\nu_2(t + 1) - 1$ is an integer and equals $-1$ for even $t$, where
$s_t = 1 + \rho^{-1} = \sqrt{2}$.

articles.title: Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions for inequality constraints
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional
real normed space, let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{R}$ and $g_1, \dots, g_m \colon E \to \mathbb{R}$,
and let $x \in E$ be a point at which $f$ and every $g_i$ are differentiable; write $D$ for
the Fréchet derivative at $x$. Suppose that $x$ is feasible, that is $g_i(x) \le 0$ for every
$i$; that $x$ is a local minimizer of $f$ on the feasible set
$\{y \in E : g_i(y) \le 0 \text{ for every } i\}$; and that the derivatives $Dg_i(x)$ of the
active constraints, those $i$ with $g_i(x) = 0$, are linearly independent. Then there exist
multipliers $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_m \ge 0$ such that $\lambda_i g_i(x) = 0$ for every $i$
and $Df(x) + \sum_{i=1}^m \lambda_i Dg_i(x) = 0$.

## Sources

- W. Karush, Minima of Functions of Several Variables with Inequalities as Side Conditions (M.Sc. thesis, Univ. Chicago, 1939); H. W. Kuhn and A. W. Tucker, Nonlinear Programming, Proc. Second Berkeley Symposium (1951), 481–492, DOI 10.1525/9780520411586-036.

articles.title: The inf-convolution of a lower semicontinuous function is Lipschitz
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a metric
space with metric $d$, and let $f : X \to [0,\infty]$ be lower semicontinuous with $f(p) < \infty$
for at least one $p \in X$. For a natural number $n$ and $x \in X$ let

$$
g_n(x) = \inf\{f(p) + n\,d(x,p) : p \in X\} \in [0,\infty].
$$

Then $|g_n(x) - g_n(y)| \le n\,d(x,y)$ for every natural number $n$ (including $n = 0$) and all
$x, y \in X$.

Each $g_n(x)$ is finite, since $g_n(x) \le f(p) + n\,d(x,p)$ for the point $p$ with
$f(p) < \infty$, so the difference is one of real numbers.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functional analysis; Nonlinear functional analysis), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_36`.

articles.title: Inf-convolution with a multiple of the distance
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a metric space with metric
$d$, let $f : X \to [0,\infty]$, and let $n$ be a natural number. For $x \in X$,

$$
g_n(x) = \inf\{f(p) + n\,d(x,p) : p \in X\},
$$

the infimum being taken in $[0,\infty]$.

articles.title: Variational characterization of projection onto a convex cone
articles.statement:
Variational characterization of the projection onto a cone with complete carrier:
`p` is the projection of `x` iff the residual pairs nonpositively with the
cone and is orthogonal to `p`. The ambient space need not be complete.

articles.title: Variational characterization determines the cone projection
articles.statement: A point satisfying the cone variational characterization is the projection.

articles.title: Cone projection residual pairs nonpositively with the cone
articles.statement: The residual of the cone projection pairs nonpositively with every point of the cone.

articles.title: Cone projection residual is orthogonal to the projection
articles.statement: The residual of the cone projection is orthogonal to the projection.

articles.title: Moreau decomposition, polar form
articles.statement:
The cone projection's residual is the
projection onto its negative polar. This accepts a Mathlib proper cone directly.

articles.title: Membership in the negative polar cone
articles.statement: Membership in the negative polar uses the nonpositive inner-product convention.

articles.title: Moreau decomposition
articles.statement:
A point is the sum of its projections onto a
proper cone and its negative polar, and the projections are orthogonal.

articles.title: Negative polar agrees with the inner dual of the negated cone
articles.statement:
In a complete ambient space, the negative polar agrees with Mathlib's
inner dual of the negated carrier.

articles.title: Bipolar theorem for closed convex cones
articles.statement: The negative bipolar of a proper cone is itself, by Mathlib's inner-dual bipolar theorem.

articles.title: Negative polar cone
articles.statement:
The negative polar is the standard dual cone of the negated set. Continuity
makes its carrier closed without requiring completeness of the ambient space.

articles.title: Cone projection residual lies in the negative polar
articles.statement: The residual of a cone projection lies in its negative polar.

articles.title: Critical point
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real Banach space and $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$. A point
$x \in E$ is a critical point of $f$ when the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$ vanishes,
$f'(x) = 0$. Here $f'(x)$ is taken to be $0$ when $f$ is not differentiable at $x$, so such
points are critical as well.

articles.title: Mountain pass level
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real Banach space, $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$ and
$a, b \in E$. The mountain pass level of $f$ between $a$ and $b$ is

$$
c = \inf_{\gamma} \sup_{t \in [0, 1]} f(\gamma(t)),
$$

the infimum taken over all continuous paths $\gamma : [0, 1] \to E$ with $\gamma(0) = a$ and
$\gamma(1) = b$. Suprema and infima are taken in $\mathbb{R}$, where a family that is unbounded
on the relevant side has supremum or infimum $0$ by convention.

articles.title: Mountain pass theorem
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real Banach space and let $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuously differentiable and satisfy the Palais–Smale condition. Let $a, b \in E$ and let
$\varepsilon, r$ be real numbers such that $a$ and $b$ are separated by a mountain range of $f$
at height $\varepsilon$ and radius $r$: $f(a) = 0$, $\varepsilon > 0$, $r > 0$,
$f(y) \ge \varepsilon$ for every $y$ with $\|y - a\| = r$, $\|b - a\| > r$ and $f(b) \le 0$.
Then the mountain pass level $c$ of $f$ between $a$ and $b$ satisfies $c \ge \varepsilon$, and
$f$ has a critical point $x$ with $f(x) = c$.

## Sources

- A. Ambrosetti and P.H. Rabinowitz, 'Dual variational methods in critical point theory and applications', J. Funct. Anal. 14 (1973) 349–381. Listed as §119 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `mountain_pass` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Mountain range
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real Banach space, $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$, $a, b \in E$ and
$\varepsilon, r \in \mathbb{R}$. The points $a$ and $b$ are separated by a mountain range of $f$
at height $\varepsilon$ and radius $r$ when $f(a) = 0$, $\varepsilon > 0$, $r > 0$,
$f(y) \ge \varepsilon$ for every $y \in E$ with $\|y - a\| = r$, $\|b - a\| > r$ and
$f(b) \le 0$.

articles.title: Palais–Smale condition
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real Banach space. A function $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$
satisfies the Palais–Smale condition when every sequence $(u_k)$ in $E$ such that $(f(u_k))$ is
bounded and the Fréchet derivatives $f'(u_k)$ tend to $0$ in operator norm has a subsequence
converging in $E$. Here $f'(x)$ is taken to be $0$ at points where $f$ is not differentiable.

articles.title: Membership in the polar
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real inner product space, $A \subseteq E$ and
$y \in E$. Then $y$ lies in the polar $A^\circ$ of $A$ if and only if $\langle x, y \rangle \le 1$
for every $x \in A$.

articles.title: The closed unit ball is self-polar
articles.statement:
In a real inner product space $E$, the polar of the
closed unit ball $\{x \in E : \|x\| \le 1\}$ is the closed unit ball itself.

articles.title: The polar of the cube is the $\ell^1$ unit ball
articles.statement:
For every $n$, the polar of the
coordinate cube $[-1, 1]^n$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, that is the set of all $y$
with $\langle x, y \rangle \le 1$ for every $x$ in the cube, is the closed $\ell^1$ unit ball
$\{y \in \mathbb{R}^n : \sum_i |y_i| \le 1\}$.

articles.title: Polar of the empty set
articles.statement:
In a real inner product space $E$, the polar of the empty
set is all of $E$, since the defining condition is vacuous.

articles.title: Polar of a linear image
articles.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be finite-dimensional real inner product spaces,
let $f : E \to F$ be a linear map with adjoint $f^* : F \to E$, and let $K \subseteq E$. Writing
$S^\circ$ for the polar of a set $S$, we have $(f(K))^\circ = (f^*)^{-1}(K^\circ)$, that is,
$y \in F$ lies in the polar of $f(K)$ if and only if $f^*(y)$ lies in the polar of $K$.

This is the set-theoretic transformation used by the Mahler volume product.

articles.title: The polar reverses inclusion
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of a real inner product space.
If $A \subseteq B$, then the polar $B^\circ$ of $B$ is contained in the polar $A^\circ$ of $A$.

articles.title: Polar of a set
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real inner product space. The polar of a set $A \subseteq E$
is the set $A^\circ = \{y \in E : \langle x, y \rangle \le 1 \text{ for all } x \in A\}$. This
uses the one-sided bound $\langle x, y \rangle \le 1$, not $|\langle x, y \rangle| \le 1$.

articles.title: The origin lies in every polar
articles.statement:
In a real inner product space $E$, for every set
$A \subseteq E$ the origin $0$ lies in the polar $A^\circ$ of $A$, since
$\langle x, 0 \rangle = 0 \le 1$ for every $x \in A$.

articles.title: Coercive bounded operators on a real Hilbert space are surjective
articles.statement:
A coercive bounded linear operator on a real Hilbert space is surjective.
This is the whole-space case of Stampacchia's theorem (compare Mathlib's
Lax–Milgram theorem, which is the analogous statement for bilinear forms).

articles.title: Stampacchia's theorem, bilinear-form form
articles.statement:
For a coercive bounded
bilinear form `B` on a real Hilbert space, a nonempty closed convex set `K`,
and a continuous linear functional `φ`, there is exactly one `u ∈ K` with
`B u (v - u) ≥ φ (v - u)` for all `v ∈ K`.

articles.title: Stampacchia's theorem, operator form
articles.statement:
For a coercive bounded linear
operator `A` on a real Hilbert space, a nonempty closed convex set `K`, and
`f ∈ E`, there is exactly one `u ∈ K` with `⟪A u - f, v - u⟫_ℝ ≥ 0` for all
`v ∈ K`.

articles.title: Variational inequality on the whole space reduces to an equation
articles.statement: On the whole space, a variational-inequality solution satisfies `A u = f`.

articles.title: Tikhonov normal operator is bijective
articles.statement: The normal operator is bijective when `Λ > 0`.

articles.title: Tikhonov minimizers solve the normal equations
articles.statement:
A minimizer of the Tikhonov functional equals a solution of the normal
equations, when `Λ > 0`.

articles.title: Solvability of the Tikhonov normal equations
articles.statement: The normal equations are solvable when `Λ > 0`.

articles.title: Existence and uniqueness of the Tikhonov minimizer
articles.statement: The Tikhonov functional has a unique minimizer when `Λ > 0`.

articles.title: Tikhonov normal operator has closed range
articles.statement: The normal operator has closed range when `Λ > 0`, since it is bounded below.

articles.title: Solutions of the normal equations minimize the Tikhonov functional
articles.statement: A solution of the normal equations minimizes the Tikhonov functional.

articles.title: Tikhonov normal operator is self-adjoint
articles.statement: The normal operator is self-adjoint, for every real `Λ`.

articles.title: Tikhonov normal operator is invertible
articles.statement: The normal operator is a unit when `Λ > 0`.

articles.title: Tikhonov normal operator has trivial kernel
articles.statement: The normal operator has trivial kernel when `Λ > 0`.

articles.title: Stability bound for Tikhonov regularized solutions
articles.statement: Stability bound for a solution of the normal equations.

articles.title: Tikhonov normal operator is surjective
articles.statement:
The normal operator is surjective when `Λ > 0`: its range is closed and
its orthogonal complement is its kernel, which is trivial since the operator
is self-adjoint.

articles.title: Real part of the Tikhonov normal operator's quadratic form
articles.statement:
The real part of the inner product of the normal operator applied to `x`
with `x` itself.

articles.title: Tikhonov solutions tend to zero as the parameter grows
articles.statement: Solutions of the Tikhonov normal equations tend to `0` as `Λ → ∞`.

articles.title: Quadratic identity for the Tikhonov functional at a normal-equation solution
articles.statement:
The quadratic identity for the Tikhonov functional around a solution of
the normal equations: the cross term vanishes by the normal equations.

articles.title: Tikhonov functional
articles.statement: The Tikhonov (ridge) functional `J(x) = ‖A x - b‖ ^ 2 + Λ * ‖x‖ ^ 2`.

articles.title: Inner product of the Tikhonov normal operator with its argument
articles.statement: The inner product of the normal operator applied to `x` with `x` itself.

articles.title: Tikhonov normal operator is bounded below by the regularization parameter
articles.statement: The normal operator is bounded below by `Λ`, for every real `Λ`.

articles.title: Normal operator of the Tikhonov problem
articles.statement: The normal operator `A† ∘L A + Λ • 1` of the Tikhonov problem.

articles.title: Existence of the Cauchy principal value of $\varphi(x)/x$
articles.statement:
For every real-valued Schwartz
function $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{R}$ there is a real number $L$ such that
$\int_{\{x \in \mathbb{R} \,:\, |x| \ge \varepsilon\}} \varphi(x)/x \, dx \to L$ as
$\varepsilon \to 0^+$, the integrals being taken with respect to Lebesgue measure.

## Sources

- F. Friedlander and M. Joshi, *Introduction to the Theory of Distributions*, Ch. 2.

articles.title: The Dirac comb is a tempered distribution
articles.statement:
There is a tempered distribution $T$ on
$\mathbb{R}$, that is, a continuous $\mathbb{C}$-linear functional on the space of
complex-valued Schwartz functions on $\mathbb{R}$, such that $T(g)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} g(n)$
for every complex-valued Schwartz function $g$ on $\mathbb{R}$.

## Sources

- <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirac_comb>.

articles.title: A function with vanishing weak third derivative on $(0,1)$ is a.e. a polynomial of degree at most $2$ on $(0,1)$
articles.statement:
**A function with vanishing weak third derivative on $(0,1)$ is a.e. a polynomial of
degree at most $2$ on $[0,1]$.** Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be integrable on $[0,1]$, and
suppose that $\int_{0}^{1} f(x)\,g'''(x)\,dx=0$ for every smooth function
$g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ whose support is contained in some closed interval
$[s,t] \subseteq (0,1)$. Then there are real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ such that $f(x)=a+bx+cx^2$
for almost every $x\in[0,1]$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Distributions, generalized functions, distribution spaces), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_66`.

articles.title: The full derivative of a distribution
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real normed space, $\Omega \subseteq E$
an open set and $F$ a real topological vector space, and let $\mathcal{D}'(\Omega, F)$ be the
space of $F$-valued distributions on $\Omega$ (continuous linear maps from the real-valued test
functions on $\Omega$ to $F$), with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets of test
functions. For $v \in E$ and $T \in \mathcal{D}'(\Omega, F)$, let $\partial_v T$ be the
directional derivative $\varphi \mapsto -T(\partial_v \varphi)$. Then there is a continuous
linear map $D$ from $\mathcal{D}'(\Omega, F)$ to the space of continuous linear maps
$E \to \mathcal{D}'(\Omega, F)$ (with the topology of uniform convergence on bounded sets) such
that $D(T)(v) = \partial_v T$ for every $T \in \mathcal{D}'(\Omega, F)$ and every $v \in E$.

## Sources

- L. Schwartz, *Théorie des distributions*, Ch. II.

articles.title: Linear maps on Schwartz space commuting with $x$ and $d/dx$ are scalars
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ be the space of complex-valued Schwartz functions on $\mathbb{R}$, and
let $M:\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})\to\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ be a $\mathbb{C}$-linear map with
$(Mf)(x)=x f(x)$ for all $f\in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$. If
$T:\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})\to\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-linear map (not assumed
continuous) with $TM=MT$ and $T\frac{d}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}T$, then there exists $c\in\mathbb{C}$
such that $Tf=cf$ for all $f\in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Operator theory; General theory of linear operators), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_54`.

articles.title: The Gaussian is a Schwartz function
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product
space. Then there is a real-valued Schwartz function $g$ on $E$ such that
$g(x) = e^{-\|x\|^2}$ for every $x \in E$.

## Sources

- <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schwartz_space>.

articles.title: The tempered distributions $(x \pm i\varepsilon)^{-1}$ converge as $\varepsilon \to 0^+$
articles.statement:
Write $S(\mathbb{R})$ for the space of complex-valued Schwartz functions on $\mathbb{R}$, and for
$\varepsilon > 0$ and $\phi \in S(\mathbb{R})$ let
$u_{\pm,\varepsilon}(\phi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} (x \pm i\varepsilon)^{-1}\phi(x)\, dx$. Then for
every $\varepsilon > 0$ both $u_{+,\varepsilon}$ and $u_{-,\varepsilon}$ are tempered
distributions, that is, continuous $\mathbb{C}$-linear functionals on $S(\mathbb{R})$, and there
are tempered distributions $u_+$ and $u_-$ such that $u_{+,\varepsilon}(\phi) \to u_+(\phi)$ and
$u_{-,\varepsilon}(\phi) \to u_-(\phi)$ as $\varepsilon \to 0^+$ for every $\phi \in S(\mathbb{R})$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Distributions, generalized functions, distribution spaces), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_15`.

articles.title: The pairing with $(x - i\varepsilon)^{-1}$
articles.statement:
For a real number $\varepsilon$ and a Schwartz
function $\phi : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$, $u_{-,\varepsilon}(\phi)$ is the complex number
$\int_{\mathbb{R}} (x - i\varepsilon)^{-1}\phi(x)\, dx$.

The integral is the Lebesgue integral, taken to be $0$ when the integrand is not integrable;
this can happen only for $\varepsilon = 0$.

articles.title: The pairing with $(x + i\varepsilon)^{-1}$
articles.statement:
For a real number $\varepsilon$ and a Schwartz
function $\phi : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$, $u_{+,\varepsilon}(\phi)$ is the complex number
$\int_{\mathbb{R}} (x + i\varepsilon)^{-1}\phi(x)\, dx$.

The integral is the Lebesgue integral, taken to be $0$ when the integrand is not integrable;
this can happen only for $\varepsilon = 0$.

articles.title: Smooth partitions of unity subordinate to a finite open cover
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a
finite-dimensional real normed space, $K \subseteq E$ a compact set, and $(U_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a
finite family of open subsets of $E$ with $K \subseteq \bigcup_i U_i$. Then there are smooth
compactly supported functions $\varphi_i : E \to \mathbb{R}$, one for each $i \in \iota$, such
that $\varphi_i(x) \ge 0$ for all $i$ and all $x \in E$, the closed support of each $\varphi_i$
is contained in $U_i$, and $\sum_{i \in \iota} \varphi_i(x) = 1$ for every $x \in K$.

## Sources

- <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_unity>.

articles.title: Browder–Göhde–Kirk fixed point theorem
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real Banach space and
let $K \subseteq E$ be a nonempty, closed, bounded, convex set. If a map $f : E \to E$ sends $K$
into $K$ and is nonexpansive on $K$, that is, $\|f(x) - f(y)\| \le \|x - y\|$ for all
$x, y \in K$, then $f$ has a fixed point in $K$: there is $y \in K$ with $f(y) = y$.

## Sources

- F. Browder, Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. USA 1965, D. Göhde, Math. Ann. 1965, and W. Kirk, Amer. Math. Monthly 1965-66, fixed-point theorem for nonexpansive mappings in uniformly convex Banach spaces; textbook Goebel and Kirk, 1990; Lean states complete uniformly convex real case with `Bornology.IsBounded` convex set.

articles.title: Normal structure
articles.statement:
A set $K$ in a real normed space has normal structure if every convex
subset $H \subseteq K$ with at least two points contains a point that is not diametral in $H$.

articles.title: Diametral point
articles.statement:
A point $x$ of a real normed space is diametral in a set $s$
if $x \in s$ and the radius of $x$ in $s$ equals the diameter of $s$.

articles.title: Nonexpansive self-map
articles.statement:
A map $T : K \to K$ from a subset $K$ of a real normed space to
itself is nonexpansive if $\|T(x) - T(y)\| \le \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in K$, that is, if $T$
is $1$-Lipschitz for the distance inherited from the space.

articles.title: Kirk's fixed-point theorem for sets with normal structure
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a reflexive real
Banach space, meaning that the canonical embedding of $E$ into its double dual is surjective, and
let $K \subseteq E$ be a nonempty, closed, bounded, convex set with normal structure. Then every
nonexpansive self-map $T : K \to K$ has a fixed point.

## Sources

- W. A. Kirk, A fixed point theorem for mappings which do not increase distances, Amer. Math. Monthly 72 (1965). Listed as §228 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Knill, §228. Problem `kirk_normal_structure` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Diameter of a set
articles.statement:
The diameter of a set $s$ in a real normed space is the supremum in
$\mathbb{R}$ of the distances $\operatorname{dist}(x, y)$ over all $x, y \in s$; by the convention
for real suprema it is $0$ when $s$ is empty or these distances are unbounded.

articles.title: Radius of a point in a set
articles.statement:
The radius of a point $x$ in a set $s$ of a real normed space
is the supremum in $\mathbb{R}$ of the distances $\operatorname{dist}(x, y)$ over all $y \in s$; by
the convention for real suprema it is $0$ when $s$ is empty or these distances are unbounded.

articles.title: Browder's demiclosedness principle
articles.statement:
If `T` is nonexpansive,
`u n ⇀ x` weakly, and `u n - T (u n) → 0`, then `T x = x`.

articles.title: Fixed points of a nonexpansive map are weakly sequentially closed
articles.statement:
The fixed-point set of a nonexpansive map is weakly sequentially
closed: if every `u n` is a fixed point of `T` and `u n ⇀ x` weakly,
then `T x = x`.

articles.title: Fixed points of maps whose iterates have null Lipschitz constants
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty
complete metric space, let $f : X \to X$, and write $f^n$ for the $n$-th iterate of $f$. Let
$(q_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers with $q_n \to 0$ such that
$d(f^n(x), f^n(y)) \le q_n \, d(x, y)$ for every $n \ge 1$ and all $x, y \in X$. Then $f$ has a
fixed point: there is $x \in X$ with $f(x) = x$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Operator theory; Nonlinear operators and their properties), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_74`.

articles.title: Markov–Kakutani fixed-point theorem
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a nonempty compact convex subset of a real
normed space $E$, and let $(F_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of continuous affine maps $E \to E$ such
that each $F_i$ maps $K$ into $K$ and $F_i(F_j(x)) = F_j(F_i(x))$ for all $i, j \in I$ and all
$x \in E$. Then there is $x \in K$ with $F_i(x) = x$ for every $i \in I$.

Commutation is required on all of $E$, not only on $K$.

## Sources

- A. Markov, C. R. Acad. Sci. URSS 1936 and S. Kakutani, Proc. Imp. Acad. Tokyo 14 (1938) 242-245, Markov-Kakutani fixed-point theorem; Lean states real normed nonempty compact convex case with globally commuting `E →ᴬ[ℝ] E` family.

articles.title: Ehrling's inequality
articles.statement:
Let $X$, $Y$, $Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $i \colon X \to Y$ be an
injective compact bounded linear operator, and let $j \colon Y \to Z$ be an injective bounded
linear operator. Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $C_\varepsilon > 0$ such that
$\|i(u)\|_Y \le \varepsilon \|u\|_X + C_\varepsilon \|j(i(u))\|_Z$ for all $u \in X$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Normed linear spaces and Banach spaces; Banach lattices), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_36`.

articles.title: Sobolev trace bound on the plane $z = 0$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$
articles.statement:
Let $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$
be a sequence of continuously differentiable functions $\mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$, where
$\mathbb{R}^3$ has coordinates $(x, y, z)$ and the max norm. For $p \in \mathbb{R}^3$ write
$\|Df_n(p)\|$ for the operator norm of the derivative of $f_n$ at $p$, which equals
$|\partial_x f_n(p)| + |\partial_y f_n(p)| + |\partial_z f_n(p)|$, the sum of the absolute values
of the partial derivatives. Suppose that for every $n$ the function
$p \mapsto |f_n(p)|^2 + \|Df_n(p)\|^2$ is Lebesgue integrable on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with integral at
most $1$. Then there is a constant $C \ge 0$ such that for every $n$ the function
$(x, y) \mapsto |f_n(x, y, 0)|^2$ is Lebesgue integrable on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with integral at most
$C$.

Since $\|Df_n(p)\|$ is at least the Euclidean length $|\nabla f_n(p)|$ of the gradient, the
hypothesis implies the bound $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} (|\nabla f_n|^2 + |f_n|^2) \le 1$ of the source
problem; conversely, if $f_n$ satisfies that bound, then $f_n / \sqrt{3}$ satisfies the hypothesis.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_56`.

articles.title: Weighted Ladyzhenskaya inequality in the plane
articles.statement:
There is a constant $C > 0$ such that
for every $C^1$ function $\omega : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ with $\omega(x) > 0$ for all $x$
and $\|\nabla\omega/\omega\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^2)} \le 1$, and every smooth compactly supported
function $u : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$,

$$
\int_{\mathbb{R}^2} u^4 \omega \le C \|u\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)}^2
\int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \left(|\nabla u|^2 + |u|^2\right) \omega.
$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Real functions; Inequalities in real analysis), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_48`.

articles.title: The constant in Young's $L^1$–$L^p$ convolution inequality cannot be lowered
articles.statement:
Let
$1 \le p \le \infty$ and $\varepsilon > 0$. Then there exist real-valued functions
$f \in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ and $g \in L^p(\mathbb{R})$ such that

$$
\|f * g\|_p > (1 - \varepsilon) \|f\|_1 \|g\|_p,
$$

where $(f * g)(x) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(t)\, g(x - t)\, dt$ and all norms are taken with
respect to Lebesgue measure.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_45`.

articles.title: Agmon's inequality on the line
articles.statement:
There is a constant $C > 0$ such that every real-valued
Schwartz function $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies

$$\|f\|_{L^\infty} \le C \, \|f\|_{L^2}^{1/2} \, \|f'\|_{L^2}^{1/2},$$

where $f'$ is the derivative of $f$ and the $L^\infty$ and $L^2$ norms are taken with respect to
Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Real functions; Inequalities in real analysis), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_94`.

articles.title: Closed subspaces of $L^2((0,1))$ inside $C((0,1))$ are finite-dimensional
articles.statement:
Let $H$ be a
closed linear subspace of the real space $L^2([0,1])$ with respect to Lebesgue measure, and
suppose that every element of $H$ is the class of a continuous function $[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$.
Then $H$ is finite-dimensional.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_11`.

articles.title: Sixth-power integral bounded by the Dirichlet energy under $L^2$ normalization
articles.statement:
There is
a constant $C_2 > 0$ such that every infinitely differentiable, compactly supported function
$u : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $\int_{\mathbb{R}} u(t)^2 \, dt = 1$ satisfies

$$\int_{\mathbb{R}} u(t)^6 \, dt \le C_2 \int_{\mathbb{R}} u'(t)^2 \, dt.$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Real functions; Inequalities in real analysis), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_79`.

articles.title: A weighted $L^6$ bound with a slowly varying weight
articles.statement:
There is a constant $C > 0$ with the
following property. Let $\theta : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuously differentiable, with
$\theta(x) > 0$ for every $x$ and $\|\theta'/\theta\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R})} \le 1$, and let
$u : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be smooth with compact support. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb{R}} u(x)^6\,\theta(x)\,dx \le C\,\|u\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})}^4
\int_{\mathbb{R}} \left(|u'(x)|^2 + |u(x)|^2\right)\theta(x)\,dx.$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Real functions; Inequalities in real analysis), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_67`.

articles.title: Nonlinear interpolation of Lipschitz maps on Lebesgue spaces (Scottish Book Problem 87)
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be Lebesgue measure on $[0, 1]$, write $\|f\|_p$ for the $L^p(\mu)$ norm, let
$1 \le \beta < \alpha \le \infty$, and let $U$ map functions $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ to
functions $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$. Suppose that $U$ maps $L^\beta(\mu)$ into $L^\beta(\mu)$;
that there is $L \ge 0$ with $\|Ux - Uy\|_\beta \le L \|x - y\|_\beta$ for all
$x, y \in L^\beta(\mu)$; and that there is $M_\alpha \ge 0$ such that every $x \in L^\alpha(\mu)$
has $Ux \in L^\alpha(\mu)$ and $\|Ux\|_\alpha \le M_\alpha \|x\|_\alpha$. Then for every $\gamma$
with $\beta < \gamma < \alpha$ there is $M_\gamma \ge 0$ such that every $x \in L^\gamma(\mu)$
has $Ux \in L^\gamma(\mu)$ and $\|Ux\|_\gamma \le M_\gamma \|x\|_\gamma$.

## Sources

- S. Banach, Problem 87 of the Scottish Book; affirmative solution by L. Maligranda, commentary in R. D. Mauldin (ed.), The Scottish Book, 2nd ed. (Birkhäuser, 2015). The linear case follows from the Riesz interpolation theorem, and Banach showed the case `α = ∞`; Maligranda's solution covers the nonlinear case as stated here, with `α = ⊤` allowed.

articles.title: Closed unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^n$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the closed unit ball of
$\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : \|x\| \le 1\}$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is the Euclidean
norm.

articles.title: Radial Sobolev embedding outside the unit ball
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 2$, let $B$ be the closed unit
ball of $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $1 < p < 2$ and $p \le q \le \infty$. Then there is a constant
$C > 0$ such that every radial function $f \colon \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ that has compact
support, whose closed support is contained in $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus B$, and which is $C^\infty$
on $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus B$, satisfies

$$\|f\|_{L^q} \le C \left( \|f\|_{L^p} + \big\| |Df| \big\|_{L^p} \right),$$

where the norms are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure and $|Df(x)|$ is the operator norm of
the derivative of $f$ at $x$.

Smoothness here means $C^\infty$. The source's formal statement asked for real-analyticity
instead, which makes the claim vacuous: an analytic, radial, compactly supported $f$ vanishes
outside the ball.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_80`, with the change above.

articles.title: Radial functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$
articles.statement:
A function $f \colon \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is
radial if $f(x) = f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $\|x\| = \|y\|$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is
the Euclidean norm.

articles.title: Real $n$-space with the Euclidean norm
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, $\mathbb{R}^n$ denotes the
$n$-dimensional real Euclidean space: real $n$-tuples with the Euclidean inner product and norm.

articles.title: Rellich–Kondrachov, sequential form
articles.statement:
Every sequence in the Rellich
ball has a subsequence converging in `ℓ²(ℕ, 𝕜)` to a point of the ball.

articles.title: Rellich–Kondrachov, closedness form
articles.statement: The Rellich ball is closed.

articles.title: Rellich–Kondrachov, compactness form
articles.statement:
The Rellich ball is compact in
`ℓ²(ℕ, 𝕜)`.

articles.title: Truncations lie in the span of the first basis vectors
articles.statement: Canonical truncations land in the span of the first `N` basis vectors.

articles.title: Finitely supported sequences in the Rellich ball
articles.statement:
If `x` is supported in a finite set `S` and its weighted sum over `S` is
at most `M ^ 2`, then `x` lies in the Rellich ball.

articles.title: Membership in the Rellich ball via partial sums
articles.statement:
Membership in the Rellich ball: every finite weighted partial sum is
bounded by `M ^ 2`.

articles.title: Squared $\ell^2$ norm as a sum of squared coordinates
articles.statement: The `ℓ²` norm squared is the sum of the squared coordinate norms.

articles.title: Tail norm identity for $\ell^2$ truncation
articles.statement:
The tail norm identity: the distance from `x` to its truncation is the
`ℓ²` norm of the tail.

articles.title: Tail estimate for the Rellich ball
articles.statement:
The tail estimate: the squared distance from `x` to its truncation is at
most `M ^ 2 / (1 + N ^ 2)`.

articles.title: Rellich ball depends only on the absolute radius
articles.statement: The Rellich ball only depends on `|M|`, since the bound is on `M ^ 2`.

articles.title: Rellich ball of weighted square-summable sequences
articles.statement:
The Rellich ball of radius `M`: sequences in `ℓ²(ℕ, 𝕜)` whose weighted
`ℓ²` energy is at most `M ^ 2`.

articles.title: Rellich weight
articles.statement: The Rellich weight `1 + n ^ 2`.

articles.title: Rellich–Kondrachov, total boundedness form
articles.statement:
The Rellich ball is
totally bounded in `ℓ²(ℕ, 𝕜)`.

articles.title: Homogeneous Sobolev seminorm for the Hölder embedding
articles.statement:
For a real number $s$ and a
Schwartz function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Fourier transform
$\hat f(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{-2\pi i x \xi} f(x) \, dx$, the homogeneous Sobolev seminorm
of $f$ is

$$
\|f\|_{\dot H^s} = \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}} |\xi|^{2s} \, |\hat f(\xi)|^2 \, d\xi \right)^{1/2},
$$

where the integral is taken to be $0$ when the integrand is not integrable.

articles.title: Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, $\mathbb{R}^n$ denotes the real
Euclidean space of dimension $n$: real vectors with coordinates indexed by $0, \dots, n-1$, with
the Euclidean inner product and norm.

articles.title: The homogeneous Sobolev seminorm controls the Hölder seminorm
articles.statement:
Let $s \in (\tfrac12, 1]$,
and for a Schwartz function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Fourier transform $\hat f$ let
$\|f\|_{\dot H^s} = \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}} |\xi|^{2s} |\hat f(\xi)|^2 \, d\xi \right)^{1/2}$
be its homogeneous Sobolev seminorm. There is a constant $C_3 > 0$ such that for every Schwartz
function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$,

$$
\sup_{x \ne y} \frac{|f(x) - f(y)|}{|x - y|^{s - \frac12}} \le C_3 \, \|f\|_{\dot H^s}.
$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_21`.

articles.title: Weak derivative
articles.statement:
Let $f, g : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ and let
$m = (m_0, \dots, m_{n-1})$ be a multi-index of order $|m| = m_0 + \cdots + m_{n-1}$. Then $g$ is
a weak derivative $D^m f$ of $f$ when every smooth ($C^\infty$) compactly supported function
$\varphi : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies

$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f \, D^m \varphi \, dx = (-1)^{|m|} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} g \, \varphi \, dx,$$

where $D^m \varphi$ is the classical mixed partial derivative and each integral is the Lebesgue
integral, taken to be $0$ when the integrand is not integrable.

articles.title: Hölder space $C^{r,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^n)$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $r$ and a real number
$\alpha$, a function $g : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ belongs to $C^{r,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ when
$g$ is $r$ times continuously differentiable, its iterated derivatives $D^j g$ for $j \le r$ are
bounded on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and its $r$-th derivative is $\alpha$-Hölder: there is $C \ge 0$ with
$\|D^r g(x) - D^r g(y)\| \le C \|x - y\|^{\alpha}$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Here
$D^j g(x)$ is the $j$-th Fréchet derivative of $g$ at $x$, a $j$-linear map measured in the
operator norm, and a negative $\alpha$ is replaced by $0$.

articles.title: Sobolev space $W^{k,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $k$ and $p \in [0, \infty]$, a
function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ belongs to $W^{k,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ when $f$ is locally
integrable and, for every multi-index $m = (m_0, \dots, m_{n-1})$ of natural numbers with
$m_0 + \cdots + m_{n-1} \le k$, $f$ has a weak derivative $D^m f$ that lies in
$L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$. Local integrability and $L^p$ are with respect to Lebesgue measure.

articles.title: Mixed partial derivative
articles.statement:
For a multi-index $m = (m_0, \dots, m_{n-1})$ of natural numbers
and a function $\varphi : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the mixed partial derivative is
$D^m \varphi = \partial_0^{m_0} \partial_1^{m_1} \cdots \partial_{n-1}^{m_{n-1}} \varphi$, where
$\partial_i^{j}$ is the $j$-fold iterate of the partial derivative $\partial_i$; thus
$\partial_{n-1}$ is applied first and $\partial_0$ last.

articles.title: Partial derivative
articles.statement:
For a coordinate index $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a function
$\varphi : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the partial derivative $\partial_i \varphi$ is the
function $\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ sending $x$ to $D\varphi(x)(e_i)$, the Fréchet derivative
of $\varphi$ at $x$ applied to the $i$-th standard basis vector $e_i$. At points where $\varphi$
is not differentiable its value is $0$.

articles.title: Sobolev embedding theorem (Morrey regime)
articles.statement:
Let $n, k, r$ be natural numbers and
$\alpha, p$ real numbers with $n < p$, $0 < \alpha \le 1$ and $r + \alpha < k - n/p$. Then every
function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ in the Sobolev space $W^{k,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is equal
almost everywhere, for Lebesgue measure, to some function $g$ in the Hölder space
$C^{r,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^n)$.

## Sources

- C.B. Morrey, 'Functions of several variables and absolute continuity, II', Duke Math. J. 6 (1940) 187–215; full Sobolev-embedding development in *Multiple Integrals in the Calculus of Variations*, Springer 1966. Listed as §111 in O. Knill, *Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics* (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `sobolev_embedding_morrey` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Sup norm on $(0,1)$ bounded by the derivative and the $L^1$ norm
articles.statement:
For every
$\varepsilon > 0$ there is a constant $C_\varepsilon > 0$ such that every function
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that is continuously differentiable on $[0,1]$ satisfies

$$\sup_{x \in [0,1]} |f(x)| \le
\varepsilon \sup_{x \in [0,1]} |f'(x)| + C_\varepsilon \int_0^1 |f(x)|\,dx.$$

At $x = 0$ and $x = 1$, $f'(x)$ is the two-sided derivative of $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$, taken to be $0$
where it does not exist; this does not change the supremum.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Real functions; Inequalities in real analysis), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_49`.

articles.title: Sup-norm bound by the $H^1$ energy for functions vanishing at both ends
articles.statement:
Let
$\alpha \le \beta$ be real numbers and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuously
differentiable on $[\alpha, \beta]$ with $f(\alpha) = f(\beta) = 0$. Then

$$\Bigl(\sup_{x \in [\alpha, \beta]} |f(x)|\Bigr)^2 \le
\frac{1}{2} \int_\alpha^\beta \bigl(f(x)^2 + f'(x)^2\bigr)\,dx.$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Real functions; Inequalities in real analysis), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_54`.

articles.title: Homogeneous Sobolev seminorm for the high-frequency sup-norm bound
articles.statement:
For a real number $s$
and a Schwartz function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Fourier transform
$\hat f(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{-2\pi i x \xi} f(x) \, dx$, the homogeneous Sobolev seminorm
of $f$ is

$$
\|f\|_{\dot H^s} = \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}} |\xi|^{2s} \, |\hat f(\xi)|^2 \, d\xi \right)^{1/2},
$$

where the integral is taken to be $0$ when the integrand is not integrable.

articles.title: Sup bound for Schwartz functions with high-frequency Fourier support
articles.statement:
Let
$s \in (\tfrac12, 1]$, and for a Schwartz function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Fourier
transform $\hat f$ let
$\|f\|_{\dot H^s} = \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}} |\xi|^{2s} |\hat f(\xi)|^2 \, d\xi \right)^{1/2}$
be its homogeneous Sobolev seminorm. There is a constant $C_2 > 0$ such that for every real
$A > 0$ and every Schwartz function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ whose Fourier transform has
closed support contained in $\mathbb{R} \setminus [-A, A]$,

$$
\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |f(x)| \le C_2 \, A^{-s + \frac12} \, \|f\|_{\dot H^s}.
$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_05`.

articles.title: Discs about the origin for the critical weighted Sobolev inequality
articles.statement:
For a real number $r$,
$B_r$ is the open disc $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < r\}$ of radius $r$ about the origin of the
Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$.

articles.title: Open discs about the origin for the annulus Hardy inequality
articles.statement:
For a real number $r$,
$B_r = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < r\}$ is the open disc of radius $r$ about the origin of the
Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $|x|$ is the Euclidean norm.

articles.title: Weighted Hardy inequality on the annulus
articles.statement:
For $r > 0$ let $B_r$ be the open disc of
radius $r$ about the origin of $\mathbb{R}^2$, let $|x|$ be the Euclidean norm, and let
$\phi(x) = \max\{|x| - 1, 0\}$ be the distance from $x$ to the closed unit disc. Let
$\Omega_1 = B_3 \setminus \overline{B}_1$ and $\Omega_2 = B_3 \setminus \overline{B}_2$, with
Lebesgue measure. For every real number $p \ge 1$ there is a constant $C > 0$ such that every
function $u \colon \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ that is continuously differentiable on $\Omega_1$,
and for which $\|\phi \, |\nabla u|\|_{L^p(\Omega_1)}$ and $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega_2)}$ are finite,
satisfies

$$\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega_1)} \le C \|\phi \, |\nabla u|\|_{L^p(\Omega_1)} + C \|u\|_{L^p(\Omega_2)}.$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_77`.

articles.title: Critical weighted Sobolev inequality on an annulus
articles.statement:
For $r > 0$ let $B_r$ be the open disc
of radius $r$ about the origin in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, let
$\Omega_1 = B_3 \setminus \overline{B}_1$ and $\Omega_2 = B_3 \setminus \overline{B}_2$, and let
$\phi(x) = \max\{|x| - 1, 0\}$, the distance from $x$ to the closed unit disc. Let $1 \le p < 2$
and $p^* = 2p/(2-p)$. Then there is a real number $C > 0$ such that every function
$u \colon \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ that is continuously differentiable on $\Omega_1$ and for
which $\|\phi \nabla u\|_{L^p(\Omega_1)}$ and $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega_2)}$ are finite satisfies

$$\|\phi u\|_{L^{p^*}(\Omega_1)} \le C\|\phi \nabla u\|_{L^p(\Omega_1)} + C\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega_2)}.$$

Here the norms are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure, $\|\phi \nabla u\|_{L^p(\Omega_1)}$ is
the $L^p(\Omega_1)$ norm of $x \mapsto \phi(x)\,|\nabla u(x)|$, and $\nabla u(x)$ is the derivative
of $u$ at $x$ within $\Omega_1$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_65`.

articles.title: The annulus of the critical weighted Sobolev inequality
articles.statement:
Let $B_r$ denote the open disc of
radius $r$ about the origin of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. The annulus $\Omega_1$ is
$B_3 \setminus \overline{B}_1$, the set of points of $B_3$ outside the closure of $B_1$, that is,
$\Omega_1 = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : 1 < |x| < 3\}$.

articles.title: Full annulus of the weighted Hardy inequality
articles.statement:
$\Omega_1 = B_3 \setminus \overline{B}_1$,
where $B_r$ is the open disc of radius $r$ about the origin of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$
and $\overline{B}_1$ is the closure of $B_1$; that is, writing $|x|$ for the Euclidean norm,
$\Omega_1$ is the annulus $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : 1 < |x| < 3\}$.

articles.title: The outer annulus of the critical weighted Sobolev inequality
articles.statement:
Let $B_r$ denote the open
disc of radius $r$ about the origin of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. The outer annulus
$\Omega_2$ is $B_3 \setminus \overline{B}_2$, the set of points of $B_3$ outside the closure of
$B_2$, that is, $\Omega_2 = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : 2 < |x| < 3\}$.

articles.title: Outer annulus of the weighted Hardy inequality
articles.statement:
$\Omega_2 = B_3 \setminus \overline{B}_2$,
where $B_r$ is the open disc of radius $r$ about the origin of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$
and $\overline{B}_2$ is the closure of $B_2$; that is, writing $|x|$ for the Euclidean norm,
$\Omega_2$ is the annulus $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : 2 < |x| < 3\}$.

articles.title: Sobolev conjugate exponent in dimension two
articles.statement:
For a real number $p$, the Sobolev conjugate
exponent is $p^* = 2p/(2 - p)$ (at $p = 2$, where the denominator vanishes, this is $0$ by the
convention that division by zero gives zero).

articles.title: The weight of the critical weighted Sobolev inequality
articles.statement:
For $x$ in the Euclidean plane
$\mathbb{R}^2$, the weight is $\phi(x) = \max\{|x| - 1, 0\}$, the distance from $x$ to the closed
unit disc.

articles.title: Weight of the annulus Hardy inequality
articles.statement:
For $x$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$,
$\phi(x) = \max\{|x| - 1, 0\}$, where $|x|$ is the Euclidean norm; this is the distance from $x$
to the closed unit disc.

articles.title: The plane of the critical weighted Sobolev inequality
articles.statement:
$\mathbb{R}^2$ denotes the Euclidean
plane, the space of pairs of real numbers with the Euclidean norm.

articles.title: Euclidean plane
articles.statement: The Euclidean plane.

articles.title: Donoho–Stark uncertainty principle
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let
$f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ be a nonzero function with discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. Then
$|G| \le |\{x \in G : f(x) \neq 0\}| \cdot |\{\psi : \hat f(\psi) \neq 0\}|$, where $\psi$ ranges
over the additive characters of $G$.

articles.title: Functions with small support and small Fourier support vanish
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian
group, let $A \subseteq G$, and let $B$ be a set of additive characters of $G$ with
$|A| \cdot |B| < |G|$. If $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ vanishes outside $A$ and its discrete Fourier
transform $\hat f$ vanishes outside $B$, then $f = 0$.

articles.title: Characters of a finite abelian group have absolute value one
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian
group and let $\psi$ be an additive character of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$, that is, a map
$\psi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\psi(0) = 1$ and $\psi(a + b) = \psi(a)\psi(b)$. Then
$|\psi(x)| = 1$ for every $x \in G$.

articles.title: Pointwise bound from a small Fourier support
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let
$f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be a set of additive characters of $G$ such that the discrete
Fourier transform $\hat f$ vanishes outside $B$. Then for every $x \in G$,
$|f(x)|^2 \le \frac{|B|}{|G|} \sum_{y \in G} |f(y)|^2$.

articles.title: Concentration bound for the Fourier transform of a function with small support
articles.statement:
Let $G$
be a finite abelian group, let $A \subseteq G$, let $B$ be any set of additive characters of $G$,
and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ vanish outside $A$, with discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. Then
$\sum_{\psi \in B} |\hat f(\psi)|^2 \le \frac{|A| \cdot |B|}{|G|} \sum_{\psi} |\hat f(\psi)|^2$,
where the last sum runs over all additive characters $\psi$ of $G$.

articles.title: Squared-norm Plancherel identity for the finite Fourier transform
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite
abelian group and $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, with discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. Then
$\sum_{\psi} |\hat f(\psi)|^2 = |G| \sum_{x \in G} |f(x)|^2$, where $\psi$ runs over all
additive characters of $G$.

articles.title: Concentration bound for a function with small Fourier support
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian
group, let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be a set of additive characters of $G$ such that
the discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$ vanishes outside $B$. Then for every $A \subseteq G$,
$\sum_{x \in A} |f(x)|^2 \le \frac{|A| \cdot |B|}{|G|} \sum_{x \in G} |f(x)|^2$.

articles.title: All-true function
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the all-true function on the Boolean cube of
dimension $n$ is the Boolean AND of all coordinates: it sends $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ to true
exactly when $x_i$ is true for every $i < n$. In dimension $0$ it is constantly true.

articles.title: Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ is the set of
functions $x : \{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$. It represents
$\{-1, 1\}^n$, with true standing for $1$ and false for $-1$.

articles.title: Empty Fourier coefficient of a constant function
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
real $c$, the normalized Fourier coefficient at the empty set of the constant function
$x \mapsto c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ equals $c$. This includes dimension $n = 0$.

articles.title: A character's own Fourier coefficient
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
$S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the character
$\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} x_i$ on $\{-1, 1\}^n$ equals $1$, that is,
$\widehat{\chi_S}(S) = 1$.

articles.title: The empty Fourier coefficient is the mean
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function
$f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the empty set is the
uniform mean of $f$: $\hat f(\emptyset) = \frac{1}{|\{-1, 1\}^n|} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x)$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of the zero function
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
$S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the identically zero
function on $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $0$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficient on the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a function
$f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ and a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is
$\hat f(S) = \frac{1}{|\{-1, 1\}^n|} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x) \chi_S(x)$, where
$\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} x_i$. That is, $\hat f(S)$ is the uniform expectation of $f \chi_S$.

articles.title: The two-bit AND has Boolean degree two
articles.statement:
The all-true function on the Boolean cube of
dimension $2$, $(x_0, x_1) \mapsto x_0 \wedge x_1$, has Boolean degree $2$; that is, its real
multilinear extension has total degree $2$.

articles.title: Constant functions have Boolean degree zero
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every Boolean
value $b$, the constant function $x \mapsto b$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Boolean
degree $0$.

articles.title: Coordinate projections have Boolean degree one
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
$i < n$, the coordinate projection $x \mapsto x_i$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has
Boolean degree $1$.

articles.title: Boolean degree
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a Boolean-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$
coordinates, and read true as $1$ and false as $0$. The Boolean degree of $f$ is the total degree
of the multilinear extension of $f$: the real multilinear polynomial in $n$ variables that takes
the value $f(x)$ at every point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$.

articles.title: Number of points of the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Boolean cube of
dimension $n$ has exactly $2^n$ points.

articles.title: Lagrange basis polynomial of a cube point
articles.statement:
Let $x$ be a point of the Boolean cube in $n$
coordinates, indexed by $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Its cube basis polynomial is the real
polynomial $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} \ell_i$ in the variables $X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}$, where $\ell_i = X_i$
if $x_i$ is true and $\ell_i = 1 - X_i$ if $x_i$ is false. Reading true as $1$ and false as $0$,
it is the Lagrange basis polynomial of $x$ on the grid $\{0,1\}^n$.

articles.title: The empty Fourier character is constant one
articles.statement:
For every $n$ and every point $x$ of the
Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, the Fourier character $\chi_\emptyset$ of the empty set of
coordinates satisfies $\chi_\emptyset(x) = 1$.

articles.title: Fourier characters square to one
articles.statement:
For every $n$, every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates and
every point $x$ of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, the Fourier character $\chi_S$ satisfies
$\chi_S(x) \cdot \chi_S(x) = 1$.

articles.title: Singleton Fourier characters are coordinate signs
articles.statement:
For every $n$, every coordinate $i$ and
every point $x$ of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, the Fourier character $\chi_{\{i\}}$ of
the singleton $\{i\}$ satisfies $\chi_{\{i\}}(x) = \sigma(x_i)$, where $\sigma$ is the sign of a
coordinate: $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.

articles.title: Fourier character on the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For a set $S$ of coordinates among $n$, the Fourier
character $\chi_S$ is the real-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates given by
$\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} \sigma(x_i)$, where $\sigma$ is the sign of a coordinate:
$\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.

articles.title: Sign of false
articles.statement: The sign $\sigma(\text{false})$ of the Boolean value false equals $-1$.

articles.title: Coordinate signs square to one
articles.statement:
For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$ satisfies
$\sigma(b) \cdot \sigma(b) = 1$.

articles.title: Sign of true
articles.statement: The sign $\sigma(\text{true})$ of the Boolean value true equals $1$.

articles.title: Sign of a Boolean coordinate
articles.statement:
The sign of a Boolean value $b$ is the real number
$\sigma(b)$ given by $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.

articles.title: Decoding a cube point as a subset
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in a
fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$; this order identifies subsets of $E$ with points of the
Boolean cube of dimension $m$. A point $x$ of that cube decodes to the subset
$\{e_j : x_j = \mathrm{false}\}$ of $E$; this inverts the encoding of subsets of $E$ as cube
points.

articles.title: Decoding inverts encoding
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in a fixed
order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$. Encode a subset $T \subseteq E$ as the point $x_T$ of the Boolean
cube of dimension $m$ whose $j$-th coordinate is false exactly when $e_j \in T$, and decode a
point $x$ as the subset $\{e_j : x_j = \mathrm{false}\}$. Then for every subset $T \subseteq E$,
decoding $x_T$ gives back $T$.

articles.title: Lagrange basis polynomials on the cube are point indicators
articles.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be points
of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and identify $y$ with the point of
$\{0,1\}^n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ when $y_i$ is true and $0$
when it is false. Then the cube basis polynomial of $x$ evaluated at $y$ equals $1$ if $x = y$
and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: The multilinear extension agrees with its function on the cube
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a Boolean
function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $y$ be a point of the cube, identified
with the point of $\{0,1\}^n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ when $y_i$
is true and $0$ when it is false. Then the real multilinear extension of $f$ evaluated at $y$
equals $1$ if $f(y)$ is true and $0$ if $f(y)$ is false.

articles.title: Subset characters agree with cube characters
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements,
listed in a fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$, and encode a subset $T \subseteq E$ as the point
$x_T$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$ whose $j$-th coordinate is false exactly when
$e_j \in T$. For all subsets $S, T \subseteq E$,

$$(-1)^{|S \cap T|} = \chi_{S'}(x_T),$$

where the left side is the Fourier character of $S$ at $T$, $S' = \{j : e_j \in S\}$ is $S$
reindexed as a set of coordinates, and $\chi_{S'}$ is the Fourier character on the cube.

articles.title: Fourier character on finite sets
articles.statement:
For finite sets $S$ and $T$, the Fourier character of
$S$ at $T$ is the real number $\chi_S(T) = (-1)^{|S \cap T|}$.

This is the subset-indexed form of the Fourier character on the Boolean cube; after reindexing
the coordinates, the two agree.

articles.title: Subset Fourier coefficients agree with cube Fourier coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite
subset of a type $\iota$ with $m$ elements, listed in a fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$, and
decode a point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$ as the subset
$D(x) = \{e_j : x_j = \mathrm{false}\}$ of $E$. Let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of
$\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$ and let $S \subseteq E$. Then the Fourier coefficient
$\hat f(S) = 2^{-m} \sum_{U \subseteq E} f(U) (-1)^{|S \cap U|}$ of $f$ at $S$ over $E$ equals
the Fourier coefficient on the cube of the function $x \mapsto f(D(x))$ at the set of
coordinates $S' = \{j : e_j \in S\}$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficient on the subsets of a finite set
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite subset of a type
$\iota$ and let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of $\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$. For a finite
subset $S$ of $\iota$, the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ over $E$ is

$$\hat f(S) = \frac{1}{2^{|E|}} \sum_{U \subseteq E} f(U) \, (-1)^{|S \cap U|},$$

the uniform average over the subsets $U$ of $E$ of $f(U)$ times the Fourier character
$\chi_S(U) = (-1)^{|S \cap U|}$.

After reindexing, it agrees with the Fourier coefficient on the Boolean cube.

articles.title: Fourier inversion on the subsets of a finite set
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite subset of a type
$\iota$ and let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of $\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$. For every
subset $T \subseteq E$,

$$f(T) = \sum_{S \subseteq E} \hat f(S) \, (-1)^{|S \cap T|},$$

where $\hat f(S) = 2^{-|E|} \sum_{U \subseteq E} f(U) (-1)^{|S \cap U|}$ is the Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $S$ over $E$ and $(-1)^{|S \cap T|}$ is the Fourier character of $S$ at
$T$.

articles.title: Plancherel identity on the subsets of a finite set
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite subset of a type
$\iota$ and let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of $\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$. Then

$$\frac{1}{2^{|E|}} \sum_{T \subseteq E} f(T)^2 = \sum_{S \subseteq E} \hat f(S)^2,$$

where $\hat f(S) = 2^{-|E|} \sum_{U \subseteq E} f(U) (-1)^{|S \cap U|}$ is the Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $S$ over $E$: the mean square of $f$ over the subsets of $E$ equals the
sum of the squared Fourier coefficients.

articles.title: Fourier degree bounds are monotone
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean
cube of dimension $n$, and let $d \le e$ be natural numbers. If $f$ has Fourier degree at most
$d$, then $f$ has Fourier degree at most $e$.

articles.title: Fourier degree is at most Boolean degree
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the Boolean
cube of dimension $n$, and let $g$ be the real function with $g(x) = 1$ if $f(x)$ is true and
$g(x) = 0$ otherwise. Then $g$ has Fourier degree at most the Boolean degree of $f$: every
Fourier coefficient $\hat g(S)$ with $|S|$ greater than the total degree of the multilinear
extension of $f$ vanishes.

articles.title: Fourier degree is at most the dimension
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the
Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $d \ge n$ be a natural number. Then $f$ has Fourier
degree at most $d$.

articles.title: The zero function satisfies every Fourier degree bound
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$ and
$d$, the zero function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Fourier degree at most $d$.

articles.title: Fourier degree at most $d$
articles.statement:
A real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube of dimension
$n$ has Fourier degree at most a natural number $d$ when its Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)$
vanishes for every set $S$ of coordinates with $|S| > d$.

This is the degree of the multilinear polynomial representing the function on the cube.

articles.title: Multilinear extension of the AND function
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the real
multilinear extension of the AND function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ (true exactly
when every coordinate is true) is the monomial $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} X_i$.

articles.title: Multilinear extension of a constant function
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$ and every
Boolean value $b$, the real multilinear extension of the constant function $b$ on the Boolean
cube of dimension $n$ is the constant polynomial $1$ if $b$ is true and the constant
polynomial $0$ if $b$ is false.

articles.title: Multilinear extension of a coordinate projection
articles.statement:
For every coordinate $i$ of the
Boolean cube of dimension $n$, the real multilinear extension of the projection $x \mapsto x_i$
is the variable $X_i$.

articles.title: Multilinear extension
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a Boolean-valued function on the Boolean cube of
dimension $n$, and read each coordinate and each value as $1$ for true and $0$ for false. The real
multilinear extension of $f$ is the polynomial in $\mathbb{R}[X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}]$

$$\sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} f(x) \prod_{i < n} \bigl(x_i X_i + (1 - x_i)(1 - X_i)\bigr).$$

For each cube point $x$ the product is its Lagrange basis polynomial: it evaluates to $1$ at $x$
and to $0$ at every other point of $\{0,1\}^n$. Hence the extension agrees with $f$ on
$\{0,1\}^n$, and it is the unique polynomial of degree at most one in each variable that does.

articles.title: Coordinates of an encoded subset
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in
the fixed order $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$ used to encode subsets of $E$ as points of the Boolean cube
of dimension $m$. For every subset $T \subseteq E$ and every coordinate $j < m$, the $j$-th
coordinate of the point encoding $T$ is true if $e_j \notin T$ and false if $e_j \in T$.

articles.title: Subsets of a finite set as points of the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For a finite set $E$ with $n = |E|$
elements, fix a bijection $e$ from $E$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (an enumeration of $E$, chosen
noncanonically). This is the bijection from the subsets $T \subseteq E$ to the Boolean cube of
dimension $n$ that sends $T$ to the point $x$ with $x_{e(a)} = \mathrm{false}$ if $a \in T$ and
$x_{e(a)} = \mathrm{true}$ if $a \notin T$, for every $a \in E$.

articles.title: Subsets of a finite set as indicator functions
articles.statement:
For a finite set $E$, this is the
bijection from the subsets $T \subseteq E$ to the functions $b$ from $E$ to
$\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ given by $b(a) = \mathrm{false}$ if $a \in T$ and
$b(a) = \mathrm{true}$ if $a \notin T$. Its inverse sends $b$ to the set
$\{a \in E : b(a) = \mathrm{false}\}$.

Members of $T$ read false, matching the convention that identifies false with the sign $-1$
and true with the sign $+1$.

articles.title: Reindexing a subset as a set of coordinates
articles.statement:
For finite sets $S \subseteq E$ with $n = |E|$,
let $e$ be the fixed bijection from $E$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (the enumeration of $E$ used to
identify subsets of $E$ with points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$). The reindexed set is
