the image $e(S) = \{e(a) : a \in S\}$, a subset of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

articles.title: Translation modulates the discrete Fourier transform
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group,
$f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, $t \in G$, and $\psi$ an additive character of $G$ with values in
$\mathbb{C}$, and write $\hat h(\psi) = \sum_{x \in G} \psi(x) h(x)$ for the discrete Fourier
transform of $h : G \to \mathbb{C}$. If $g(x) = f(x - t)$ for all $x \in G$, then
$\hat g(\psi) = \psi(t) \hat f(\psi)$.

Proof: reindex the finite sum by $x \mapsto x + t$ and use $\psi(x + t) = \psi(x) \psi(t)$.

## Sources

- A. Terras, Fourier Analysis on Finite Groups and Applications, Ch. 2 (translation and modulation).

articles.title: Discrete Fourier transform on a finite abelian group
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and
$f : G \to \mathbb{C}$. The discrete Fourier transform of $f$ is the function on the additive
characters $\psi$ of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$ (maps with $\psi(0) = 1$ and
$\psi(a + b) = \psi(a)\psi(b)$) given by $\hat f(\psi) = \sum_{x \in G} \psi(x) f(x)$.

No complex conjugate is applied to the character.

articles.title: Fourier inversion on a finite abelian group
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|$
elements, let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, and write $\hat f(\psi) = \sum_{y \in G} \psi(y) f(y)$ for
the discrete Fourier transform of $f$ at an additive character $\psi$ of $G$ with values in
$\mathbb{C}$. Then for every $x \in G$,
$f(x) = \frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{\psi} \overline{\psi(x)} \, \hat f(\psi)$, where $\psi$ runs over
all additive characters of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$.

Proof: expand the transform and collapse the inner sum with the orthogonality of characters.
This is the Fourier inversion formula (4.4) of K. Conrad, Characters of finite abelian groups,
Section 4, https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/grouptheory/charthy.pdf, up to reindexing
$\psi \mapsto \psi^{-1}$ (Conrad conjugates the character in the transform rather than in the
inversion sum).

## Sources

- A. Terras, Fourier Analysis on Finite Groups and Applications, Ch. 2, Fourier inversion theorem.

articles.title: Plancherel formula on a finite abelian group
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|$
elements, let $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$, and write $\hat h(\psi) = \sum_{x \in G} \psi(x) h(x)$
for the discrete Fourier transform of $h : G \to \mathbb{C}$ at an additive character $\psi$ of
$G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$. Then $\sum_{x \in G} \overline{f(x)} \, g(x)$ equals
$\frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{\psi} \overline{\hat f(\psi)} \, \hat g(\psi)$, where $\psi$ runs over all
additive characters of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$.

Proof: apply Fourier inversion to $g$, exchange the finite sums, and identify the conjugated
inner sum with $\overline{\hat f(\psi)}$. K. Conrad, Characters of finite abelian groups,
Section 4, proves the same identity by checking it on characters.

## Sources

- A. Terras, Fourier Analysis on Finite Groups and Applications, Ch. 2, Plancherel formula.

articles.title: The $p = 1$ endpoint of Hausdorff–Young
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and
$f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, with discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. For every additive character
$\psi$ of $G$, $|\hat f(\psi)| \le \sum_{x \in G} |f(x)|$.

articles.title: Hausdorff–Young inequality on a finite abelian group
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian
group, let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ have discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$, let $p$ be a real
number with $1 < p \le 2$, and let $q = p/(p - 1)$. Write $|G|$ for the number of elements
of $G$ and let $\psi$ run over the additive characters of $G$. Then
$\left(\sum_{\psi} |\hat f(\psi)|^q\right)^{1/q} \le
|G|^{1/q} \left(\sum_{x \in G} |f(x)|^p\right)^{1/p}$.

The statement also assumes $\sigma$-algebras on $G$ and on its character group in which
singletons are measurable; on a finite set such a $\sigma$-algebra contains every subset, so
this is no restriction.

articles.title: The $p = 2$ endpoint of Hausdorff–Young (Plancherel)
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian
group and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ have discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. Then, with
$\psi$ running over the additive characters of $G$ and $|G|$ the number of elements of $G$,
$\sum_{\psi} |\hat f(\psi)|^2 = |G| \sum_{x \in G} |f(x)|^2$.

articles.title: Coordinate signs have absolute value one
articles.statement:
For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$,
which is $1$ for true and $-1$ for false, satisfies $|\sigma(b)| = 1$.

articles.title: Additivity of Fourier coefficients
articles.statement:
For all real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the
Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient
of $f + g$ at $S$ is the sum of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at $S$:
$\widehat{f + g}(S) = \hat f(S) + \hat g(S)$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of the noise operator
articles.statement:
For every real $\rho$, every real-valued
function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the
Fourier coefficient at $S$ of $T_\rho f$, the noise operator with parameter $\rho$ applied to $f$,
is $\widehat{T_\rho f}(S) = \rho^{|S|} \hat f(S)$.

articles.title: Flipping a coordinate negates the Fourier coefficients of the sets containing it
articles.statement:
Let $f$
be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, let $i$ be a coordinate, and
let $g(x) = f(x^{\oplus i})$, where $x^{\oplus i}$ is the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate
flipped. Write $\hat f(S)$ and $\hat g(S)$ for the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at a set
$S$ of the $n$ coordinates. Then for every such $S$, $\hat g(S) = -\hat f(S)$ if $i \in S$ and
$\hat g(S) = \hat f(S)$ if $i \notin S$.

articles.title: Homogeneity of Fourier coefficients
articles.statement:
For every real $c$, every real-valued function $f$
on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier
coefficient of $c f$ at $S$ is $c$ times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$:
$\widehat{c f}(S) = c \hat f(S)$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of a constant function
articles.statement:
For every real $c$ and every set $S$ of the
$n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the constant function $x \mapsto c$ on the
Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates is $c$ if $S = \emptyset$ and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of a character
articles.statement:
For all sets $S$ and $T$ of the $n$ coordinates, the
Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the Fourier character $\chi_T$ on the Boolean cube in $n$
coordinates, $\chi_T(x) = \prod_{i \in T} \sigma(x_i)$ with $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and
$\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$, is $1$ if $T = S$ and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients as averages
articles.statement:
For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube
in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)$
is the average of $f(x) \chi_S(x)$ over all points $x$ of the cube,
$\hat f(S) = \mathbb{E}_x [f(x) \chi_S(x)]$, where $\chi_S$ is the Fourier character of $S$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients as sums over the cube
articles.statement:
For every real-valued function $f$ on the
Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient
of $f$ at $S$ is $\hat f(S) = \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_x f(x) \chi_S(x)$, where the sum runs over all
points $x$ of the cube and $\chi_S$ is the Fourier character of $S$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients determine the function
articles.statement:
If two real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on
the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates have the same Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S) = \hat g(S)$ at
every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, then $f = g$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of a difference
articles.statement:
For real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the
Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the Fourier coefficient
of $f - g$ at $S$ is $\widehat{f - g}(S) = \hat f(S) - \hat g(S)$.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the Fourier expansion
articles.statement:
For real numbers $a_T$ indexed by the sets
$T \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $g(x) = \sum_T a_T \chi_T(x)$ on the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$, where $\chi_T$ is the Fourier character of $T$. Then for every set
$S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ the Fourier coefficient of $g$ at $S$ is $\hat g(S) = a_S$.

articles.title: Constant functions have zero influence
articles.statement:
For every real number $c$ and every coordinate
$i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of coordinate $i$ on the constant function with value $c$
on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $0$.

articles.title: Influence of a Boolean function as a flip probability
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a real-valued function
on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ that takes only the values $1$ and $-1$, and let
$i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then the influence of coordinate $i$ on $f$ equals the probability,
for $x$ uniform on the cube, that $f(x^{\oplus i}) \ne f(x)$, where $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with
its $i$-th coordinate flipped.

articles.title: Fourier formula for influence
articles.statement:
For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of coordinate $i$ on
$f$ is $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \sum_{S \ni i} \hat f(S)^2$, where $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and the sum runs over the sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that
contain $i$.

articles.title: Influences are nonnegative
articles.statement:
For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$ of
coordinate $i$ on $f$ satisfies $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \ge 0$.

articles.title: Influence of a coordinate
articles.statement:
For a real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ and a coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of $i$ on $f$ is
$\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \mathbb{E}_x\big[\big((f(x) - f(x^{\oplus i})) / 2\big)^2\big]$, where the
expectation is over $x$ uniform on the cube and $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate
flipped.

articles.title: Semigroup property of the noise operator
articles.statement:
For all real numbers $\rho$ and $\sigma$ and every
real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$, applying the noise operator $T_\sigma$
and then $T_\rho$ to $f$ gives $T_{\rho\sigma} f$: $T_\rho(T_\sigma f) = T_{\rho\sigma} f$.

articles.title: The noise operator fixes constants
articles.statement:
For every real number $\rho$ and every real number $c$,
the noise operator $T_\rho$ maps the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ to itself.

articles.title: Characters are eigenfunctions of the noise operator
articles.statement:
For every real number $\rho$ and every
set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ maps the Fourier character $\chi_S$
on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to the function $x \mapsto \rho^{|S|} \chi_S(x)$, so $\chi_S$ is
an eigenfunction of $T_\rho$ with eigenvalue $\rho^{|S|}$.

articles.title: Fourier expansion of the noise operator
articles.statement:
For every real number $\rho$, every function $f$
from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$ and every point $x$ of the cube,

$$T_\rho f(x) = \sum_{S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}} \rho^{|S|} \, \hat f(S) \, \chi_S(x),$$

where $T_\rho$ is the noise operator, $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$,
$\chi_S$ is the Fourier character of $S$, and $\rho^0 = 1$ also when $\rho = 0$.

articles.title: Positivity of the noise operator
articles.statement:
For every real number $\rho$ with $|\rho| \le 1$, the
noise operator $T_\rho$ on the Boolean cube maps nonnegative functions to nonnegative functions:
if $f$ is a real function on the cube with $f(y) \ge 0$ for every point $y$, then
$T_\rho f(x) \ge 0$ for every point $x$ of the cube.

articles.title: The noise operator $T_1$ is the identity
articles.statement:
For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the noise operator with $\rho = 1$ fixes $f$: $T_1 f = f$.

articles.title: The noise operator $T_0$ takes the mean
articles.statement:
For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the noise operator with $\rho = 0$ sends $f$ to the constant
function whose value is the mean $\mathbb{E}_x f(x) = 2^{-n} \sum_x f(x)$ of $f$ under the
uniform distribution.

articles.title: Noise operator on the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For a real number $\rho$ and a function $f$ from the
Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ sends $f$ to the function

$$T_\rho f(x) = \sum_y \Bigl(\prod_{i < n} \frac{1 + \rho \sigma(x_i) \sigma(y_i)}{2}\Bigr) f(y),$$

where $y$ runs over all points of the cube and $\sigma$ is the sign of a coordinate:
$\sigma(\mathrm{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\mathrm{false}) = -1$.

For $-1 \le \rho \le 1$, $T_\rho f(x)$ is the expectation of $f(y)$ when each coordinate of $y$
independently equals the corresponding coordinate of $x$ with probability $(1 + \rho) / 2$; the
formula is used for every real $\rho$.

articles.title: Constant functions have zero total influence
articles.statement:
For every real number $c$, the constant
function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ has total influence $0$.

articles.title: Total influence in Fourier form
articles.statement:
For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the total influence of $f$ is

$$\mathrm{I}[f] = \sum_{S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}} |S| \, \hat f(S)^2,$$

where $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.

articles.title: Total influence is nonnegative
articles.statement:
For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the total influence of $f$ is nonnegative.

articles.title: Total influence on the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For a function $f$ from the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the total influence of $f$ is the sum of the influences of its $n$
coordinates, $\mathrm{I}[f] = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$, where
$\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \mathbb{E}_x \left[\left(\frac{f(x) - f(x^{\oplus i})}{2}\right)^2\right]$,
$x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped and $\mathbb{E}_x$ is the uniform average
over the points $x$ of the cube.

articles.title: Constant functions have zero variance
articles.statement:
For every real number $c$, the constant function
with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ has variance $0$ under the uniform
distribution.

articles.title: Variance as mean square minus squared mean
articles.statement:
For every function
$f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform
distribution equals $\mathbb{E}_x[f(x)^2] - (\mathbb{E}_x[f(x)])^2$, where $\mathbb{E}_x$
denotes the uniform average over the $2^n$ points $x$ of the cube.

articles.title: Variance in terms of Fourier coefficients
articles.statement:
For every function
$f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform
distribution equals $\sum_{S \neq \emptyset} \hat f(S)^2$, where the sum runs over the nonempty
sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.

articles.title: Poincaré inequality on the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For every function
$f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform
distribution is at most the total influence of $f$: $\mathrm{Var}[f] \le I[f]$.

articles.title: Variance on the Boolean cube is nonnegative
articles.statement:
For every function
$f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform
distribution is at least $0$.

articles.title: Variance on the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For a function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the
Boolean cube, its variance under the uniform distribution is
$\mathrm{Var}[f] = \mathbb{E}_x\big[(f(x) - \mathbb{E}_y[f(y)])^2\big]$, where $\mathbb{E}_x$
denotes the uniform average over the $2^n$ points $x$ of the cube.

articles.title: Flipping a coordinate in a Fourier character
articles.statement:
Let $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let
$x$ be a point of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, let $i < n$, and write $x^{\oplus i}$ for
$x$ with coordinate $i$ flipped. Then the Fourier character $\chi_S$ satisfies
$\chi_S(x^{\oplus i}) = -\chi_S(x)$ if $i \in S$, and $\chi_S(x^{\oplus i}) = \chi_S(x)$ if
$i \notin S$.

articles.title: Coordinate signs are nonzero
articles.statement:
For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$ (equal
to $1$ for true and $-1$ for false) is nonzero.

articles.title: Sign of a negated Boolean value
articles.statement:
For every Boolean value $b$, the sign of its negation
is the negative of its sign: $\sigma(\lnot b) = -\sigma(b)$, where $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$
and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.

articles.title: The noise operator preserves the mean
articles.statement:
For every real $\rho$ and every function
$f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the uniform average over the cube of
$T_\rho f$, the image of $f$ under the noise operator with parameter $\rho$, equals the uniform
average of $f$.

articles.title: Averages are invariant under flipping a coordinate
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be an additive commutative
monoid that is a module over the nonnegative rationals, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean
cube in $n$ coordinates to $M$, and let $i < n$. Writing $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with coordinate
$i$ flipped, the uniform average of $f(x^{\oplus i})$ over all points $x$ of the cube equals the
uniform average of $f(x)$.

articles.title: Average over the Boolean cube as the empty Fourier coefficient
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$
and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average $\mathbb{E}_x f(x)$ of $f$
over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ equals the Fourier coefficient $\hat f(\emptyset)$ of $f$ at
the empty set.

articles.title: Uniform average over the Boolean cube as a sum
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f$ over the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $\mathbb{E}_x f(x) = \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x)$.

articles.title: Plancherel's identity on the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all functions
$f, g : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f g$ over the Boolean cube
$\{-1, 1\}^n$ is the sum, over all sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, of the products of the
Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at $S$:
$\mathbb{E}_x f(x) g(x) = \sum_S \hat f(S) \hat g(S)$.

articles.title: Parseval's identity on the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function
$f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f^2$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$
is the sum, over all sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, of the squares of the Fourier
coefficients of $f$ at $S$: $\mathbb{E}_x f(x)^2 = \sum_S \hat f(S)^2$.

articles.title: A coordinate flip fixes the other coordinates
articles.statement:
For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of
dimension $n$ and all coordinates $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $j \ne i$, the $j$-th
coordinate of $x^{\oplus i}$, the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped, is $x_j$.

articles.title: A coordinate flip negates the flipped coordinate
articles.statement:
For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube
of dimension $n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the $i$-th coordinate of
$x^{\oplus i}$, the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped, is the negation $\lnot x_i$ of
$x_i$ (true and false exchanged).

articles.title: Flipping a coordinate twice
articles.statement:
For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and
every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, writing $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with its $i$-th
coordinate flipped, we have $(x^{\oplus i})^{\oplus i} = x$.

articles.title: Flipping a coordinate is an involution
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every coordinate
$i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the map $x \mapsto x^{\oplus i}$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$,
which flips the $i$-th coordinate, is an involution: applying it twice gives the identity.

articles.title: A coordinate flip moves every point
articles.statement:
For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension
$n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the point $x^{\oplus i}$ obtained from $x$ by
flipping its $i$-th coordinate is different from $x$.

articles.title: Coordinate flip on the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
For a point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$
and a coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the point $x^{\oplus i}$ is obtained from $x$ by
negating its $i$-th coordinate (exchanging true and false) and leaving every other coordinate
unchanged.

articles.title: Fourier inversion on the Boolean cube
articles.statement:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $f$ be a real-valued
function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $x$ be a point of the cube. For each subset
$S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ let $\hat f(S)$ be the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and $\chi_S$
the Fourier character of $S$. Then $\sum_S \hat f(S) \chi_S(x) = f(x)$, the sum ranging over all
subsets $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

articles.title: Flipping a coordinate preserves sums over the cube
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be an additive commutative
monoid, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $f$ a function from the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ to $M$, and
$i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. For a point $x$ of the cube write $x^{\oplus i}$ for the point $x$ with
its $i$-th coordinate flipped. Then $\sum_x f(x^{\oplus i}) = \sum_x f(x)$, both sums ranging over
all points $x$ of the cube.

articles.title: Dual orthogonality of the Boolean cube characters
articles.statement:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $x, y$ be
points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$. For each subset $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ let
$\chi_S$ be the Fourier character of $S$. Then $\sum_S \chi_S(x) \chi_S(y)$, the sum ranging over
all subsets $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, equals $2^n$ if $x = y$ and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Sum of a Boolean cube character
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every subset $S$ of
$\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the sum of the Fourier character $\chi_S$ over all points of the Boolean cube
of dimension $n$ equals $2^n$ if $S$ is empty and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Orthogonality of the Boolean cube characters
articles.statement:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $S$ and $T$ be
subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $\chi_S$ and $\chi_T$ be their Fourier characters. Then
$\sum_x \chi_S(x) \chi_T(x)$, the sum ranging over all points $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension
$n$, equals $2^n$ if $S = T$ and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Convolution theorem for the discrete Fourier transform
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$. For
$\varphi : \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ write
$\hat\varphi(k) = \sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}} e^{-2\pi i jk/n} \varphi(j)$ for its discrete
Fourier transform, and let $\mathcal{F}^{-1}$ be the inverse of the map
$\varphi \mapsto \hat\varphi$. Then for all $f, g : \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every
$t \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, the value at $t$ of $\mathcal{F}^{-1}$ applied to
$k \mapsto \hat f(k)\,\hat g(k)$ equals the circular convolution
$\sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}} f(j)\,g(t - j)$.

## Sources

- MIT 6.046J Spring 2015 Lecture 3, polynomial product theorem, cyclic form.

articles.title: Riesz–Thorin interpolation on finite sets, auxiliary form
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ and $\kappa$ be
finite sets, each with a σ-algebra in which singletons are measurable and with the counting
measure, and write $\|g\|_r \in [0, \infty]$ for the $\ell^r$ norm of $g$ with respect to the
counting measure. Let $p_0, p_1, p, q_0, q_1, q \in [1, \infty]$ and $\theta \in [0, 1]$ satisfy
$1/p = (1-\theta)/p_0 + \theta/p_1$ and $1/q = (1-\theta)/q_0 + \theta/q_1$, where $1/\infty = 0$.
Let $M_0, M_1 \in [0, \infty]$ and let $T : \mathbb{C}^\iota \to \mathbb{C}^\kappa$ be a
$\mathbb{C}$-linear map with $\|Tf\|_{q_0} \le M_0 \|f\|_{p_0}$ and
$\|Tf\|_{q_1} \le M_1 \|f\|_{p_1}$ for all $f \in \mathbb{C}^\iota$. Then
$\|Tf\|_q \le M_0^{1-\theta} M_1^{\theta} \|f\|_p$ for all $f \in \mathbb{C}^\iota$, where
products and powers are computed in $[0, \infty]$ with $0 \cdot \infty = 0$ and $c^0 = 1$.

This is the Riesz–Thorin interpolation theorem on finite sets with finiteness assumed as a
property rather than given by an explicit enumeration of the elements; that theorem is derived
from this one.

articles.title: Riesz–Thorin interpolation theorem on finite sets
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ and $\kappa$ be finite
sets, each with a σ-algebra in which singletons are measurable and with the counting measure, and
write $\|g\|_r \in [0, \infty]$ for the $\ell^r$ norm of $g$ with respect to the counting measure.
Let $p_0, p_1, p, q_0, q_1, q \in [1, \infty]$ and $\theta \in [0, 1]$ satisfy
$1/p = (1-\theta)/p_0 + \theta/p_1$ and $1/q = (1-\theta)/q_0 + \theta/q_1$, where $1/\infty = 0$.
Let $M_0, M_1 \in [0, \infty]$ and let $T : \mathbb{C}^\iota \to \mathbb{C}^\kappa$ be a
$\mathbb{C}$-linear map with $\|Tf\|_{q_0} \le M_0 \|f\|_{p_0}$ and
$\|Tf\|_{q_1} \le M_1 \|f\|_{p_1}$ for all $f \in \mathbb{C}^\iota$. Then
$\|Tf\|_q \le M_0^{1-\theta} M_1^{\theta} \|f\|_p$ for all $f \in \mathbb{C}^\iota$, where
products and powers are computed in $[0, \infty]$ with $0 \cdot \infty = 0$ and $c^0 = 1$.

## Sources

- M. Riesz, Sur les maxima des formes bilinéaires et sur les fonctionnelles linéaires, Acta Math. 49 (1927), 465–497, DOI 10.1007/BF02564121; and G. O. Thorin, Convexity theorems generalizing those of M. Riesz and Hadamard with some applications, Comm. Sem. Math. Univ. Lund 9 (1948), 1–58, Riesz-Thorin interpolation theorem; Stein-Shakarchi Complex interpolation; Lean states finite counting-measure complex `→ₗ[ℂ]` form with explicit interpolation identities `p⁻¹=(1-θ)p₀⁻¹+θp₁⁻¹` and bound `M₀^(1-θ)M₁^θ`.

articles.title: Convolution on a finite abelian group is associative
articles.statement:
For a finite abelian group $G$
and functions $f, g, h : G \to \mathbb{C}$, we have $(f * g) * h = f * (g * h)$, where the
convolution is $(f * g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\,g(x - y)$.

articles.title: Convolution on a finite abelian group is commutative
articles.statement:
For a finite abelian group $G$
and functions $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$, we have $f * g = g * f$, where the convolution is
$(f * g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\,g(x - y)$.

articles.title: The delta function is a left identity for convolution
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian
group and let $\delta_0 : G \to \mathbb{C}$ be the function with $\delta_0(0) = 1$ and
$\delta_0(y) = 0$ for $y \ne 0$. Then $\delta_0 * g = g$ for every $g : G \to \mathbb{C}$,
where the convolution is $(f * g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\,g(x - y)$.

articles.title: Convolution on a finite abelian group
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. The
convolution of functions $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$ is the function $f * g : G \to \mathbb{C}$
given by $(f * g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\,g(x - y)$, with no normalizing factor $1/|G|$,
where $|G|$ is the number of elements of $G$.

articles.title: Young's convolution inequality on a finite abelian group
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian
group and, for $u : G \to \mathbb{C}$ and real $s > 0$, write
$\|u\|_s = \left(\sum_{x \in G} |u(x)|^s\right)^{1/s}$. Let $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$ and let
$p, q, r$ be real numbers with $p > 1$, $q > 1$, $r > 1$ and $1/p + 1/q = 1 + 1/r$. Then the
convolution $(f * g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\,g(x - y)$ satisfies
$\|f * g\|_r \le \|f\|_p \, \|g\|_q$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of the lifted periodic function
articles.statement:
The Fourier coefficients of the descended function are the interval
coefficients `fourierCoeffOn`.

articles.title: Coefficient identity for a `C¹` periodic function
articles.statement:
For `n ≠ 0`,
`ĉₙ(f) = (T / (2π i n)) · ĉₙ(f')`. The boundary term in integration by parts
vanishes by periodicity.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients on $(0, 0+T)$ equal those on $(0, T)$
articles.statement:
The interval coefficients on `(0, 0 + T]` agree with those on `(0, T]`; this
bridges Mathlib's `fourierCoeff_liftIoc_eq`, which is stated on `(a, a + T]`.

articles.title: Pointwise convergence on one period
articles.statement: **Pointwise convergence on one period.**

articles.title: Uniform convergence:
articles.statement:
The Fourier series of a `C¹` periodic function
converges uniformly (in `C(AddCircle T, ℂ)`) to `f` on the circle.

articles.title: Functions with absolutely convergent Fourier series
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$. A continuous function
$f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ lies in the Wiener algebra when the family of its
Fourier coefficients $\hat f(n) = \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T f(x) e^{-2\pi i n x / T} \, dx$,
$n \in \mathbb{Z}$, is summable in $\mathbb{C}$.

For complex families, summability is equivalent to
$\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} |\hat f(n)| < \infty$.

articles.title: Wiener algebra on the circle
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$. A continuous function
$f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ lies in the Wiener algebra when the family of its
Fourier coefficients $\hat f(n) = \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T f(x) e^{-2\pi i n x / T} \, dx$,
$n \in \mathbb{Z}$, is summable in $\mathbb{C}$.

For complex families, summability is equivalent to $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} |\hat f(n)| < \infty$,
so these are the functions with absolutely convergent Fourier series.

articles.title: Lifted periodic function agrees with the original on a period
articles.statement: The descended function agrees with `f` on the period `(0, T]`.

articles.title: Lift of a periodic continuous function to the circle
articles.statement:
A `T`-periodic continuous function descends to a continuous function on the
circle `AddCircle T`, via `AddCircle.liftIoc`.

articles.title: Continuous functions are square-integrable on one period
articles.statement: A continuous function on `ℝ` is square-integrable on one period.

articles.title: Norm form of the coefficient identity
articles.statement: **Norm form of the coefficient identity.**

articles.title: Fourier coefficient bounded by the sup norm on a period
articles.statement: A Fourier coefficient bounded by the sup norm on one period.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of a `C¹` periodic function are absolutely summable
articles.statement: **Fourier coefficients of a `C¹` periodic function are absolutely summable.**

articles.title: Decay rate:
articles.statement: `n · ‖ĉₙ(f)‖ → 0` along the cofinite filter.

articles.title: Wiener's 1/f theorem
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$, and let $f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ be
a continuous function in the Wiener algebra with $f(x) \ne 0$ for every $x$. Then there is a
continuous function $g : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ with $g(x) = f(x)^{-1}$ for every
$x$, and $g$ lies in the Wiener algebra.

## Sources

- N. Wiener, Tauberian theorems, Ann. of Math. 33 (1932), 1-100. Listed as §226 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Knill, §226. Problem `wiener_inverse_closed` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Wiener–Lévy theorem
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$, and let $f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ be a
continuous function in the Wiener algebra. Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be an open set containing
the range of $f$, and let $\varphi : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic at every point of $U$.
Then there is a continuous function $g : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ with
$g(x) = \varphi(f(x))$ for every $x$, and $g$ lies in the Wiener algebra.

## Sources

- P. Lévy, Sur la convergence absolue des séries de Fourier, Compositio Math. 1 (1935), 1-14; N. Wiener, Tauberian theorems, Ann. of Math. 33 (1932), 1-100. Listed as §226 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Knill, §226. Problem `wiener_levy_analytic_calculus` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Bartuccelli–Deane–Zelik constant $\beta$
articles.statement:
Let
$\beta = \pi \left( 2\gamma + 2 \log 2 + 3 \log \pi - 4 \log \Gamma(\tfrac14) \right)$, where
$\gamma$ is the Euler–Mascheroni constant and $\Gamma$ is the gamma function.

This is the exact constant from the Appendix of the source, not a decimal approximation.

## Sources

- arXiv:1012.2061v1, Appendix constant formula, lines 1901-1915.

articles.title: Extremal coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a kernel-admissible extremal parameter and write
$|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$ for $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$. The extremal coefficients $c_p(k)$, complex
numbers indexed by $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, are as follows. If $p$ is a finite parameter $\mu$, then
$c_p(0) = 0$ and $c_p(k) = 2\pi / (|k|^2 (1 + \mu |k|^2))$ for $k \neq 0$. If $p$ is the
first-shell parameter, then $c_p(k) = \pi$ when $|k|^2 = 1$ and $c_p(k) = 0$ otherwise. If $p$ is
the biharmonic parameter, then $c_p(0) = 0$ and $c_p(k) = 2\pi / |k|^4$ for $k \neq 0$.

The values are real and do not depend on the proof of admissibility.

articles.title: Extremal parameters
articles.statement:
An extremal parameter is either a finite extremal parameter, that
is, a real number $\mu$ with $\mu < -1$ or $\mu > 0$, or one of two further parameters: the
first-shell parameter, standing for the endpoint $\mu = -1$, and the biharmonic parameter,
standing for the endpoint $\mu = \infty$.

Together these cover the parameter domain $(-\infty, -1] \cup (0, \infty]$, the two endpoints
being represented by limiting coefficient families rather than by values of $\mu$.

articles.title: Finite extremal parameters
articles.statement:
A finite extremal parameter is a real number $\mu$ with
$\mu < -1$ or $\mu > 0$.

The endpoints $\mu = -1$ and $\mu = \infty$ are not finite extremal parameters; the extremal
parameter domain adds them separately.

articles.title: Explicit extremals
articles.statement:
A continuous real function $u$ on the torus
$\mathbb{T} = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ is an explicit extremal when there are a
kernel-admissible extremal parameter $p$ and a real number $a \neq 0$ such that the extremal
coefficients $c_p(k)$ are summable over $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the Fourier coefficient
$\hat u(k) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_{[0, 2\pi]^2} u(x) e^{-i k \cdot x} \, dx$ equals $a \, c_p(k)$
for every $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, and
$u(x) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} a \, c_p(k) \, e^{i k \cdot x}$ for every
$x \in \mathbb{T}$.

articles.title: Kernel-admissible extremal parameters
articles.statement:
Write $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$ for a frequency
$k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$. A finite extremal parameter $\mu$ is kernel-admissible when
$|k|^2 \neq 0$ and $1 + \mu |k|^2 \neq 0$ for every nonzero frequency $k$; the first-shell
parameter is always kernel-admissible; the biharmonic parameter is kernel-admissible when
$|k|^2 \neq 0$ for every nonzero frequency $k$.

These conditions make every reciprocal in the extremal coefficients well defined.

articles.title: Same extremal orbit
articles.statement:
Two continuous real functions $u$ and $v$ on the torus
$\mathbb{T} = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ lie in the same extremal orbit when there are a
real number $a \neq 0$ and a point $x_0 \in \mathbb{T}$ such that $v(x) = a \, u(x - x_0)$ for
every $x \in \mathbb{T}$.

articles.title: Axis frequency
articles.statement:
For $i \in \{0, 1\}$, the axis frequency $e_i$ is the frequency in
$\mathbb{Z}^2$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ and whose other coordinate is $0$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of the lowest-shell witness
articles.statement:
For every frequency $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$,
the Fourier coefficient of the lowest-shell witness at $k$ equals $1/2$ if $k$ lies in the
lowest shell, that is, $k$ is one of $(1, 0)$, $(-1, 0)$, $(0, 1)$, $(0, -1)$, and equals $0$
otherwise.

articles.title: Fourier reconstruction
articles.statement:
Let $u$ be a continuous real function on the torus of period
$2\pi$ in each coordinate, let $a_k$ ($k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$) be its Fourier coefficients, and let
$c_k = a_k / (2\pi)$ be the Fourier coefficients, with respect to normalized Haar measure, of its
unit representative on $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$. If the family $(c_k)_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2}$
is summable, then for every point $x$ of the torus, with unit rescaling
$y \in (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$, the series
$\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} (2\pi)^{-1} a_k \, e^{2\pi i (k_0 y_0 + k_1 y_1)}$ converges
unconditionally to $u(x)$.

articles.title: Frequency weights are nonnegative
articles.statement:
For every frequency $k = (k_0, k_1) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$,
the frequency weight $k_0^2 + k_1^2$ is nonnegative.

articles.title: Gradient energy of the lowest-shell witness
articles.statement:
The gradient energy of the lowest-shell
witness equals $1$.

articles.title: $H^2$ functions have a summable gradient energy series
articles.statement:
If $u$ is a continuous real
function on the torus of period $2\pi$ that lies in $H^2$, with Fourier coefficients $a_k$, then
the family $\left((k_0^2 + k_1^2) \, |a_k|^2\right)_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2}$ is summable.

articles.title: Laplacian energy of the lowest-shell witness
articles.statement:
The Laplacian energy of the lowest-shell
witness equals $1$.

articles.title: $H^2$ functions have a summable Laplacian energy series
articles.statement:
If $u$ is a continuous real
function on the torus of period $2\pi$ that lies in $H^2$, with Fourier coefficients $a_k$, then
the family $\left((k_0^2 + k_1^2)^2 \, |a_k|^2\right)_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2}$ is summable.

articles.title: The lowest-shell unit polynomial is real-valued
articles.statement:
For every point $y$ of the unit torus
$(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$, the lowest-shell unit polynomial $P$ satisfies
$\operatorname{Im} P(y) = 0$.

Its Fourier modes come in opposite pairs $\pm k$ with equal coefficients.

articles.title: Lowest-shell unit polynomial
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ let
$e_n(y) = e^{2\pi i\, n \cdot y}$ be the Fourier monomial on the unit torus
$(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$. The lowest-shell unit polynomial is the continuous function
$P : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ given by
$P = (4\pi)^{-1}\bigl(e_{(1,0)} + e_{(-1,0)} + e_{(0,1)} + e_{(0,-1)}\bigr)$, the normalized sum
of the Fourier monomials of the four nonzero frequencies of smallest length.

articles.title: The lowest-shell witness is admissible at $\delta = 1$
articles.statement:
The lowest-shell witness $u$
satisfies the conditional constraints with $\delta = 1$: it is a zero-mean $H^2$ function on the
torus, its gradient energy is $1$, and its Laplacian energy is $1$.

articles.title: Value of the lowest-shell witness at the origin
articles.statement:
The lowest-shell witness $u$ takes the
value $u(0) = 1/\pi$ at the origin of the torus.

articles.title: The lowest-shell witness is in $H^2$
articles.statement:
The lowest-shell witness $u$ belongs to the spectral
Sobolev space $H^2$: if $a_k(u)$ denotes its Fourier coefficients, the series
$\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} (1 + |k|^2)^2 |a_k(u)|^2$ converges.

articles.title: The lowest-shell witness is a zero-mean $H^2$ function
articles.statement:
The lowest-shell witness $u$
belongs to the spectral Sobolev space $H^2$ and has mean $0$.

articles.title: Lowest-shell witness
articles.statement:
The lowest-shell witness is the continuous real function $u$ on the
torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ given by
$u(x_1, x_2) = \frac{1}{4\pi}(e^{i x_1} + e^{-i x_1} + e^{i x_2} + e^{-i x_2})
= \frac{\cos x_1 + \cos x_2}{2\pi}$,
the normalized sum of the four lowest nonzero Fourier modes.

articles.title: Lowest frequency shell
articles.statement:
The lowest shell is the set $\{e_1, -e_1, e_2, -e_2\}$ of
frequencies in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, where $e_1 = (1, 0)$ and $e_2 = (0, 1)$; these are the four nonzero
frequencies of smallest length.

articles.title: Additivity of Fourier coefficients on the 2-torus
articles.statement:
For continuous functions
$f, g : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ and every frequency $n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the
$n$-th Fourier coefficient $\hat h(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i\, n \cdot x} h(x)\,dx$ (normalized Haar
measure) satisfies $\widehat{f + g}(n) = \hat f(n) + \hat g(n)$.

articles.title: Integrability of Fourier integrands on the 2-torus
articles.statement:
For every continuous function
$f : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ and every frequency $n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the
function $x \mapsto e^{-2\pi i\, n \cdot x} f(x)$ is integrable with respect to normalized Haar
measure.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of a Fourier monomial on the 2-torus
articles.statement:
For frequencies
$m, n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the $n$-th Fourier coefficient, taken with respect to normalized Haar
measure on $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$, of the monomial $e_m(x) = e^{2\pi i\, m \cdot x}$ is $1$ if
$n = m$ and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Homogeneity of Fourier coefficients on the 2-torus
articles.statement:
For every $c \in \mathbb{C}$, every
continuous function $f : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ and every frequency
$n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the $n$-th Fourier coefficient (normalized Haar measure) satisfies
$\widehat{c f}(n) = c\, \hat f(n)$.

articles.title: The mean is the real part of the zeroth Fourier coefficient
articles.statement:
For every continuous
function $u : \mathbb{T} \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T} = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$,
the mean of $u$ equals the real part of the zeroth Fourier coefficient
$\int_{(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2} \tilde u(y)\,dy$, taken with respect to normalized Haar measure,
of the unit representative $\tilde u$ of $u$ (the function $u$, viewed as complex-valued and
transported to the unit-period torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$).

articles.title: The lowest-shell witness has mean zero
articles.statement:
The lowest-shell witness, the function
$w(x_1, x_2) = (\cos x_1 + \cos x_2)/(2\pi)$ on the torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, has
mean $0$.

articles.title: Upper bounds for the sharp remainder
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{T} = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$. For
real $\delta$, let $\theta(\delta)$ be the supremum in the extended reals of $u(0)^2$ over all
continuous functions $u : \mathbb{T} \to \mathbb{R}$ that are zero-mean $H^2$ functions with
gradient energy $1$ and Laplacian energy $\delta$, and let
$R(\delta) = 4\pi\,\theta(\delta) - \log\delta - \log(1 + \log\delta)$, computed in the extended
reals. For every extended real number $b$, the sharp remainder value
$\sup_{\delta \ge 1} R(\delta)$, a supremum in the extended reals, is at most $b$ if and only if
$R(\delta) \le b$ for every real $\delta \ge 1$.

articles.title: Upper bounds for the conditional supremum
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{T} = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$.
For every real $\delta$, let $\theta(\delta)$, the conditional supremum, be the supremum in the
extended reals of $u(0)^2$ over all continuous functions $u : \mathbb{T} \to \mathbb{R}$ that are
conditionally admissible at $\delta$, that is, zero-mean $H^2$ functions with gradient energy $1$
and Laplacian energy $\delta$. Then for every extended real number $b$, $\theta(\delta) \le b$ if
and only if $u(0)^2 \le b$ for every such $u$.

articles.title: Unit representative of the lowest-shell witness
articles.statement:
The unit representative of the
lowest-shell witness is the lowest-shell polynomial
$(4\pi)^{-1}\bigl(e_{(1,0)} + e_{(-1,0)} + e_{(0,1)} + e_{(0,-1)}\bigr)$ on the unit torus
$(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$, where $e_n(y) = e^{2\pi i\, n \cdot y}$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}^2$.

articles.title: The unit rescaling fixes the origin
articles.statement:
The coordinate rescaling from the torus
$(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ to the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$ maps $0$ to $0$.

articles.title: Conditionally admissible functions
articles.statement:
Let $\delta$ be a real number. A continuous
function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is admissible at level $\delta$
when it is a zero-mean $H^2$ function, its gradient energy equals $1$, and its Laplacian
energy equals $\delta$.

articles.title: Squared values at the origin of admissible functions
articles.statement:
For a real number $\delta$,
this is the set of extended real numbers $u(0)^2$, where $u$ ranges over the continuous
functions $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ that are conditionally admissible
at level $\delta$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients on the torus
articles.statement:
Let $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$
be continuous and let $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ be a frequency. The Fourier coefficient of $u$ at
$k$ is $a_k = 2\pi c_k$, where $c_k = \int_{[0,1]^2} u(2\pi y)\, e^{-2\pi i\, k \cdot y}\, dy$
is the Fourier coefficient of the rescaled function $y \mapsto u(2\pi y)$ on the unit torus
with respect to normalized Haar measure. Equivalently,
$a_k = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_{[0,2\pi]^2} u(x)\, e^{-i\, k \cdot x}\, dx$.

articles.title: Frequency ratio
articles.statement:
For a continuous function
$u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$, the frequency ratio is the Laplacian energy
of $u$ divided by the gradient energy of $u$.

Applications assume positive gradient energy; when the gradient energy is $0$, the quotient is
taken to be $0$.

articles.title: Squared frequency
articles.statement:
For a frequency $k = (k_1, k_2) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the frequency
weight is $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$, the squared frequency of the mode $e^{i k \cdot x}$ on the
torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$.

articles.title: Integer frequencies
articles.statement:
The frequencies are the elements of the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$,
that is, the pairs $k = (k_1, k_2)$ of integers; they index the Fourier modes of the torus
$(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$.

articles.title: Gradient energy
articles.statement:
For a continuous function
$u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ with Fourier coefficients $a_k$, the gradient
energy is $\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} |k|^2 \, |a_k|^2$, where $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$; the sum is
taken to be $0$ when the series diverges.

By Parseval's identity, for smooth $u$ this equals $\int_{[0,2\pi]^2} |\nabla u(x)|^2 \, dx$.

articles.title: Functions in $H^2$
articles.statement:
A continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$
with Fourier coefficients $a_k$ is in $H^2$ when the series
$\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} (1 + |k|^2)^2 \, |a_k|^2$ converges, where $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$.

This is the full spectral $H^2$ condition, not a restriction to trigonometric polynomials.

articles.title: Zero-mean $H^2$ functions
articles.statement:
A continuous function
$u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is a zero-mean $H^2$ function when it is in
$H^2$ and its mean is $0$.

articles.title: Laplacian energy
articles.statement:
For a continuous function
$u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ with Fourier coefficients $a_k$, the Laplacian
energy is $\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} |k|^4 \, |a_k|^2$, where $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$; the sum is
taken to be $0$ when the series diverges.

By Parseval's identity, for smooth $u$ this equals $\int_{[0,2\pi]^2} |\Delta u(x)|^2 \, dx$.

articles.title: Mean of a function on the torus
articles.statement:
For a continuous function $u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$
on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, its mean is
$\int_{(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2} u(2\pi y)\, d\mu(y)$, where $\mu$ is the normalized Haar measure
on the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$ and $y \mapsto 2\pi y$ is the inverse of the rescaling
to unit period.

Since $\mu$ is a probability measure, this is the average
$(2\pi)^{-2} \int_{[0, 2\pi]^2} u(x)\, dx$; the Lebesgue integral of $u$ over a period cell is
$(2\pi)^2$ times the mean.

articles.title: Logarithmic remainder
articles.statement:
For real $\delta$, the remainder is the extended real number
$R(\delta) = 4\pi\,\theta(\delta) - \log \delta - \log(1 + \log \delta)$, where $\theta(\delta)$
is the conditional supremum of $u(0)^2$ over the functions conditionally admissible at $\delta$.

Here $\log$ is the real logarithm with the conventions $\log 0 = 0$ and $\log x = \log |x|$ for
$x < 0$, so $R(\delta)$ is defined for every real $\delta$.

articles.title: Sharp logarithmic remainder
articles.statement:
The sharp remainder is the supremum, in the extended reals
$[-\infty, \infty]$, of the remainders
$R(\delta) = 4\pi\,\theta(\delta) - \log \delta - \log(1 + \log \delta)$ over all real
$\delta \ge 1$, where $\theta(\delta)$ is the conditional supremum of $u(0)^2$ over the functions
conditionally admissible at $\delta$.

The definition does not assume that the supremum is finite or attained.

articles.title: Set of remainder values
articles.statement:
The set of extended real numbers $R(\delta)$ for all real
$\delta \ge 1$, where $R(\delta) = 4\pi\,\theta(\delta) - \log \delta - \log(1 + \log \delta)$
is the logarithmic remainder and $\theta(\delta)$ is the conditional supremum of $u(0)^2$ over
the functions conditionally admissible at $\delta$.

Every $\delta \ge 1$ is included, not only sufficiently large ratios.

articles.title: Conditional supremum of the squared value at the origin
articles.statement:
For real $\delta$,
$\theta(\delta)$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$, of the
conditional point values at $\delta$: the numbers $u(0)^2$ over all continuous
$u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$
that are conditionally admissible at $\delta$, that is, of mean zero and in $H^2$ with gradient
energy $1$ and Laplace energy $\delta$.

The supremum may be $+\infty$, and it is $-\infty$ when no function is admissible.

articles.title: The torus of period $2\pi$
articles.statement:
The two-dimensional torus
$\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, the product of two copies of the circle
$\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Uniform logarithmic remainder bound
articles.statement:
For a real constant $L$, the bound with constant $L$
holds when, for every continuous $u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus
$\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ that has mean zero and lies in $H^2$, has positive
gradient energy $E(u)$, and, writing $\Delta(u)$ for its Laplace energy, has frequency ratio
$\Lambda(u) = \Delta(u)/E(u) \ge 1$, every point $x$ of the torus satisfies
$u(x)^2 \le \frac{E(u)}{4\pi}\bigl(\log \Lambda(u) + \log(1 + \log \Lambda(u)) + L\bigr)$.

articles.title: Normalized Haar measure on the unit torus
articles.statement:
The measure on the unit torus
$(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$ that is the product of two copies of the Haar probability measure on the
circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: A function on the torus as a function on the unit torus
articles.statement:
For a continuous function
$u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, its
unit representative is the continuous function $\tilde u : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$
given by $\tilde u(y) = u(2\pi y)$, the composition of $u$ with the inverse of the rescaling to
unit period, with its real values regarded as complex numbers.

articles.title: Rescaling the torus to unit period
articles.statement:
The homeomorphism from the torus
$\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ onto the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$
that sends $(x_1, x_2)$ to $(x_1/(2\pi), x_2/(2\pi))$.

articles.title: Double-log bound with coefficient $a$ and constant $L$
articles.statement:
For real numbers $a$ and $L$, the
double-log bound holds when every continuous function $u : \mathbb{T} \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus
$\mathbb{T} = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ that is a zero-mean $H^2$ function, has gradient energy
$E(u) > 0$ and has frequency ratio $\delta(u) \ge 1$ (the Laplacian energy divided by $E(u)$)
satisfies, at every point $x \in \mathbb{T}$,

$$u(x)^2 \le \frac{E(u)}{4\pi}\bigl(\log\delta(u) + a\log\bigl(1 + \log\delta(u)\bigr) + L\bigr).$$

The inner logarithm is taken of $1 + \log\delta(u)$, which is at least $1$ because
$\delta(u) \ge 1$.

articles.title: One-log bound with coefficient $c$ and constant $K$
articles.statement:
For real numbers $c$ and $K$, the
one-log bound holds when every continuous function $u : \mathbb{T} \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus
$\mathbb{T} = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ that is a zero-mean $H^2$ function, has gradient energy
$E(u) > 0$ and has frequency ratio $\delta(u) \ge 1$ (the Laplacian energy divided by $E(u)$)
satisfies, at every point $x \in \mathbb{T}$,

$$u(x)^2 \le c\,E(u)\bigl(\log\delta(u) + K\bigr).$$

articles.title: Optimal one-log coefficient
articles.statement:
The infimum, taken in the extended reals, of all real
numbers $c$ for which there is a real constant $K$ such that the one-log bound with
coefficient $c$ and constant $K$ holds. It is $+\infty$ when no such $c$ exists.

articles.title: Dirichlet–Jordan theorem on pointwise convergence of Fourier series
articles.statement:
Let
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be $2\pi$-periodic and of bounded variation on $[-\pi, \pi]$,
and for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ let $c_n = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} f(t) e^{-int}\,dt$ be its
Fourier coefficients. Then at every $x \in \mathbb{R}$ the one-sided limits
$f(x^+) = \lim_{y \to x,\, y > x} f(y)$ and $f(x^-) = \lim_{y \to x,\, y < x} f(y)$ exist, and
the symmetric partial sums of the Fourier series converge to their average:

$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \sum_{n=-N}^{N} c_n e^{inx} = \frac{f(x^+) + f(x^-)}{2}.$$

By periodicity, the coefficients $c_n$ equal the corresponding integrals over $[-\pi, \pi]$.

This is the bounded-variation (Dirichlet–Jordan) form. It is distinct from the version of
Dirichlet's theorem that assumes $f$ continuously differentiable and concludes convergence to
$f(x)$; here $f$ may be discontinuous and the limit is the average of the one-sided limits.

## Sources

- Y. Katznelson, *An Introduction to Harmonic Analysis*, 3rd ed., Ch. I, §5 (functions of bounded variation; Dirichlet–Jordan test).
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirichlet%27s_theorem_on_Fourier_series

articles.title: Dirichlet's theorem on pointwise convergence of Fourier series
articles.statement:
Let
$f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be $2\pi$-periodic and continuously differentiable, and for
$n \in \mathbb{Z}$ let $\hat f_n = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} e^{-int} f(t)\,dt$ be the $n$-th
Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $[0, 2\pi]$. Then for every $x \in \mathbb{R}$ the symmetric Fourier
partial sums $S_N(f)(x) = \sum_{n=-N}^{N} \hat f_n e^{inx}$ converge to $f(x)$ as $N \to \infty$.

## Sources

- P. G. L. Dirichlet (1829) and L. Fejér (1900). Listed as §46 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `fourier_dirichlet_fejer` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Fejér's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous and
$2\pi$-periodic, and write $S_k(f)$ for the $k$-th symmetric Fourier partial sum of $f$. Then the
Cesàro means $\sigma_N(f) = (S_0(f) + S_1(f) + \dots + S_N(f)) / (N + 1)$ converge to $f$
uniformly on $\mathbb{R}$ as $N \to \infty$.

## Sources

- P. G. L. Dirichlet (1829) and L. Fejér (1900). Listed as §46 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `fourier_dirichlet_fejer` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Cesàro means of Fourier series
articles.statement:
For $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$, a natural number
$N$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the $N$-th Cesàro mean of the Fourier series of $f$ at $x$ is the
average of the first $N + 1$ symmetric Fourier partial sums,
$\sigma_N(f)(x) = \frac{1}{N+1} \sum_{k=0}^{N} S_k(f)(x)$, where
$S_k(f)(x) = \sum_{n=-k}^{k} \hat f_n e^{inx}$ and
$\hat f_n = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} e^{-int} f(t)\,dt$ is the $n$-th Fourier coefficient of
$f$ on the interval $[0, 2\pi]$.

articles.title: Symmetric Fourier partial sums
articles.statement:
For $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$, a natural number
$N$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the $N$-th symmetric Fourier partial sum of $f$ at $x$ is
$S_N(f)(x) = \sum_{n=-N}^{N} \hat f_n e^{inx}$, where
$\hat f_n = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} e^{-int} f(t)\,dt$ is the $n$-th Fourier coefficient of $f$
on the interval $[0, 2\pi]$.

articles.title: Convolutions and linear combinations of translates have the same closure
articles.statement:
Let
$T = \mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ with the measure induced by Lebesgue measure on $[0, 2\pi)$, and
let $L^1(T)$ be the space of real-valued integrable functions on $T$ modulo equality almost
everywhere. Fix a real-valued integrable $f$ on $T$. Let $B_f \subseteq L^1(T)$ be the set of
classes of the finite linear combinations of translates
$x \mapsto \sum_{i=1}^N a_i f(x - \tau_i)$ with $N \in \mathbb{N}$, $a_i \in \mathbb{R}$ and
$\tau_i \in T$, and let $M_f \subseteq L^1(T)$ be the set of classes of the convolutions
$(f * g)(x) = \int_T f(y)\, g(x - y)\,dy$ with $g$ real-valued and integrable on $T$. Then $M_f$
and $B_f$ have the same closure in $L^1(T)$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Commutative Banach algebras and commutative topological algebras), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_12`.

articles.title: The circle $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$
articles.statement:
The circle $T = \mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, the
quotient of the additive group $\mathbb{R}$ by its subgroup $2\pi\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Cesàro–Fourier means
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and $f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$. For
$N \in \mathbb{N}$, the $N$-th Cesàro–Fourier mean of $f$ is the average of its first $N + 1$
partial Fourier sums,

$$\sigma_N f(x) = \frac{1}{N+1} \sum_{k=0}^{N} S_k f(x),$$

where $S_k f$ is the $k$-th partial Fourier sum of $f$.

articles.title: Cesàro–Fourier means are convolutions with the Fejér kernel
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and let
$f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ be integrable with respect to the Haar probability
measure $dt$ on the circle. Then for every $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
$x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, the $N$-th Cesàro–Fourier mean of $f$ satisfies

$$\sigma_N f(x) = \int_{\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}} K_N(t)\, f(x - t)\, dt,$$

where $K_N$ is the $N$-th Fejér kernel.

This is the bridge from the definition of $\sigma_N f$ to the kernel-theoretic analysis
underlying Fejér's theorem.

articles.title: Quantitative Fejér theorem
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$, let $f$ be a continuous complex-valued function
on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, and write $\sigma_N f$ for its $N$-th Cesàro–Fourier
mean. Let $\varepsilon > 0$ and $\delta > 0$ be such that $|f(a) - f(b)| < \varepsilon / 2$ for
all points $a, b$ of the circle at distance less than $\delta$. Then there is
$N_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $|f(x) - \sigma_N f(x)| < \varepsilon$ for every $N \ge N_0$ and
every point $x$ of the circle.

The proof writes $f(x) - \sigma_N f(x) = \int K_N(t)\,(f(x) - f(x - t))\,dt$, where $K_N$ is the
$N$-th Fejér kernel and the integral is against the Haar probability measure, and splits it
into the points $t$ at distance less than $\delta$ from $0$, where $f(x) - f(x - t)$ is small,
and the remaining points, where the Fejér kernel is $O(1/((N+1)\delta^2))$.

articles.title: The sum of Dirichlet kernels is a squared modulus
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$,
let $e_n(x) = e^{2\pi i n x / T}$ be the $n$-th Fourier character on the circle
$\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. For every natural number $N$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$,
put $G = \sum_{k=0}^{N} e_k(x)$. Then the iterated sum of Dirichlet kernels satisfies
$\sum_{k=0}^{N} \sum_{n=-k}^{k} e_n(x) = G\,\overline{G} = |G|^2$.

articles.title: Continuity of the Fejér kernel
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$. For every natural number $N$, the $N$-th
Fejér kernel $K_N$ is a continuous function from the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$ to
$\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: The Fejér kernel as a squared modulus
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and, for $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, let
$e_k(x) = e^{2\pi i k x / T}$ be the $k$-th Fourier character on the circle
$\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. For every natural number $N$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$,
the $N$-th Fejér kernel satisfies $K_N(x) = \frac{1}{N+1} \left|\sum_{k=0}^{N} e_k(x)\right|^2$.

In particular $K_N(x)$ is a nonnegative real number, so $|K_N(x)| = \operatorname{Re} K_N(x)$.

articles.title: Integrability of the Fejér kernel
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$. For every natural number $N$, the $N$-th
Fejér kernel $K_N$ is integrable on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$ with respect to the
normalized Haar measure, the Haar measure of total mass $1$.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the Fejér kernel
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$. For every natural number $N$ and every
$x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, the real part of the $N$-th Fejér kernel at $x$ is nonnegative:
$\operatorname{Re} K_N(x) \ge 0$.

articles.title: Properties of the Fejér kernel
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$, let $N$ be a natural number, let $K_N$ be
the $N$-th Fejér kernel on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, let $\mu$ be the normalized Haar
measure on $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$ (of total mass $1$), and let $e_1(x) = e^{2\pi i x / T}$.
Then $\operatorname{Re} K_N(x) \ge 0$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$;
$K_N(-x) = K_N(x)$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$; the function on $\mathbb{R}$ sending
$t$ to $K_N$ evaluated at the class of $t$ in $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$ is $T$-periodic;
$\int K_N \, d\mu = 1$; and for every $\delta > 0$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$ with
$\delta \le |1 - e_1(x)|$ we have $|K_N(x)| \le \frac{4}{(N+1)\delta^2}$.

articles.title: Symmetry of the Fejér kernel
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$. For every natural number $N$ and every
$x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, the $N$-th Fejér kernel satisfies $K_N(-x) = K_N(x)$.

articles.title: The Fejér kernel
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, let
$e_n(x) = e^{2\pi i n x / T}$ be the $n$-th Fourier character on the circle
$\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. For a natural number $N$, the $N$-th Fejér kernel is the function
$K_N : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ given by the Cesàro mean of the Dirichlet kernels,
$K_N(x) = \frac{1}{N+1} \sum_{k=0}^{N} \sum_{n=-k}^{k} e_n(x)$.

Writing $x$ also for a real representative, when $\sin(\pi x / T) \ne 0$ the kernel has the closed
form $K_N(x) = \frac{1}{N+1} \left(\frac{\sin((N+1)\pi x / T)}{\sin(\pi x / T)}\right)^2$.
This normalization is for the Haar probability measure on $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$; for $T = 2\pi$,
the kernel for integration against Lebesgue measure is $K_N / (2\pi)$.

articles.title: Fejér's theorem: uniform convergence of Cesàro–Fourier means
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and let $f$ be
a continuous complex-valued function on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$ (equivalently, a
continuous $T$-periodic function on $\mathbb{R}$). Then the Cesàro–Fourier means $\sigma_N f$
converge to $f$ uniformly on the circle as $N \to \infty$.

articles.title: Integrability of Fourier characters
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$. For every integer $n$, the Fourier
character $e_n(x) = e^{2\pi i n x / T}$ is integrable on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$ with
respect to the normalized Haar measure, the Haar measure of total mass $1$.

articles.title: Convolution of a function with a Fourier character
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$, let
$f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ be integrable with respect to the Haar probability
measure $dt$ on the circle, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ let $e_n(x) = e^{2\pi i n x / T}$ be the
$n$-th Fourier character, and let $\hat f(n) = \int_{\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}} e_{-n}(t)\, f(t)\, dt$
be the $n$-th Fourier coefficient of $f$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and every
$x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$,

$$\int_{\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}} e_n(t)\, f(x - t)\, dt = \hat f(n)\, e_n(x).$$

Thus the $n$-th term of the partial Fourier sum of $f$ at $x$ is the convolution of $f$ with
the Fourier character $e_n$.

articles.title: Products of Fourier characters
articles.statement:
Let $T$ be a real number and, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, let
$e_n$ be the $n$-th Fourier character on $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, given by
$e_n(x) = e^{2\pi i n x / T}$ (the constant $1$ when $T = 0$). For every integer $n$ and all
$x, t \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, we have $e_{-n}(t)\, e_n(x) = e_n(x - t)$.

articles.title: Integrability of a function twisted by a Fourier character
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and let
$f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ be integrable with respect to the Haar probability
measure on the circle. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$,
the function $t \mapsto e^{2\pi i n t / T} f(x - t)$ is integrable with respect to the same
measure.

This is used to interchange sums and integrals in the convolution computation.

articles.title: Fourier characters at a difference
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ let
$e_n(x) = e^{2\pi i n x / T}$ be the $n$-th Fourier character on $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. Then
for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and all $x, t \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$,
$e_n(x - t) = e_{-n}(t)\, e_n(x)$.

articles.title: The Dirichlet kernel has integral one
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$, let
$e_n(t) = e^{2\pi i n t / T}$ be the $n$-th Fourier character on the circle
$\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, and for $k \in \mathbb{N}$ let $D_k = \sum_{n=-k}^{k} e_n$ be the
$k$-th Dirichlet kernel. With respect to the Haar probability measure on the circle,
$\int D_k = 1$; only the term $n = 0$ contributes, by orthogonality.

articles.title: The Fejér kernel has integral one
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$. The $N$-th Fejér
kernel $K_N$ on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$ satisfies $\int K_N = 1$ with respect to the
Haar probability measure on the circle. This is one of the defining properties of an
approximation to the identity.

articles.title: Integral of a Fourier character
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, let
$e_n(t) = e^{2\pi i n t / T}$ be the $n$-th Fourier character on the circle
$\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. With respect to the Haar probability measure on the circle,
$\int e_n = 1$ if $n = 0$ and $\int e_n = 0$ otherwise. This is the orthogonality of the
Fourier basis.

articles.title: The Fejér kernel has $L^1$ norm one
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$. For every $N \in \mathbb{N}$, the
$N$-th Fejér kernel $K_N$ on $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$ satisfies

$$\int_{\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}} |K_N(t)|\, dt = 1,$$

where $dt$ is the Haar probability measure on the circle.

Since $K_N \ge 0$, this is the normalization $\int K_N = 1$; it is used to control
convolutions with $K_N$ in the proof of Fejér's theorem.

articles.title: Pointwise bound for the Fejér kernel
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$. For every point
$x$ of the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, the $N$-th Fejér kernel satisfies
$|K_N(x)| \le N + 1$.

This follows from the triangle inequality applied to the iterated Dirichlet sum defining
$K_N$, together with $\sum_{k=0}^{N} (2k+1) = (N+1)^2$.

articles.title: Partial Fourier sums
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and $f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$. For
$N \in \mathbb{N}$, the $N$-th partial Fourier sum of $f$ is the function

$$S_N f(x) = \sum_{n=-N}^{N} \hat f(n)\, e_n(x),$$

where $e_n(x) = e^{2\pi i n x / T}$ is the $n$-th Fourier character and
$\hat f(n) = \int_{\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}} e_{-n}(t)\, f(t)\, dt$ is the $n$-th Fourier coefficient,
the integral taken against the Haar probability measure on the circle.

articles.title: Reindexing a sum of Fourier characters, negative range
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$, let
$e_n(t) = e^{2\pi i n t / T}$ be the $n$-th Fourier character on the circle
$\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, and let $N \in \mathbb{N}$. For every point $x$ of the circle,
$\sum_{k=0}^{N} e_{k-(N+1)}(x) = \sum_{n=-(N+1)}^{-1} e_n(x)$.

It is used in the proof that the iterated Dirichlet sum defining the Fejér kernel equals
$\left|\sum_{k=0}^{N} e_k(x)\right|^2$.

articles.title: Reindexing a sum of Fourier characters, positive range
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$, let
$e_n(t) = e^{2\pi i n t / T}$ be the $n$-th Fourier character on the circle
$\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, and let $N \in \mathbb{N}$. For every point $x$ of the circle,
$\sum_{k=0}^{N} e_{(N+1)-k}(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{N+1} e_n(x)$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of a measure on the circle
articles.statement:
For a measure $\mu$ on the circle
$\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ and an integer $k$, the $k$-th Fourier coefficient of
$\mu$ is $\hat\mu_k = \int_{\mathbb{T}} e^{ikx} \, d\mu(x)$.

articles.title: Fourier decay of a circle measure passes to integrable densities
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a finite
Borel measure on $\mathbb{C}$ concentrated on the unit circle $T = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| = 1\}$,
that is, $\mu$-almost every $z$ lies in $T$, and suppose that $\int z^n \, d\mu(z) \to 0$ as
$n \to \infty$ through $\mathbb{N}$. Then for every $\mu$-integrable function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$,

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} \int z^n f(z) \, d\mu(z) = 0.
$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Set functions and measures on spaces with additional structure), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_13`.

articles.title: Wiener's atom-detection formula
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on the circle
$\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, with Fourier coefficients
$\hat\mu_k = \int_{\mathbb{T}} e^{ikx} \, d\mu(x)$. Then
$\frac{1}{N} \sum_{k=1}^{N} \lvert \hat\mu_k \rvert^2 \to \sum_{x \in \mathbb{T}} \mu(\{x\})^2$
as $N \to \infty$.

## Sources

- N. Wiener, The Fourier Integral and Certain of its Applications (1933). Listed as §66 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `wiener_atom_detection` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients of the Mathieu–Fibonacci periodic function
articles.statement:
Let
$\varphi = (1 + \sqrt{5}) / 2$ be the golden ratio. For each natural number $n \ge 1$, the $n$-th
coefficient is the real number
$c_n = (2 / \log \varphi) \, |\Gamma(1 + 2 n \pi i / \log \varphi)|^2$, where $\Gamma$ is the
complex Gamma function.

In the source, these are the coefficients of the cosine series
$H(x) = 1 + \sum_{n \ge 1} c_n \cos(4 n \pi x / \log \varphi)$ of a periodic function $H$.

articles.title: Periodic convolution
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a normed ring that is a normed algebra over
$\mathbb{R}$ (for example $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$), let $T$ be a real number, and let
$f, g : \mathbb{R} \to A$ with $g$ periodic of period $T$, that is, $g(x + T) = g(x)$ for all
real $x$. Then the function $x \mapsto \int_0^T f(t)\, g(x - t)\, dt$ is periodic of period
$T$. The function $f$ need not be periodic or integrable.

articles.title: A Fourier coefficient is bounded by the L¹ norm
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$, let $\mu$ be the Haar
probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$, and let $E$ be a normed space over
$\mathbb{C}$. For every function $f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to E$ and every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$,
the $n$-th Fourier coefficient $\hat f(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i n t / T} f(t)\,d\mu(t)$ satisfies
$\|\hat f(n)\| \le \int \|f(t)\|\,d\mu(t)$.

The bound holds because $|e^{-2\pi i n t / T}| = 1$. No integrability is assumed: as usual for
the Bochner integral, an integral whose integrand is not integrable is $0$, and so is any
$E$-valued integral when $E$ is not complete.

articles.title: Riemann–Lebesgue for continuous functions
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and let $\mu$ be the Haar
probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. For every continuous function
$g : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$, the Fourier coefficients
$\hat g(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i n t / T} g(t)\,d\mu(t)$ tend to $0$ as $|n| \to \infty$, that is,
along the cofinite filter on $\mathbb{Z}$.

The proof uses Parseval's identity in $L^2(\mu)$: the sequence $|\hat g(n)|^2$ is summable, so
it tends to $0$.

articles.title: Riemann–Lebesgue lemma on the circle
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and let $\mu$ be the Haar probability
measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. For every $\mu$-integrable function
$f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$, the Fourier coefficients
$\hat f(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i n t / T} f(t)\,d\mu(t)$ tend to $0$ as $|n| \to \infty$, that is,
along the cofinite filter on $\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Riemann–Lebesgue lemma on an interval
articles.statement:
Let $a < b$ be real numbers and let
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be integrable on $[a, b]$. Then the Fourier coefficients of $f$
on $[a, b]$,

$$\hat f(n) = \frac{1}{b - a} \int_a^b e^{-2\pi i n x / (b - a)} f(x)\,dx,$$

tend to $0$ as $|n| \to \infty$, that is, along the cofinite filter on $\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Fourier coefficients determine a continuous function
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and let $\mu$ be the
Haar probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. For a function
$h : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, let
$\hat h(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i n t / T} h(t)\,d\mu(t)$ be the $n$-th Fourier coefficient of $h$. If
two continuous functions $f, g : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfy
$\hat f(n) = \hat g(n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, then $f = g$.

articles.title: Uniqueness of Fourier coefficients in L²
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and let $\mu$ be the Haar
probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. If an element $F$ of
$L^2(\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}, \mu; \mathbb{C})$ has Fourier coefficients
$\hat F(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i n t / T} F(t)\,d\mu(t)$ equal to $0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$,
then $F = 0$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}, \mu; \mathbb{C})$.

articles.title: Uniqueness of Fourier coefficients for continuous functions
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and let $\mu$
be the Haar probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. If a continuous function
$f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ has Fourier coefficients
$\hat f(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i n t / T} f(t)\,d\mu(t)$ equal to $0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$,
then $f = 0$.

articles.title: Uniqueness of Fourier coefficients on an interval
articles.statement:
Let $a, T \in \mathbb{R}$ with
$T > 0$, and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous with $f(a) = f(a + T)$. If the
Fourier coefficients of $f$ on $[a, a + T]$,

$$\hat f(n) = \frac{1}{T} \int_a^{a+T} e^{-2\pi i n x / T} f(x)\,dx,$$

are $0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, then $f(x) = 0$ for every $x \in [a, a + T]$.

This is a corollary of uniqueness on the circle: the endpoint condition makes $f$ on
$[a, a + T]$ descend to a continuous function on $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Injectivity of the Fourier-coefficient map
articles.statement:
Let $T > 0$ and let $\mu$ be the Haar
probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. The map sending a continuous function
$f : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{C}$ to its sequence of Fourier coefficients
$(\hat f(n))_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$, where $\hat f(n) = \int e^{-2\pi i n t / T} f(t)\,d\mu(t)$, is
injective.

articles.title: Homogeneous Sobolev seminorm (band-limited derivative bound)
articles.statement:
For
$s \in \mathbb{R}$ and a Schwartz function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Fourier transform
$\hat f(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) e^{-2\pi i x\xi}\,dx$, the homogeneous Sobolev seminorm of
order $s$ is

$$\|f\|_{\dot H^s} = \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}} |\xi|^{2s}\, |\hat f(\xi)|^2\,d\xi\right)^{1/2},$$

where the integral is taken to be $0$ when its integrand is not integrable.

articles.title: Bernstein inequality for Schwartz functions with Fourier support of finite measure
articles.statement:
Fix $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For a Schwartz function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ write
$\hat f(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(x) e^{-2\pi i \langle x, \xi \rangle}\,dx$ for its Fourier
transform, and write $|E|$ for the Lebesgue measure of a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$. There
is a constant $C > 0$ such that for every Borel set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ with
$|E| < \infty$, all $p, q \in [1, \infty]$ with $p \le q$ and $p \le 2$, and every Schwartz
function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ whose Fourier transform has closed support
$\overline{\{\xi : \hat f(\xi) \ne 0\}}$ contained in $E$,

$$\|f\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^n)} \le C\, |E|^{1/p - 1/q}\, \|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)},$$

where $1/q = 0$ for $q = \infty$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Distributions, generalized functions, distribution spaces), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_47`.

articles.title: Bernstein inequality for band-limited Schwartz functions
articles.statement:
For a Schwartz function
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ write $\hat f(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) e^{-2\pi i x\xi}\,dx$
for its Fourier transform. There is a constant $C_0 > 0$ such that for every $p \in [1, \infty]$
and every Schwartz function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\hat f(\xi) = 0$ whenever
$|\xi| \ge 1$,

$$\|f'\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R})} \le C_0 \|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R})}.$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_70`.

articles.title: Bernstein-type bound for the derivative of a band-limited Schwartz function
articles.statement:
Let
$s \in (\tfrac12, 1]$. For a Schwartz function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ write
$\hat f(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) e^{-2\pi i x\xi}\,dx$ for its Fourier transform and
$\|f\|_{\dot H^s} = \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}} |\xi|^{2s} |\hat f(\xi)|^2\,d\xi\right)^{1/2}$ for
its homogeneous Sobolev seminorm. There is a constant $C_1 > 0$ such that for every real
$A \ge 0$ and every Schwartz function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\hat f(\xi) = 0$
whenever $|\xi| > A$,

$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |f'(x)| \le C_1 A^{3/2 - s}\, \|f\|_{\dot H^s}.$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_00`.

articles.title: Bañuelos–Janakiraman upper bound for the Beurling–Ahlfors transform
articles.statement:
For a function
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ let $Bf(z)$ be the limit as $\varepsilon \to 0^+$ of
$-\frac{1}{\pi} \int_{|w - z| > \varepsilon} \frac{f(w)}{(z - w)^2} \, dA(w)$, where $dA$ is
Lebesgue area measure (a junk value where the limit does not exist), and for real $p > 1$ let
$p^* = \max(p, p/(p - 1))$. For every real $p > 1$ and every almost everywhere strongly measurable
$f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, $\|Bf\|_{L^p} \le 1.575\,(p^* - 1)\,\|f\|_{L^p}$, with the
$L^p$ norms taken in $[0, \infty]$.
